title: 'A lot happier now': US Olympic figure skater Alysa Liu talks after winning gold
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: When you knew you won that gold medal, what was that feeling that hit you? And don't worry, we have a bleep button. Um, I mean, it didn't really change how I felt about anything. Uh, the moment I finished my program I was at, like, on such a high. Um, literally nothing could bring me higher or lower. When you stepped away from figure skating, what did maybe the silence and the absence of the crowds teach you that the roaring arenas never could? Mmm, I mean it showed me a different side, that's for sure. And I got to experience something new, and that's always valuable. Watching you out there, I don't know what was stronger, your jumps or your joy. It's just emanating from you. Who is Alysa Liu now compared to the 13-year-old kid who burst onto the scene? Ooh, I mean, I would say I know myself a lot better. But you know, I'd hope I do at 20. Um, but yeah, I don't know. I'm a lot happier now. As athletes, through all the highs and the lows, the ups and the downs, parents, family are there every step of the way. How much has your family meant to you in this journey? Family is everything to me, so are my friends. Um, they keep me grounded and, uh, yeah, honestly like, they're the reason why I, I feel like I, am able to do so much. When young girls look at you now, what, what do you hope they see? Mmm, I hope they see that they have limitless potential. Limitless? Yeah. Yeah, this is unlimited. Mm-hmm. What's next for the hair? Um, I mean, it's, I'll let it grow out and then end of December, I'll add another one. So this will end up down here, and I'll just add a new one. And what would this last ring say about this past year? I don't know. I don't know. Another year. Just another year. Yeah, just another year. Easy-breezy. You come out here with your striped hair, your unique piercings. What do you hope you being you says to anyone out there kind of struggled to find their place? Oh my god. I hope they know that it's good to break down, I guess, barriers and, um, do, do risky things and, you know, go against some people sometimes. Yeah, it's liberating. Can you teach me a pose, a position? I got to, I got to show these to my daughters. What do we got for me? Okay, we'll do my ending pose. So, so, you point your toe. Point my toe. Hand on your hip. Hand on my hip. And then point up. Point up. And that's it. Ooh! I got that gold medal glow. Congratulations, amazing. Thank you.

title: LOCUSTS ARE COMING!! || SHORT MOVIE CLIPS
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Faced with the swarming army of eager locusts, the two tough guys were so frightened that they didn't dare stay any longer and took off running. But how could these prehistoric locusts let them get away? They gave chase fiercely. The locusts craved a big feast. A huge, bloody mouth swallowed them whole. It was an ancient man-eating plant. Seeing the locusts, the plant became extremely excited, swinging its massive jaws and devouring them one by one, quickly finishing off all the pursuing locusts. Only then did the two men narrowly escape disaster. But before they could get far, a sudden cliff appeared in front of them. The gap was simply too wide for them to jump across. Meanwhile, the swarm of locusts had broken through the blockade and was once again chasing after them frantically. Seeing they were about to be devoured, the man above became desperate. He stared at the stone statue behind them, then, risking all, he rammed it with his head. In the next second, the statue shook violently then toppled to bridge the gap, forming an escape route. The two didn't dare waste a moment and dashed across to save their lives. Little did they know, an even more terrifying presence awaited them ahead. Xiao Hong Shu, Little Red Book.

title: diary cinematic video | how journaling can change your life
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Today at 9:15 a.m. I wrote something in my diary that I have never admitted to anyone, not even my bird, not even to myself. Dear diary, here are the things I never say out loud. I miss people, I know I shouldn't. I tell everyone I'm okay, but some nights, I'm not. Day by day, nothing feels different for me, but when I look back, everything has changed. I have mastered the art of saying I'm fine because explaining the truth felt heavier than hiding it. When the room gets quiet, my thoughts don't. Old conversations replay like music in my head. Memories, they hit harder. It gets loud inside my head with words I wish I had said. And some endings, well, they don't come with explanations. They say, your problems begin to lose their weight, the moment you write them down. So, I did. I wrote the messy parts, the overthinking, how exactly I felt at those particular moments, things that keep me awake. Well, the pain didn't disappear, of course, but it didn't feel so heavy anymore. And, I realized something. Honesty with yourself changes everything because in the end, you are the creator of your life. So tell me, if no one was watching, how would you live tomorrow?

She talks about the weight of unsaid words, the persistence of memories, and how writing her thoughts down has helped ease her emotional burden. Her speech is slow and deliberate, matching the contemplative mood of the music. She concludes with a powerful realization about self-honesty and leaves the listener with a thought-provoking question about how they would live if no one was watching.

It is not hyperbole to say that today, I am the most famous and talked about person in the country and one of the most recognizable people in the world. President Trump seems to be enamored of me, even though I am taking the spotlight away from him." Critics say Fauci became obsessed with the fame he received during the pandemic, instead of focusing on his role as the country grappled with COVID. title: Journal with Me: Master Your Mindset (in 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There is this poem that says our soul is the sail of our life and how our soul is set determines how our life goes. Have you believed the lie that the winds matter more than your sail? The winds around us are ferocious forces, that is for sure. But they are not what guides us. Darling, the winds change with seasons, with tempests, and those who forget their sail are surely at the wind's mercy, tossed and directionless. Raise your sail, dear one. With it, you will use the winds to set the direction, the course of your life. Happiness, bliss, shalom, peace exists in one place—inside of you—and in one time—right now. This ancient wisdom is your sail. You are the gatekeeper, the manager of your sacred space. Therefore, commune daily with her. Ask, "How is she?" For as she goes, so does the rest of life. And when we get tempted to wrench that soul into conforming, into behaving, into lockstep with every other soul, we must remember that she is a wild spirit, that her dreams are not meant for others' validation, that she sways the oaks and sends cracks through Earth's tectonic plates when she realizes the power and beauty of her sail. These two things can be true at the same time: treacherous winds are blowing and your soul is set on peace, hope, love, and joy.

She encourages self-care, inner peace, and embracing the soul's wild, non-conforming nature. The entire recording is clean and well-produced, aiming to inspire tranquility and introspection.

title: First Manifestation of 2026 | Night Meditation to Change Your Money Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: अगर आपने मेरा पिछला वीडियो देखा था तो आप जानते हो कि डिसिप्लिन कैसे बिल्ड होती है। हैबिट्स कैसे चेंज होती हैं और कैसे हम 2026 में 99% लोगों से आगे जा सकते हैं। लेकिन आज मैं आपको एक अनकंफर्टेबल सच बताने वाला हूं। बहुत सारे लोग डिसिप्लिन हो जाते हैं, मेहनत करते हैं, रूटीन फॉलो करते हैं, फिर भी पैसा उनके पास रुकता नहीं। क्योंकि प्रॉब्लम एफर्ट की नहीं होती, प्रॉब्लम होती है उस कहानी की जो आप हर रात सोने से पहले अपने दिमाग को सुना रहे होते हो। जब आप बेड पर लेटते हो, लाइट्स बंद होती हैं, फोन साइड में होता है, उस वक्त आपका कॉन्शियस माइंड धीरे-धीरे शटडाउन होता है और सबकॉन्शियस फुल्ली अवेक होता है। और वही सबकॉन्शियस डिसाइड करता है कि आप कितना पैसा डिज़र्व करते हो, कितनी शांति डिज़र्व करते हो और आपका फ्यूचर किस लेवल का होगा। अगर आप बचपन से सुनते आए हो कि पैसा कमाना मुश्किल है, पैसा गंदा होता है, या मेरे जैसे लोग ज्यादा पैसा नहीं कमाते, तो चाहे आप दिन में कितनी भी मेहनत कर लो, रात को वही बिलीफ सिस्टम एक्टिव हो जाता है। इसलिए आज की रात मोटिवेशन की नहीं है, आज की रात रीसेट की है। मैं चाहता हूं कि आप इस वीडियो को सोते वक्त सुनो। कोई एफर्ट नहीं, कोई विजुअलाइजेशन प्रेशर नहीं, बस सुनते रहो। अब अपनी आंखें बंद करो, एक गहरी सांस लो और धीरे-धीरे छोड़ दो। इमेजिन करो जैसे आप पूरे यूनिवर्स के बीच में हो, तारों के नीचे, बिल्कुल सेफ। और मैं धीरे-धीरे आपके सबकॉन्शियस से बात करूंगा। आज रात हम पुरानी मनी स्टोरी को रिलीज कर रहे हैं। अपने मन में बोलो, बिना आवाज के भी चलेगा। जो भी बिलीव्स मैंने पैसा लेकर कैरी किए, जो डर, गिल्ट या गिल्ट के साथ आए, मैं उन्हें आज... रिलीज करता हूं। फील करो जैसे कोई हैवी वेट चेस्ट से निकल रहा हो। अब मैं आपके सबकॉन्शियस को एक नई आइडेंटिटी दे रहा हूं। रिपीट मत करो, बस सुनो। पैसा मेरे लिए सेफ है, पैसा मेरे लिए नेचुरल है, मैं पैसा संभाल सकता हूं, मैं पैसा ग्रो कर सकता हूं, मैं पैसा डिज़र्व करता हूं। अगर बीच-बीच में नींद आए, परफेक्ट, क्योंकि सबकॉन्शियस को वही चाहिए। आज रात आप एफर्ट से नहीं, वर्दिनेस से अट्रैक्ट कर रहे हो। इमेजिन करो कि यूनिवर्स आपको पुश नहीं कर रहा बल्कि सपोर्ट कर रहा है। जैसे अपॉर्चुनिटीज नेचुरली आ रही हैं, लोग मदद कर रहे हैं, आइडियाज फ्लो हो रहे हैं, आपको प्रूव नहीं करना पड़ रहा, बस रिसीव करना पड़ रहा है। और अब तीन शब्द मैं आपके सबकॉन्शियस में प्लांट कर रहा हूं- मैं रेडी हूं। रेडी फॉर मनी, रेडी फॉर पीस, रेडी फॉर ग्रोथ। कल सुबह जब आप उठोगे, कुछ ड्रामेटिक नहीं होगा, लेकिन एक चीज बदलेगी, आपका अंदर का रिलेशनशिप पैसों के साथ और वही छोटा सा शिफ्ट 2026 को अलग बना देगा। याद रखना, डिसिप्लिन आपको एक्शन देता है, लेकिन आइडेंटिटी आपको रिजल्ट देती है। और आज रात आपने अपनी आइडेंटिटी अपग्रेड की है। बस इस ऑडियो को सुनते हुए सो जाओ, यूनिवर्स का काम शुरू हो चुका है। अगर यह वीडियो आपके दिल को थोड़ा सा भी शांत करे, या आपको लगे कि यह सिर्फ सुनना नहीं बल्कि महसूस करना था, तो प्लीज इस वीडियो को लाइक करो, चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करो और इसे उन लोगों के साथ शेयर करो जो मेहनत तो कर रहे हैं, लेकिन अंदर से थक चुके हैं। कमेंट में My life is short

And started living right here
My life is short
I won't spend it keeping score

My life is short

title: I don’t chase I attract
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I don't chase, I attract. Everything finds its way back. I don't stress, I don't fight. My whole life is flowing right. I breathe in peace, I let go fear. What is mine is already here. I don't want, I don't wait. The universe knows my fate. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I don't need to check the 3D. I trust myself, I trust the unseen. Everything comes at the perfect time. I want it and it's already mine. I don't rush time, I let it flow. What is for me already knows. I don't chase dreams, I don't pretend. Everything meets me in the end. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I slowed my breath, I changed the tone. Started acting like it's already done. Now I choose what I assume. Life says yes to every move. If it's mine, it won't pass me by. It finds its way, I receive the sign. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I always get what I want, I always get what I need. Everything happens in my favor, everything flows easily. I don't chase, I attract. What I want wants me more, and it's already knocking on my door.

on our own.

so we were liars,
so we're no heroes,
we're still survivors.

and I'll be right here
by your side.

and we can't go back.
But now we're seeing all the beauty
in the broken glass.

darkness and harmony.

the colors stuck inside our head?
Get up and let the jagged edges
meet the light instead.
Show me what's underneath.
I'll find your harmony.
Fearless and on the fire.

G-Crew.

title: Cartel (Official Music Video) Cheema Y | Gur Sidhu
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: ਨਿੱਕੀ ਉਮਰੋਂ ਹੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕੀਤੀ ਫੀਮ ਚੈੱਕ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਦੇ ਗਿਆ ਸਟਾਂਗ ਜੱਟ ਨੂੰ। ਪੂਜਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਮੈਂ ਬੈੱਡ ਤੇ ਵਿਛਾ ਕੇ ਰਫਲਾਂ, ਯਾਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਲੱਗੀ ਐ ਬਿਲੋ ਘੜੀ ਲੱਤ ਨੂੰ। ਸਾਡੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਆਂ ਨਾਰਾਂ 'ਚ ਫਸੀ ਹੋਈ ਐ ਸ਼ਰਲੀ, ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਕੀ ਐ ਕਰੀ ਜਾਣ ਤਰਲੇ। ਐਵੇਂ ਲਿੰਕ ਕੱਢ-ਕੱਢ ਕੇ ਨਾ ਫੋਨ ਤੂੰ ਕਰਾ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਛੱਡਣਾ ਤੇ ਬਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਛੱਡਣਾ। ਫਿਰ ਲੱਭਦੇ ਰਵੋਂਗੇ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਭਣਾ, ਕਸ਼ਮੀਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਾਦੀਆਂ 'ਚ ਬੰਦਾ ਦੱਬਣਾ। ਇੱਕ ਭਰੀ ਐ ਅਲਮਾਰੀ ਬਿਲੋ ਮੈਗਜ਼ੀਨਾਂ ਨਾਲ, ਦੂਜਾ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਮੇਰੀ ਕਿਸਨ 47 ਨਾ ਪੱਤੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ। ਸਾਨੂੰ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਬਲੱਡ ਤੱਕ ਰਿਪ ਜਾਣਦੇ, ਅਸੀਂ ਬੁੱਕਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਰਫਲਾਂ ਦਾ ਲਿਖ ਜਾਣਦੇ। ਅਸੀਂ ਰਹੀ ਦਾ ਤਿਆਰ ਸਭ ਛੱਡਣ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਲੋ, ਪਰ ਸਾਂਭ ਕੇ ਰੱਖੀ ਦੇ ਸਿੱਕੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਰਾਜ ਦੇ। ਪਿੰਡ ਜਾਵਾਂ ਤੇ ਭੰਗੀਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਲਾਵਾਂ ਰਗੜੇ ਤੇ ਐੱਲ. ਏ. ਲੋ ਰਾਈਡਰ ਕਲੱਬ ਯਾਰ ਦਾ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਕੇ ਚੜ੍ਹਾਈ ਯਾਰ ਦੀ ਤੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਖਰਚਾ ਐ ਵੱਧ ਯਾਰ ਦਾ। ਅਸੀਂ ਬੋਲੀ ਦਾ ਨੀ ਬੱਸ ਗੈਂਗ ਸਾਈਨ ਦੇਈ ਦੇ, ਤਾਂਹੀਓਂ ਮਾਫ਼ੀਏ ਦੀ ਗੱਡੀ ਨਹੀਂਓਂ ਰਾਹ ਡੱਕਦੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ। ਕੁੜੇ ਕਿਹੜੀਆਂ ਭੁਲੇਖਿਆਂ 'ਚ ਕਰੀ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਨੇ, ਐਵੇਂ ਵੈਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਦਲ ਮਖੌਲ ਦਊਂਗਾ। ਇੱਕ ਚਮਚਾ ਸਟੀਲ ਪਾਈਪ ਤਿੰਨ ਸਪਰਿੰਗ ਦੇਦੋ, ਘਰੇ ਈ ਬਣਾ ਪਿਸਤੌਲ ਦਊਂਗਾ। ਤੁਸੀਂ ਬਾਰਡਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਕੁਝ ਵੀ ਟਪਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ, ਅਸੀਂ ਪੁਲਾਂ ਥੱਲੋਂ ਕੁਝ ਵੀ ਲੰਘਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਾਂ। ਅਸੀਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਬਣਾ ਕੇ ਜਾਲੀ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ ਨੀ, ਅਸੀਂ ਇੱਧਰ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਧਰ ਨੂੰ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਾਂ। ਕੁੜੇ ਕਿੰਨੀ ਵਾਰੀ ਹੋਈ ਸਿਕਿਓਰਿਟੀ ਕੁੜੇ, ਕੁੜੇ ਕਿੰਨੀ ਵਾਰੀ ਚੌਂਕੀ ਮੇਰਾ ਨਾਂ ਰੱਟਦੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ। ਅੱਧੀ ਜੇਲਾਂ 'ਚ ਬੈਠੀ ਐ ਕਾਰਟੇਲ ਜੱਟ ਦੀ, ਅੱਧੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੋਹਣੀਏ ਫਰਾਰੀ ਕੱਢਦੀ।

transcription: सवेरे समय का शो देखा, उसमें उसने कहा कि... स्टैंड-अप कॉमेडियन और यूट्यूबर समय रैना लगातार चर्चा में बने हुए हैं। वजह है उनका नया स्टैंड-अप स्पेशल 'स्टिल अलाइव'। इस नए यूट्यूब वीडियो में समय ने अपनी जिंदगी के सबसे मुश्किल दौर के बारे में खुलकर बात की। साथ ही उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि टफ फेज में सिर्फ दो लोगों ने उनका साथ दिया, जिन्हें वो इंस्टाग्राम पर भी फॉलो करते हैं - राखी सावंत और दीपक कलाल। पूरे शो के दौरान समय ने राखी सावंत और दीपक कलाल की काफी टांग खींची और उन पर जोक्स भी किए। लेकिन इसके बावजूद दीपक कलाल इमोशनल हो गए और उन्होंने एक वीडियो शेयर करते हुए कहा... ...उसने कहा कि, अब आप आपके पापा के... को स्क्रेच करो, तो कूपन निकलेगा। कोई बहुत... कूपन आपको निकलेगा। इसीलिए मैं पापा को कहूंगा आई लव यू पापा, क्योंकि मैंने हमेशा मम्मी को ही बोला आई लव यू। लेकिन मेरे पापा की उम्र भी 85 है, और मैं कहूंगा आई लव यू पापा। लव यू पापा। कमेंट सेक्शन में बताइए क्या समय रैना देश के नंबर वन कॉमेडियन बन चुके हैं? यस और नो।

transcription: क्या लगता है कुल्लू क्या कर रहा होगा वहाँ पे? मज़ाक कर रहा होगा। मज़ाक? मस्ती। हां चक्ष, तुम्हें भी ये लगता है? मेरे को ट्रस्ट है उसपे बाकी देखते हैं। योगेश, वैसे क्या लगता है किसके साथ कनेक्शन है अकांक्षा? वारिस, उसके भी कर्ली बाल हैं। बाल से क्या हो गया, वो योगेश थोड़ी है। ठीक है चलो देख ही लेते हैं ना सीधे। मैंने फर्स्ट डेट कर रखी है ना यहाँ पे, उस हिसाब से बता रही हूँ की अच्छा था आज का। तुम लोग चिड़िया उड़ तो नहीं खेले? चिड़िया उड़ कौन खेलता है डेट पे? वो लग रहा है ठंडा। अभी तो शुरू करा है। मैं गिर रही हूँ। क्यूँ गिर रही है? मेरे प्यार में गिरना है तेरे को। I feel betrayed, I feel like a fool. और मेरे को लगता है हम दोनों ही बेवकूफ़ हैं। कितना आसान हो जाता है ना लोगों के लिए एकदम से ऐसे फ्लिप करना। कुल्लू जी इज़ हंड्रेड टाइम्स बेटर देन हिमांशु। हिमांशु हमें बात नहीं करने देता, हिमांशु इस... वो बोल नहीं सकते! कुल्लू जी इज़ द बेस्ट। बात करो ना। मेरा मज़ाक मत बनाओ अब। मेरा मज़ाक मत बनाओ मेरे इमोशंस का! मेरे इमोशंस का मज़ाक मत बनाओ! आपके अकॉर्डिंग चलेगा क्या? बच्चा है क्या घर का? You sound like a spoiled brat, आप हमें नहीं बता सकते हो कि मुझे बाहर भेजो। What is wrong with you? वो मज़ाक बना रहा है मेरा वहाँ पे। वहां चिल्ला रहे हो तुम लोग, मतलब क्या है? मतलब क्या है वहां चिल्लाने का? This is what she did. भेज दो ना मुझे यहाँ से! I want to go home! I want to go home! I want to go home!

title: Journal Reading 010 | Trust Your Journey, It Was Carved For You
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There was a point in time, earlier on in my spiritual awakening journey, when I was concerned with growth and getting better. Not that I don't want to grow now because of course I do, but in the beginning, the pursuit of growth was all-consuming. It was ego-driven. I went to the gym regularly, I meditated, I read self-help, spiritual books, and took notes. I even took up coaching others in an attempt to ditch the nine-to-five scene. None of the habits stuck for more than a few months, but I would always come back to them the following year. Like I said, it was ego-driven. I wanted to do better because, deep down, I felt I wasn't good enough. I felt behind in life, like I should be further along. And although that way of pursuing growth and self-improvement served its purpose, I now understand it's not the best way. Actually, I would even go as far as to say as adding habits to your daily routine for the sole purpose of getting better is the very thing that keeps you from getting better. Often times, our pursuit for better is rooted in social validation. We want to be liked, we want to be accepted, we want to be seen in a particular light. And the problem doesn't come from not being noticed or liked. Often times, along these sorts of external focus journeys, we are seen and liked, but we aren't seen and liked for who we actually are. I believe a better way to improve oneself is not to download a bunch of habits influencers have said that have changed their lives, but to do more of the things you enjoy. Lean into yourself, and forget what the internet says is good or bad. If running is what you love, then run because you love it, not because you think in three months you'll be a different person. If you genuine- if you genuinely enjoy having a couple of beers at the end of the day, have a couple of beers. The biggest lie the self-improvement space sold us was that there's something wrong with who we are, and that we need to fix it. There is nothing wrong with who you are or where you are at in life. We are all walking our own paths, evolving at our own pace. Don't let a stranger on the internet make you feel less than you are. True and lasting change will come when you're ready. And when you're ready, the change will be effortless. Trust your journey. It was carved for you. Thank you for watching. Have a good day.
caption: In a clear and calm voice, a woman shares a personal monologue about her journey with self-improvement and spiritual awakening. She reflects on how her initial pursuit of growth was driven by ego and a feeling of inadequacy, leading her to adopt habits like going to the gym and reading self-help books, which didn't stick. She shares her realization that forcing self-improvement habits for social validation can be counterproductive, and instead advocates for doing what one truly enjoys and trusting one's own pace of life. Her tone is reflective and sincere, and the quiet background of the recording allows her message to be heard clearly.

title: Fix Your Messy Life | The Bullet Journal Method | Ryder Carroll | chapter 4 (B01_0001_04)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Bullet journaling accepts that every day is different rather than trying to impose the same structure each time. This makes it flexible and able to handle whatever comes up. The main point is that bullet journaling embraces chaos with a system that can change as needed. A daily log has not set amount of space, use what you need that day. Some days may take just one page, others more. The monthly log has two pages, one for the calendar and one for tasks. Write events, tasks and notes on the calendar page next to each date. List tasks for the month on the other page. If a task is for a different month, write it in the future log, then add future tasks to the next month's log when that month starts. You can make custom pages for specific topics like health goals or a hobby. Use the index at the front to keep track of all your pages and collections. List the topic and page numbers. Keep adding to the index as needed. This flexible approach accepts that every day is different. The system can grow and change along with your need.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Secret Method | The Bullet Journal Method | Ryder Carroll | chapter 6 (B01_0001_06)

transcription: Your bullet journal can be a useful tool for setting and achieving meaningful goals. Start by making a goals collection to write down both big and small goals. This helps transform vague dreams into real objectives. Next, create timelines for your goals, using something like the 5-4-3-2-1 method. Identify goals for the next 5 years, 4 months, 3 weeks, 2 days and 1 hour. You will likely have many goals, so prioritize by carefully considering each one. Ask yourself if the goal is really important and worth the effort. Choose one personal and one professional goal in each timeframe, for a total of 10 priority goals. It's important to regularly re-evaluate your goals to make sure they still matter. One way is with goal sprints, breaking big goals into smaller steps to test your commitment. This can help you focus on goals that inspire you and keep you motivated, long term. Clarification and prioritizing will help make your goals a reality.

title: How to Build Habits That Actually Stick
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You're not failing when it comes to habits. You're just starting too many at once. Most people don't struggle because they're lazy. They struggle because they try to change their entire life overnight. They want to wake up earlier, start working out, eat healthier, drink more water, meditate, journal, read more, spend less time on their phone, all at the same time. And for a few days, it feels exciting, but then everything falls apart. Not because you're incapable, because your brain can't sustain that much change all at once. If your habits never seem to stick, the problem isn't motivation. It's the way you're trying to build them. Most habits fail because there's no structure behind them. People rely on motivation instead of systems. They tell themselves, "I'll work out after work tomorrow. I'll start eating healthier in a few days. I'll remember to do it." But vague habits don't survive real life because life gets busy, you get tired, your routine changes, your motivation drops, and if there's no repeatable structure, the habit disappears with it. Another mistake people make is setting the barrier too high. They think, "If I'm going to work out, I'm going to do 1 hour. If I'm going to read, I need to read an entire chapter. If I'm going to meal prep, I need to fix my entire diet." Eventually, your brain starts resisting it, not because the goal is bad, because the effort required feels too big to repeat consistently. That's why intensity usually fails. It asks too much before consistency exists. If you want a habit to stick, make it smaller, smaller than you think it should be. Make it so easy your brain has no reason to avoid it. Want to start working out? Don't commit to an hour. Commit to putting your shoes on and doing 5 to 10 minutes. Want to read more? Read one page. Want to meditate? Sit down for 30 seconds. Your goal in the beginning should not be full transformation. It should be repetition because repetition creates familiarity and familiarity lowers resistance. You're not trying to prove how disciplined you are. You should be trying to teach your brain that this is something you do now. Another thing that helps is attaching your habits to something that already exists. Instead of saying, "I'll do it later," anchor it to something specific. After I brush my teeth, I'll stretch. After work, I'll take a walk for 10 minutes. After making my coffee, I'll journal for a few minutes. The less decisions your brain has to make, the easier consistency becomes. That's what systems do. They reduce friction. Here's the part that nobody likes hearing. Consistency is supposed to feel boring sometimes. Social media makes change look exciting and intense, but real progress usually looks repetitive, quiet, simple, unimpressive. A lot of people quit because a habit no longer feels exciting. But habits that last aren't built on excitement. They're built on repeatability. You don't need perfect days. You need enough days repeated over time. Missing one day isn't failure. Starting over every single week is. The goal isn't to become a different person overnight. The goal is to create a system that you can maintain over time. If you want habits that actually stick, stop trying to change everything at once. Make the habit smaller. Remove friction. Repeat it consistently. Build structure around it. Because consistency is not built through intensity. It's built through repetition. Small actions repeated daily will always beat out massive effort that only lasts a week. Until one day, they become automatic. If this helped, subscribe. I'll be breaking down systems for your lifestyle so you can actually build something that works.

title: Bison Attack Survivor Speaks out on Dangerous Encounter

transcription: Look out, bison! Look out! For the first time overnight, Carl McDaniel is opening up about his now-viral face-to-face encounter with a raging bison last Friday at Montana's Yellowstone National Park. The 65-year-old grandfather, now recovering from a broken femur after the massive animal chased him around a camp before tossing him high into the air. McDaniel telling CNN, "We were about 100 yd away and the bison was not aggressive, so they snapped a few photos and continued walking." Photographer, Mike MacLeod, filmed the wild encounter. They were doing everything right. They were respectful, and once the bison showed any agitation, they left, and they were just at the wrong time and the wrong place. McDaniel says, around that time, a truck drove by and the driver honked his horn, in what he believes, was an apparent attempt to get the bison to move. And it worked. The sound agitated the bison and it began running toward them. McDaniel telling CNN, "There was not a lot of time. So, I told my grandson to run in one direction, and I went the other to try and draw him away." After chasing the pair around a wooded area, the hulking animal eventually caught up to McDaniel and sent him flying. McDaniel says he was on the ground and unable to move when something remarkable happened. "He was right on top of me, he could have stomped on me, he could have gored me, he could have done almost anything to take my life, and he did not do so." That's when the photographer says he immediately stopped filming and ran to help, yelling at the bison along with other Good Samaritans to scare it off. Because I could see that bison was standing over him and, um, pumping his head, very aggressive and agitated. And I knew that somebody had to distract that thing. McDaniel, who had surgery on Sunday, says he's grateful for all the people who helped, and thankful it was not much worse. See. I mean, what a story. And so, what does his recovery look like now, Camilla? Yeah, Savannah, so Carl McDaniel told CNN that he broke his femur in four places near his hip. He says he'll be doing physical therapy for the next few days to start walking. But he was thankfully able to stand yesterday, Savannah. Wow. And good for the person shooting to put down that camera and help. Right. Exactly. No. The right thing to do. Thank you so much. Hey, thanks for watching, and don't forget you can catch the Today Show every morning on NBC, or take Today when you're on the go. Just follow the Today podcast on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you listen.

title: Aurora Innovation: Business Review Highlights Q4 2025 with Co-Founder & CEO Chris Urmson
transcription: 2025 was a really big year for us. We launched our driverless trucks for the first time. We've been operating them day in and day out. Q4 continued to be great progress for us. We are, as of January, to over 250,000 driverless miles, which is nearly triple the mileage we had in October, increasing our revenue 25% quarter-over-quarter. And of course, we did all this while maintaining a perfect safety record and perfect on-time record. Our latest release unlocks our ability to operate driverlessly in the rain, in the fog, and in heavier wind. This unlocks really meaningful utilization gains because in the past, the Aurora Driver had been blocked from operation up to 40% of the time because of weather. This release also unlocks driverless operation between El Paso and Phoenix and complete bidirectional driverless operation between Fort Worth and El Paso. Fort Worth to Phoenix is a big deal because it's a 1,000-mile lane, and that 1,000 miles means that a person can't drive that in a single day within their hours of service limits. It means that the Aurora Driver is now offering a superhuman benefit to our customers. This year, we're really going to see our generalized AI approach unlock some rapid expansion. We expect to be operating across the Sun Belt this year, going to customer endpoints, really serving the need of our customers. That's going to start with one of the leading US carriers and their endpoint in Phoenix. We're also going between a sand mine and a customer site in Midland for Detmar. Detmar is a great example of how endpoints unlock value for customers. The Aurora Driver is going to be operating 20 hours a day for Detmar, hauling frac sand for their oil and gas industry customers on this 60-mile lane that's mostly freeway, effectively doubling the productivity of their assets. On top of that, we're going to be running from Laredo to Dallas, hauling berries for Driscoll's for Hirschbach. And we're going to end the year with over 200 trucks operating driverlessly day in and day out. Our new fleet's going to come online in Q2. It's going to be on the International LT platform, and we're not going to have to have an observer on board. With Volvo, we've really entered the industrialization phase. We're working with the New River Valley factory, where the first VNL with the Aurora Driver installed has come off the line, and that's really setting us up for the future. This is the foundation you need to really deliver product at scale. Looking further ahead to our third-generation system, we continue to make great progress on Novia. This hardware generation is really going to enable scale, allowing us to produce tens of thousands of trucks. We ended 2025 in a really strong position with $1.5 billion on our balance sheet. We anticipate that'll fund operations until we achieve positive free cash flow in 2028. Scaling over 200 trucks means that we're going to be able to generate somewhere between 14 and 16 million dollars of revenue this year. That's a 400% increase year-on-year. We're seizing the opportunity to transform logistics, one of the most important industries on the planet, and we're well on our way to having tens of thousands of Aurora-driven trucks on the road.

title: BPCL Recruitment 2026 Out | Process Operator & Technician Jobs | CBT | Diploma Jobs | BPCL Vacancy
transcription: Hello everyone, welcome to Med Easy. My name is Mandvi Dubey. So student, aaj aapke liye yahan jo opportunity aayi hai wo BPCL ki taraf se aayi hai. BPCL ek Maharatna CPSE hai, aur yahan pe jo aapke liye recruitment nikli hai wo aapki Mumbai aur Kochi refinery mein hai. Yahan pe Process Technician Chemical, Operator Chemical, aur Technician Mechanical mein, and Technician Electrical stream mein aapke liye yahan pe vacancies hain. Wahin agar hum baat karein to yahan pe Chemical ke liye 60, and Operator-Operator ke liye yahan pe 64 vacancies hain. Wahin Technician Operator Mechanical stream ke liye 38 vacancies hain, Technician Electrical stream ke liye yahan pe aapki 17 vacancies mention kar rakhi hain. Isi ke sath basic pay agar aapka dekhein to 26,500 rahega, pay scale aapka jo rahega, 26,500 se 34,000 ke rahega, isi ke sath aapko other benefits bhi yahan pe allowances milte hain. Minimum education qualification ki baat karein to agar aapne kisi bhi stream se diploma kar rakha hai, then you can apply, aur isi ke sath hi one year yahan should have minimum experience aapka yahan pe rehna chahiye, theek hai? Aur yahan pe eligible streams bhi mention hai to wo aap log check out kar lenge. Iske sath higher qualification yahan pe allowed nahi hogi, ye bhi yahan pe clearly mention kar rakha hai. And agar hum yahan pe dekhein, students, to yahan pe aapka jo age ka criteria rahega, minimum 18 years, maximum 25 years. Age relaxation bhi hai as per government norms, to wo bhi aap check out kar sakte hain. Selection procedure ki baat karein to CBT based test hoga aapka stage first mein jismein aapka domain knowledge 60 marks ka rahega and aapka jo general aptitude hai wo aapka 40 marks ka rahega. Isi ke sath yahan pe second stage jo rahega, students, wo skill proficiency test rahega, and third stage pre-employment medical examination rahega. CBT aapka objective type yahan pe pura test rehne wala hai. And yahan pe reservation and relaxation bhi hai as per government guidelines. Aur is notification ki PDF link aapko video ke description box mein mil jayegi, aap wahan ja ke bhi go through kar sakte hain. Aap iski official website pe ja ke visit karke is application form ko fill kar sakte hain and yahan pe jo iski link hai wo aapko video ke description box mein mil jayegi, aap wahan ja ke bhi go through kar sakte hain. Agar hum dekhein to 29-07-2026 se iske form start ho gaye hain fill out hona, aur jo iski last date rahegi, student, wo 13-08-2026 rahegi, to iski last date se pehle aap is form ko zaroor fill karlein. Hope so, student, ye information aapke liye kaafi zyada beneficial rahi hogi. Aur if you have any other doubt, please do comment in the comment box. Thank you so much, take care, stay tuned.

title: How Buyers Actually Evaluate a Business (In Under 3 Minutes)
transcription: So can you speak a little bit about how buyers evaluate a business? So, you know, Rick, most owners they they see it through the lenses of the time that they have invested in building the business and, you know, it's always the rose-colored glasses sometimes. However, buyers they tend to evaluate through the risk and the transferability and also the future earnings of the business. When, you know, a buyer comes to the table and it's a private equity group or strategic buyers, they often show up with their own teams of attorneys and analysts and accountants and all the players that are involved. That makes that playing field very complex very quickly and without having the right advisor on your side to help you navigate that, it it can get very, very sticky quickly. Um, you know, one of the reasons we wanted to host this webinar today is because we frequently meet owners who have built remarkable companies, but haven't given much thought at all to the exit process until a circumstance, you know, comes to the forefront. And that could be anything from a seller being burn out or having health issues, or maybe there's a partner in the business that they have a dispute with. All kinds of things can happen that that can cause someone to want to, as I say, have a knee-jerk reaction to getting the business on the market and selling it. By the time they reach out, you know, we want to make sure that the financials are lender ready for the for the most part because most lenders they want to see clean financials. Um, you know, it doesn't mean that that it can't be fixed, but we need to be able to work quickly with the advisors, with the folks that are involved on on the seller's team to make that more attractive to the lenders so we can get it across the finish line. And when you get those cleaned up, it definitely makes the process go much smoother.

title: Insurers' Shifting Priorities - Pricing Modernization Webinar Clip
transcription: Okay, so this data comes from our annual survey of insurers on the factors that shape their IT investment priorities. So last year, and in most prior years, the number one thing is growth. If it'll help me grow, I will spend money. But this year, the picture changed noticeably. Growth, as you can see, moved down to third place, while data and innovation emerged as the leading priorities. In fact, last year, data wasn't even in the top five, and so here it is, number one, without even being something that we saw last year. Now, that does not mean that growth and efficiency are no longer important, because nearly all insurers, 98%, still said growth was a big area of focus in 2026. But what's changing is how they're thinking about achieving it, right? Increasingly, insurers are seeing data as the foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement. And so these priorities, they're no longer really separate initiatives, they're deeply interconnected, they're increasingly dependent upon each other. So, growth, number one thing that carriers are focusing on. But at the same time, the market environment is changing. Now, this comes from a study of policyholders who had a personal auto claim in the last two years. And we picked personal auto because we were looking at the claims experience. And personal auto is kind of homogeneous when it comes to claims, as opposed to something like, you know, general liability. Anyway, we found that 25% of those who had a claim loved their carrier so much after the claim that they would pay more to stay. But half of all policyholders with a claim told us that they were actively looking for lower premium elsewhere, or had already moved. So, policyholders shopping at historically high rates. And in that environment, the goal can't just be how low can you go to keep your customers, right? Or to attract new customers. That approach always creates long-term profitability challenges. So, the real question is, what is the right price for this specific customer based on their individual risk profile? Now, when insurers rely on broad rating bands, they increase the likelihood of adverse selection, right? Because the lower-risk customers are more likely to leave in search of pricing that more adequately reflects their actual risk, while the higher-risk customers are more likely to stay because they're getting a lower price than they should be paying. And this is why pricing precision matters so much right now, like not only for attracting the customers who are actively shopping, but also for retaining the ones already in your portfolio.

She notes a significant shift in priorities: while growth was traditionally the top priority, data and innovation have now emerged as the leading focus areas, with growth dropping to third place. However, she explains that growth remains crucial, with 98% of insurers still prioritizing it, but the method has shifted—insurers now view data as the essential foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement.

The speaker then transitions to changing market dynamics, referencing a study on policyholders who filed auto claims in the past two years. She highlights a stark contrast in customer loyalty: while 25% of customers would pay more to stay with their current carrier, a massive 50% are actively shopping for lower premiums or have already switched. She warns against competing solely on low prices, as this undermines long-term profitability. Instead, she advocates for pricing precision based on individual risk profiles to avoid adverse selection, where low-risk customers depart for better rates and high-risk customers remain. title: Disconnected Management Systems Are Undermining Strategy Execution
transcription: Here we're focusing on strategy and performance, right? And when we talk about strategy and performance, there is a series of corporate processes that are part of this big umbrella that we call strategy and performance corporate processes. So we have governance, we have succession management, we have project management, audits, balanced scorecards, ISOs, certifications, innovation management, KPIs, OKRs, budgets and so much more, right? I'm not going to go through all of these. The idea is there is a number of practices or processes or management models that have, that interact with each other and we call corporate management. And each one of these can have a software to support that practice, right? So you can have a software for OKRs, for example, another software for your BIs or your dashboards or your balanced scorecard, another software for your Scrum projects or task management and so on. So for each of these practices, we have a whole ecosystem of softwares to support that practice, right? And what we've been seeing in organizations is that as you adopt an app or a software for each of these practices, they stop interacting with themselves. This should be practices that are make sense independently, but they're also part of a management system, and they should interact with each other. But when you have apps or softwares for each of these, they stop talking to each other. They start acting as silos of information, right? And this is the reality that we see in most organizations. If we take a look at this chart, this chart is the number of app SaaS apps, on average, for each organization, right? So the average number of SaaS apps. And we see that in 2015, we had only 8 SaaS apps, on average, for an organization. And this jumped to 80 in 2020 in just 5 years, then to 130 in 2022. This is the phenomenon that we call SaaS sprawl or app sprawl, right? It was the proliferation of SaaS applications in organizations, and it just boomed, right? From, in 7 years, from 8 to 130. And all of these specialized apps came about and companies adopted them, and for each activity, each management practice, you had an app for that or you have an app for that. But this created big problems in the organizations, right? Managing SaaS is a new problem for IT. So there are so many providers, that managing it all is a huge problem. And integrating it all is a huge problem. So if you have 8 SaaS applications, and you buy the 9th, okay, you're going to integrate, you know, this new SaaS application with 8 others to connect the information. But if you have 130 apps, and you buy the 131st, how are you going to connect all this? It's- it's impossible, right? So this has become a big pain in, especially in larger corporations.

title: Are You Pricing Your MedSpa Services for Profit—or Just to Stay Competitive?
transcription: The second truth is the one that made me the most uncomfortable when I finally sat with it. Your pricing is a confession. Every time you set a price, every time you discount without real reason, every time you say the number and then apologize when someone flinches, you are making a statement about what you believe you are worth. I underpriced for years. Years of doing extraordinary things in a 300 sq ft room in Central Plaza, years of introducing treatments Jamaica had never seen and charging as though I was grateful for the opportunity rather than confident in the value. And here is the real truth underneath that truth. I was scared. Not of the work. Never of the work. I was scared that if I priced what I was actually worth, people would say no. That fear kept me overworked and underpaid for longer than I want to admit.

title: Why Are Top Economists Warning of a Rising Recession Risk in 2026?
transcription: Recession risk is rising fast and could hit within weeks. Will geopolitical tensions and inflation push the global economy over the edge right now? Energy prices are not just a headline. When energy costs rise, businesses face higher expenses and often pass those on to consumers. This causes people to cut back on spending, creating a feedback loop that weakens economic growth. This dynamic is a key reason economists are so worried about inflation's lingering impact on the economy in 2026. Top economist Mohamed El-Erian has issued a stark warning. He says the global economy faces a critical eight-week window to prevent a recession. The trigger is the reopening of a crucial oil route currently disrupted by geopolitical tensions. If this route stays closed, energy supplies tighten further, pushing costs higher and escalating recession risks worldwide. Another leading economist, Mark Zandi, agrees recession risks are rising significantly. He estimates about a 40% chance of recession this year. However, Zandi still sees a path to avoid it, especially if geopolitical tensions ease. The key challenge is managing inflation, which remains elevated even if tensions cool. Investors are already feeling the pressure. Zandi warns the S&P 500 could fall by as much as 30% as the market adjusts to the real economic risks behind inflated stock valuations. This signals a painful correction ahead for many portfolios as the economy deals with these pressures. Even if geopolitical tensions ease and energy routes reopen, elevated prices are expected to persist. Zandi estimates this will cost the average household roughly $1,400 a year. This ongoing inflation squeeze means families will feel the impact directly through higher everyday expenses. What this means for you is clear: the next two months are critical. Energy prices and geopolitical events could shape your financial future. You might face higher costs and a volatile stock market. Staying informed and cautious with spending and investments is key. title: Introducing Claude Fable 5
transcription: Today we're launching Claude Fable 5. The most capable model we've ever released to the public. Fable 5 is a mythos class model with safeguards that make it ready for general use. We didn't broadly release our previous model with this level of capability because when we finished training and testing it, we saw that the model, Claude Mythos Preview, was finding thousands of cybersecurity vulnerabilities. A model that can find flaws like that can also be used to exploit them. So instead of releasing it, we handed it to the people who protect the world's critical software and put it to work fixing the holes before someone could break through them. It was the right call for the moment, but it was never the goal. We believe powerful AI should be safe and accessible. That's why we went to work on Claude Fable 5. Every Claude model has safeguards to keep it from doing harm. Fable needed more cautious ones than anything we've built before. Our safety systems for Fable 5 automatically review requests that touch on high-risk areas like cybersecurity or biology. Those requests are then redirected to Opus 4.8. We do that intentionally so people can continue to benefit from the capabilities of a powerful model like Fable without the cyber and biology risks that come with it. The safeguards are broad today, but we'll keep refining them so that they're better at allowing safe requests. We built Claude Fable 5 for your most ambitious work. It can stay with a problem far longer than any model before it. It's highly autonomous and can operate for days without intervention. And it's not just coding. It can take on projects in finance, research, economics, law - complicated tasks that used to need constant supervision. So point it at something that matters. What's the problem we'll look back on and wonder why it took so long to solve? We know what Claude Fable 5 can do. The interesting part is what you'll do with it.

title: UKREiiF 2026: 'Where the smart money is moving' panel discussion
transcription: So, we're here at UKREIIF this year, talking all things living UK real estate. The current environment for living real estate in the UK is one with viability challenges and concerns. We've got rising build cost inflation, increased regulation, economic difficulties. What there also is, is a huge amount of opportunity. There is pent-up demand, there is under supply, there is no shortage of debt available, there is capital being deployed. It is a huge time for opportunity. The smart money is moving primarily into affordable housing, I would say, though how you define that depends on a number of factors, but clearly the biggest risk to any investment strategy is take-up and demand at this moment, and so through various lenses people are trying to make sure that whatever it is that they're investing in or developing is affordable for the end user, so that the project is viable long-term. I think there's quite a lot of opportunity for living product, because there is a fundamental requirement and demand for good quality accommodation across all the living sectors, asset classes. Especially when there is a bit of an affordability gap. So, those that can deliver product that meets that demand are going to be very well placed. 2026, for me, has also been the year of co-living. We're seeing more institutionalisation of co-living, in terms of an accepted asset class for co-investors. So, I think the opportunities at the moment, very much from a housebuilders point of view, are in the land market. Slightly longer-term strategic sites, gray belt, something where you can work with a landowner to really maximize the number of homes on a site, and really go out there and get a planning consent. I believe that the opportunities in the living sector lie in working in partnership, both with local governments, local councils, with developers, with capital, trying to bring everybody together to achieve the ultimate goal of delivering more housing for the country. I think the smart money in living is moving to affordable with a small 'a'. That's how we deal with the viability concerns. That's where some degree of public subsidy can unlock delivery. I also see there's huge opportunities in partnerships becoming platforms, with long-term sustainable partnerships between registered providers, developers and investors to unlock delivery at scale.

title: Designing the Safer Transit Bus | Innovation for Operator Health
transcription: As was mentioned, I'm Jonathan Hack. I've spent my career in the transportation sector, all in the innovation area. And we've got an exciting panel discussion for you here today. You're going to hear from various perspectives. You're going to hear from the TTC, from Dr. Sarah Fox. You're going to hear from the Amalgamated Transit Workers Union, and you're going to hear from the operators themselves. What I want to talk about today is, um, a kind of deceptively simple idea, which is that if we want safer transit systems, we need to design them with the people who actually do the work. At the end of the day, like, we really want to democratize innovation. We want to make sure that it's cascaded across, so it should be coming from the workers, from the front line. With every new technology that finds its way into the bus, we then take a step back and say, well, how does that now combine with all the other things? Participation is not optional. It's a safety requirement. There's often a tendency to frame innovation that's something that happens to workers. Um, but what this research shows is that transit operators are already experts in safety-critical system management. The challenge moving forward is building processes that recognize and incorporate that expertise.

title: Inside the Cigna Healthcare Broker Connect & Insight Forum 2026 | Corporate Event Highlights
transcription: Welcome to the Cigna Broker Insight Conference 2026. We are really grateful to have you here. Thank you for joining us. It's great to see so many, uh, familiar faces, uh, here with us. Delighted to have you here to host for what we hope is an engaging, insightful, and enjoyable conversation. Since the opening of our expanded office in May, many of you and your teams have been in with us, have spent time with us through workshops and different working sessions. The collaboration during those sessions and the feedback you have shared has been incredibly valuable to us. And I'm happy to confirm that Africa continues to be a key growth market for us. Our commitment here is long-term, deliberate, and strategic, and Kenya sits right at the heart of that journey. As advocates for improving health, we've been conducting annual insight studies that help us better understand the key aspects of people's health and well-being in order to improve the vitality of those we serve. The data that I will present today reflects a sample of over 500 people in Kenya and over 11,000 globally, and those are not necessarily Cigna customers, but are really a cross-section of of the society. I'm sure you, you will agree with me, because both health and vitality are foundational for thriving individuals, for thriving families, thriving communities, and they help foster, ultimately, a healthy economy, a healthy workforce, and a healthy society. The true value of any health solution is only ever revealed in a moment of crisis. And in that moment, what people desperately need is not just coverage. They need to know that someone is there, someone who knows their name, someone who picks up the phone, and someone who comes to them. Cigna Africa is that someone. We pass our love back to your teams in the offices, please pass our love to them, and we look forward to partnering. Thank you very much. I have been honored to be your MC tonight, and we look forward to seeing more of you in the coming events. Asanteni sana.

transcription: आशीष, आपसे शुरुआत करते हैं। इंडेक्स स्टॉक पहले BEL। क्या एक्सपेक्ट करें? स्टेडी नंबर्स यहां पर देखने को मिल सकते हैं। अच्छा BEL में ख़ास बात ये होती है कि मैं ब्रोकरेज हाउस की रिपोर्ट्स पढ़ रहा था कि क्वार्टरली बेसिस पर हर बार क्योंकि प्रोडक्ट मिक्स अलग-अलग होता है तो हर बार मार्जिन एक जैसे या फिर हर बार मार्जिन में ग्रोथ आप एक्सपेक्ट करके नहीं चल सकते। ख़ास बात होती है कि आर्डर बुक कैसी है, एग्जीक्यूशन कैसा देखने को मिला और टॉपलाइन कैसी है। ये BEL के केस में बड़ा इंपॉर्टेंट होता है। तो सबसे पहले आप देखें तो टॉपलाइन काफी हेल्दी है, कारण ये कि आर्डर इनफ्लो बहुत अच्छा रहा है। पूरे FY24 में देखें या क्वार्टर 4 में, तक़रीबन 14% की बढ़त यहां पर एक्सपेक्टेड है। 10,371 करोड़ का अनुमान मार्केट लगाकर चल रहा है। अगर आप आपरेशनल फ्रंट पर देखें तो स्टेडी क्वार्टर है, हालांकि कोई गिरावट नहीं है, बढ़त भी नहीं है, 2% के आसपास के चेंज आपको देखने को मिलेंगे। और मार्जिन जैसा कि मैंने बताया कि प्रोडक्ट मिक्स के ऊपर बहुत ज्यादा डिपेंड करता है तो जो 30.6% का एबिटा मार्जिन पिछले साल थे, अब इस बार 27.4 देखने को मिल सकते हैं और मुनाफे का आंकड़ा भी बिल्कुल फ्लैट है, कोई बढ़त नहीं है, सिर्फ 3% की ग्रोथ यहां पर देखने को मिलेगी। लेकिन बड़ा इंपॉर्टेंट होता है कि एग्जीक्यूशन कैसा है। तो इस क्वार्टर के दौरान एग्जीक्यूशन क्योंकि वैसे भी इनकी तरफ से जो अपडेट आया था क्वार्टर 4 का, उसमें पता चल रहा था कि एग्जीक्यूशन बढ़िया देखने को मिला है और आर्डर इनफ्लो की बात करें तो 11,200 करोड़ के आसपास यानी पिछले साल के मुकाबले 30% ज्यादा है। एक्सपोर्ट की रेवेन्यू, एक्सपोर्ट के ऑर्डर्स ये लगातार बढ़ रहे हैं, पिछले साल के मुकाबले एक्सपोर्ट की रेवेन्यू 34% बढ़ सकती है और ख़ास तौर पर इनका एग्जीक्यूशन इनके की-प्रोडक्ट्स में कैसा है, इसका मार्केट पर ज्यादा फोकस रहेगा। नंबर्स के लिहाज से आप एटलीस्ट स्टेडी नंबर्स एक्सपेक्ट करके चल सकते हैं। स्टेडी नंबर्स फ्रॉम BEL। ये आशीष ने अगर आप देखें, एक्सपेक्टेशन जाहिर की, पूर्वानुमान में।

transcription: नमस्कार, आप देख रहे हैं बिस्तख और मैं हूं आपके साथ चिराग ठाकुर। देश की दिग्गज आईटी कंपनी टाटा कंसल्टेंसी सर्विसेज यानी कि टीसीएस ने गुरुवार को अपने चौथे तिमाही के नतीजे जारी किए, जिसमें कंपनी का प्रदर्शन मजबूत रहा। कंपनी का कंसोलिडेटेड नेट प्रॉफिट सालाना आधार पर 12% बढ़कर ₹13,718 करोड़ पहुंच गया। पिछले साल इसी तिमाही में यह ₹12,224 करोड़ था। कंपनी ने ₹31 प्रति शेयर का फाइनल डिविडेंड घोषित किया है। इससे निवेशकों को सीधा फायदा मिलेगा। टीसीएस का ऑपरेशन से रेवेन्यू 10% बढ़कर ₹70,698 करोड़ हो गया है। कंपनी को यह फायदा ऐसे समय में हुआ है जब आईटी सेक्टर आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस में नए-नए बदलाव के कारण उतार-चढ़ाव भरे दौर से गुजर रहा है। इस कारण कंपनी के शेयरों में हाल में बड़ी गिरावट आई थी। टीसीएस ने इस तिमाही में 12 अरब डॉलर की कुल डील वैल्यू यानी कि टीसीबी हासिल की है। जिसमें तीन बड़ी मेगा डील शामिल है। कंपनी की विकास दर में आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस की भूमिका सबसे अहम रही है। कंपनी की सीओओ आरती सुब्रमण्यम के अनुसार FY26 एआई अपनाने के मामले में एक निर्णायक साल रहा। चौथी तिमाही में कंपनी का सालाना एआई रेवेन्यू 2.3 अरब डॉलर के पार निकल गया है। टीसीएस ने अपने हाइपरवोल्ड निवेश के जरिए ओपनएआई, एएमडी और एबीबी जैसी दिग्गज कंपनियों के साथ रणनीतिक हाथ मिलाया है। कंपनी ने इंटरप्राइज ट्रांसफॉर्मेशन, डिजिटल इंजीनियरिंग और क्लाउड मॉर्डनाइजेशन जैसे क्षेत्रों में मजबूत डील्स हासिल किया है। कंपनी ने माना की वैश्विक आर्थिक चुनौतियां बनी हुई हैं लेकिन ग्राहकों का टेक्नोलॉजी निवेश पर भरोसा मजबूत है। नतीजों के ऐलान से पहले बीएसई पर टीसीएस का शेयर 1.09% की तेजी के साथ ₹2587.75 पर बंद हुआ। एक्सपर्ट का मानना है कि शानदार मार्जिन और एआई क्षेत्र में कंपनी की बढ़ती पकड़ आने वाले समय में स्टॉक को और मजबूती दे सकती है। इसके अलावा, टीसीएस ने 1 अप्रैल से सभी ग्रेड के कर्मचारियों के लिए सालाना सैलरी बढ़ोतरी लागू करने का ऐलान किया है। हालांकि, इस बार कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी इसका खुलासा नहीं किया गया है। खास बात यह है कि कंपनी एक तरफ सैलरी बढ़ा रही है तो दूसरी तरफ कुल कर्मचारियों की संख्या में सालाना आधार पर कमी भी देखने को मिली है। हालांकि, इस बार सबसे बड़ा सवाल यही है कि सैलरी में कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी। कंपनी ने अभी तक हाइक का परसेंट स्पष्ट नहीं किया है। पिछले साल FY25 में टीसीएस ने सैलरी हाइक में करीब 5 महीने की देरी की थी और सितंबर 2025 से इसे लागू किया गया था। उस समय औसतन 4.5% से 7% तक की बढ़ोतरी दी गई थी। जबकि बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने वाले कर्मचारियों को डबल डिजिट हाइक मिला था। आप टीसीएस के नतीजों के बारे में क्या सोचते हैं, कमेंट करके हमें जरूर बताएं और बने रहे बिस्तख के साथ।

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 explained: How the new 48-team format works
transcription: For years, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has talked about getting more countries involved at a World Cup. That push finally took shape in January 2017 when football's governing body voted to expand the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Under the new format, there will be 104 matches at this World Cup. That's 40 more than at Qatar 2022. Those games will be played across 16 host cities in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. That's a huge change from the compact 2022 tournament in Qatar where a fan could realistically attend two or even three matches in a single day. The 48 teams will be split into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group plus the eight best third-placed teams will move into a new 32-team knockout phase. From there, the tournament runs through the round of 32, the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and then the final. By the time we get to the decider at MetLife Stadium in New York, New Jersey, on July the 19th, the champions will have played eight matches. That's one more than the seven required by Argentina when they won Qatar 2022.

title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup explained in 2 minutes
transcription: The stage is set for this year's FIFA Men's World Cup, with the opening matches kicking off tomorrow. The tournament, held every four years, will be unlike any before it. Here's why. Firstly, it will be the biggest World Cup in history, the most complex one yet. For the first time ever, the tournament will be shared across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and matches will be played across 16 cities. The competition is expanding, too. Instead of the traditional eight groups, this year's tournament will feature 12, made up of four teams each. 48 national teams will compete, instead of 32. With more teams in the mix, the road to glory could be tougher to predict. The expansion means a record number of matches. Teams will play 104 matches over 39 days, making it the longest ever World Cup run. With more teams involved, there could be more opportunities for underdogs to make their mark. Among those returning to the World Cup include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, and Iraq, while four debutants are getting their boots on the pitch for the first time. They are Uzbekistan, Jordan, Curacao, and Cape Verde. But staging the World Cup across three countries brings major logistical challenges. Some teams could end up traveling thousands of kilometers between venues, crossing borders and time zones. FIFA has grouped matches regionally to reduce travel, but long journeys may still be unavoidable for teams that progress deep into the tournament. And depending on where they're playing, the climates could be different, from the high altitude of Mexico City to Miami's heat and humidity. To manage that, FIFA has mandated cooling and hydration breaks during matches. Next, technology will play a bigger role than ever before. Every player will have a digital avatar to remodel on-pitch actions. These changes make it easier for officials to see what would go on during fast or obstructed plays, so they can provide more accurate calls for offsides or potential handballs. And then, of course, there are the stars. This could be the last dance for several legends. Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed this will be his last World Cup. Argentina's Lionel Messi and Croatia's Luka Modrić are also widely expected to be making their final appearances on the game's biggest stage. For football's greats, one final bow. For a new generation, a chance to make history. The road to World Cup glory is about to begin.

title: How Mohammad Irfan Went From Street Hawker To India's Most Viral Protest Voice
transcription: सिर्फ पेट रोटी खा लेना ही जीवन नहीं है। शहरी सलम में जीवन नरक है। मैं कहता हूँ लोकतंत्र में ना अहंकार नहीं संवाद होना चाहिए और संवाद के दरवाज़े दोनों तरफ़ से खुले होने चाहिए। संविधान की शपथ में ना गरिमा शब्द का, व्यक्ति की गरिमा, राष्ट्र की एकता और अखंडता को सुनिश्चित, तो व्यक्ति की गरिमा, गरिमा, गरिमा नहीं गिरनी चाहिए सर। जय श्री कृष्णा सर, मैं इरफ़ान सर और आज मुझे आपसे बहुत सारी बातें करनी है सर। चार ट्रिलियन की अर्थव्यवस्था में ना पढ़े-लिखों का ही जीवन संवरा है? A voice that rose about the slogans at Jantar Mantar is now being heard in the country's political corridors. Mohammad Irfan, the hawker with little formal education whose speeches went viral during the student protest, met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday. Rahul Gandhi said Irfan's understanding of the constitution and his desire to learn reflected the strength of India's youth. Hours after the meet, Irfan spoke exclusively to India Today's sister platform, The Lallantop, with a message that cuts across party lines. मैं आज राहुल गांधी से मिला तो मैंने उनसे यही कहा कि अगर सर आप जो हम आपसे अपनी मांगे रख रहे हैं, आप विपक्ष के बड़े नेता हैं और आज नहीं तो कल सत्ता में आएंगे, अगर आपने हमारी बातों के वादाखिलाफी की तो हम अपनी असहमति आपके खिलाफ भी रखेंगे। For Irfan, accountability does not stop with one government or one political party. और हम न्यूट्रल हैं, हम इस देश का भला चाहते हैं। He also spoke about the struggles of migrant workers. 2024 का एनसीआरबी का डाटा कहता है कि 1 लाख 70 हजार 746 मौतें हुई जिसमें 31% दिहाड़ी मजदूर थे और वजह एक थी कि घर में तंगी और मानसिक संतुलन डिस्टर्ब होना, आर्थिक तंगी थी। तो हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उस वर्ग को जो इस देश की बड़ी आबादी है और खून-पसीना लगा रही है इस देश के निर्माण में? हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उसे? From the streets of Jantar Mantar to the national spotlight, his story is not about political power. It's about the power of a citizen's voice to be heard. If you liked the video, do like, comment, share, and subscribe.
caption:
The audio begins with a passionate and energetic speech in Hindi by a man named Mohammad Irfan. His voice is intense, slightly raspy, and filled with conviction as he talks about the hardships of slum life, the true meaning of democracy, and the dignity of individuals. A dramatic, suspenseful instrumental track plays in the background, amplifying his emotional delivery. 

This is followed by a brief, casual clip where Irfan warmly greets someone, saying "Jai Shree Krishna," amidst outdoor ambient sounds and footsteps. 

Soon, a professional male narrator with a clear Indian English accent takes over, introducing Irfan as a hawker with limited formal education whose speeches went viral. The narrator explains Irfan's recent meeting with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. The background transitions to a motivational, upbeat news-style instrumental track.

The audio continues with a mix of the narrator's commentary and snippets of Irfan's speeches. Irfan speaks with great fervor about political accountability, emphasizing that his dissent will remain even if the opposition comes to power. He also highlights the struggles of migrant workers, citing grim statistics about their deaths and mental stress due to financial hardship. 

The video wraps up with the narrator emphasizing the power of a citizen's voice, followed by an upbeat outro track encouraging viewers to like, comment, share, and subscribe.

title: Hear from Afroman after the verdict in his civil trial
transcription:
Outside this Adams County courthouse, the sound of victory.
After a jury sided with the musician Afroman, whose real name is Joseph Foreman, after a days-long civil defamation trial. Afroman, speaking to WCPO right after the verdict.
I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.
...the jury finds in favor of the defendant.
Seven Adams County Sheriff's deputies sued the musician. They argued Afroman used security video from a 2022 raid of his home and put it in music videos using deputies' likeness without permission.
There's damage to reputation, there's pain and suffering, there's public humiliation. There's everything you saw and heard from these detectives, from the witness stand.
This raid taking place nearly a year ago following search warrants related to possession and trafficking in drugs and kidnapping. The rapper was never charged. Along with using the surveillance video in multiple music videos, including in the song "Lemon Pound Cake", the deputies also say Afroman called them thieves and pedophiles among other things on social media.
I didn't go down here and sue the police department. I fixed up the damages they made, and I sung songs about them to raise money to do it. They were unapologetic.
The deputies wanted Afroman to pay $3.9 million in damages.
We got about a total of 250 pieces given out. This is the last one, and I'd like to give it to you.
Supporters of Afroman coming from near and far, with a message both verbally and symbolically.
For me, this isn't really about Afroman, it's about free speech. So, when someone like Afroman stands up for my free speech by using his talents, his musical talents, to fight the corrupt system, we gotta come out and support him.
I'm glad thing, you know, things went my way. But if they would have took it all from me, I was happy about all the love I was getting from everybody. After them people kicked my kicked my door in.
In Adams County, Jay Warren, WCPO 9 News.
When life give you lemons, you make lemon pound cake.

I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.

transcription: दोस्तों आईपीएल 2026 को लेकर आरसीबी टीम की कड़ी प्रैक्टिस शुरू हो चुकी है। जी हां दोस्तों, इसी बीच आरसीबी के खिलाड़ियों द्वारा दोस्तों 20-20 ओवर का वार्म अप मैच खेला गया। जी हां दोस्तों, इस वार्म अप मैच में एक तरफ थी कुणाल पांड्या की टीम, वहीं दूसरी तरफ थी वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम और वहीं दोस्तों, इस वार्म अप मैच में दोस्तों वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम पहले बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए आई और दोस्तों, हमें इस मुकाबले में जितेश शर्मा की काफी ताबड़तोड़ और विस्फोटक बल्लेबाजी देखने को मिली। जी हां दोस्तों, आपको बता दें कि इस मुकाबले में जितेश शर्मा मात्र 37 गेंदों में 81 रनों की शानदार पारी खेले और वहीं दोस्तों, टीम डेविड मात्र 14 गेंदों में 36 रनों की ताबड़तोड़ पारी खेले और वहीं कप्तान वेंकटेश अय्यर के 16 गेंदों में 30 रन और विराट कोहली के 12 गेंदों में 29 रनों की बदौलत वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम कुणाल पांड्या की टीम के सामने सात विकेट के नुकसान पर 234 रन बनाती है। 235 रनों के लक्ष्य का पीछा करते हुए कुणाल पांड्या की टीम की तरफ से रजत पाटीदार और देवदत्त पडिक्कल की काफी तूफानी और विस्फोटक बल्लेबाजी देखने को मिली। दोस्तों, आपको बता दें कि इस मुकाबले में देवदत्त पडिक्कल और कप्तान कुणाल पांड्या बतौर ओपनर बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए आए और दोस्तों, देवदत्त पडिक्कल ने 33 गेंदों में 63 रन, वहीं कुणाल पांड्या ने 23 गेंदों में 58 रन बनाए और दोस्तों, रजत पाटीदार के 25 गेंदों में 74 रनों के बदौलत कुणाल पांड्या की टीम निर्धारित 20 ओवर में 247 रन बनाई। तो दोस्तों, यहां पर आपको क्या लगता है कि आरसीबी टीम आईपीएल 2026 को लेकर जिस तरह से प्रैक्टिस कर रही है, वह अपने आने वाले वाले मुकाबले में दोस्तों हैदराबाद को हरा पाएगी कि नहीं, अपनी राय कमेंट बॉक्स में जरूर बताएं।

title: Marco Rubio Rails Against 'Globalist Bureaucrats' At ICC And 'So-Called International Law'
transcription: For 250 years, Americans have governed ourselves as a free and sovereign people. We choose our own leaders, we determine our own laws, and when we're accused of a crime, we stand for judgment before a jury of our own peers. This is the essential and indispensable feature of our form of government. It is the foundation of our shared way of life. But today, powerful people in faraway places want to take that away from us. They believe that they should be in charge of your laws, of your country, your life, and they don't care whether or not you agree. Halfway across the world, there's an institution that calls itself the International Criminal Court. Maybe you've heard of it, maybe you haven't. But chances are you don't know the names of its judges, of its prosecutors, or its president, and you shouldn't have to. But as we speak, the ICC and its friends are waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles, but with statutes and compacts and the force of so-called international law. When the ICC was born 24 years ago, they told us that it was merely a narrow backstop, a global court that would step in to prosecute only the gravest offenses, things like genocide and war crimes, and only when a nation's courts were unable to prosecute them on their own. But the truth is, it was something far more radical and extreme. It was a global tribunal staffed by unelected globalist bureaucrats who claim their power is almost unlimited. The danger of this global court has only continued to grow. Today, it threatens every aspect of our political and legal system. Border patrol agents removing violent criminals from our country, American Marines risking their lives to defend our homeland, prosecutors working to dismantle terrorist plots to attack and kill Americans. If we stand idle, all of them would be at the mercy of foreign judges thousands of miles away, facing the constant risk of prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called crime of defending their own country. The American people never agreed to any of this, and they never will. Read the words of our Declaration of Independence. We fought a revolution against a foreign power transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses. Independence is our birthright. We will never let foreign bureaucrats take that away from us. This administration will not sit by as the ICC and its allies seek to threaten our people. If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.
caption: In this audio clip, a mature male speaks with a distinct, confident American accent. His tone is slow-paced and patriotic, delivering a serious and resolute message about American sovereignty. title: Highlights | Quantum USA
transcription: Quantum technologies are vitally important to economic prosperity and to national security. Over the next few years, the demand for quantum-literate professionals is going to outpace the supply, and that's something that, you know, we need an answer for. Post-quantum cryptography and the exercise of migrating towards that is far more complex than anyone really understood. It's far more than just switching algorithms. We need to iterate quickly, fail fast, get back up, build the muscle memory to continue to develop what we can with what we have. There are tremendous assets in the field of quantum technology, and what we need to do is better coordinate those by developing an operational strategy and then executing together. It's important to bring people together to discuss things forthrightly and transparently. We have differing opinions perhaps, but it's important to hear those differing opinions. We're thinking about these technologies in terms of a system, how they interconnect, how they relate to one another. We are also thinking about dual-use capabilities in order to accelerate market adoption. We need to bring in different teams with diverse perspectives because we need experts in quantum, we need experts in industry to build the use cases and create those bridges, and then we need people that know how to create that interconnection layer. Now we're dealing in a multi-domain environment, not only just across networking, security, and compute or cloud, but also across land, air, sea, and space. And so all the stakeholders that will ensure a right business or mission outcome need to be involved because it's not just about quantum as a compute, it's really about how we connect and protect that compute to deliver that mission or business outcome. There is a whole lot to be discovered, and now is the time. Collaboration across domain experts, quantum scientists, software developers, business leaders, research centers, I can keep going on and on. Now is the time to start thinking about that. I really think the biggest points for a quantum strategy right now is taking care of the organizational and human layers of this transition. We have so much untapped workforce full of potential who can help us accelerate the adoption of post-quantum cryptography and the quantum strategy overall. The United States is gaining increasing awareness that we need to do better and be thinking ahead about the dependencies we have in our supply chains, advanced R&D investments that are needed to continue advancing enabling technologies that are providing key components for quantum technologies, also growing our workforce to ensure that we can continue innovating at pace as these technologies come to fruition in the next 3 to 5 years. It's critical to get together the public and private sector: policymakers, standards developers, innovators, scientists, and the folks from the commercial world together to talk about the implications of these technologies, how we roll them out, and how we secure them. There's a lot of work, but it's going to be fun, and I'm excited to be a part of it. So thank you for having me.

title: Women in Leadership Conference 2026 Highlights: A Day of Inspiration ✨
transcription: We are at the Grove Hotel and Resort. It is absolutely phenomenal. I think it's our best Women in Leadership conference yet. It's the sixth annual conference. Every year we think it can't get any better, and every year we have amazing speakers, attendees, sponsors, and it just goes to show that community in Hertfordshire is becoming stronger. Days like today are important in- for many aspects, really. I think, first of all, it's about recognizing, celebrating how far women have come and I think it's sometimes really remember that we need to highlight that, but also just how strong women are together and how good we are at having that resilience and supporting and helping each other. And it does feel like a proper safe space, and an opportunity for everyone to grow, which I think is quite unique in the world at the moment. Leadership, particularly as a woman, is not always straightforward. As CEO, you carry the full picture, the commercial weight, the people decisions, the responsibility when things go right and also when they don't. This year's theme of Give to Gain feels incredibly relevant because when women give, something powerful happens. We don't diminish ourselves; we strengthen each other. Just think about what you could achieve now that we do have these amazing technologies and these amazing communities of women supporting us. My key takeaway from today is hearing about women's journeys, and to see from where they started and where they've got to, and I think it reminds us all what opportunities there are out there for us, and what a celebration today to hear these stories. Come on, girls, the world is our oyster. So, at Mad Science of Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, our mission is to inspire the next great British scientist. So, it feels kind of special to actually be acknowledged for everything that I do leading a team. I have 100 staff members, and, you know, dedicate my time to being a single mom and a business owner, and it's nice to be recognized for that. There's one message that I'd like to leave you with today, especially in a room full of amazing leaders and women: be yourself unapologetically, because that is enough, and then give to others. So, give opportunities, give trust, give feedback, and give support, and more importantly, give encouragement. Go out there, get your gold medal in whatever it may be in life.

title: 2026 NACo Annual Conference: Day 3 Recap
transcription: Day three of NACo's annual conference challenged county leaders to think bigger. The day was headlined by astronaut Colonel Chris Hadfield, who drew on his experiences commanding the International Space Station to share a simple but powerful message: prepare relentlessly, stay curious, and don't let uncertainty stand in the way of progress. Earlier, the general session celebrated the innovation already happening in counties across America, recognizing more than 1,800 achievement award-winning programs from over 140 counties and state associations. Proof that some of the country's most creative solutions are being developed at the local level. That spirit of innovation carried into the exhibit hall, where main stage presentations and common ground conversations connected county leaders with new technologies, fresh ideas, and peers tackling many of the same challenges back home. From celebrating what's working to exploring what's possible, day three was a reminder that the best ideas don't stay in one county, they spread. As the conference nears its end, the momentum continues, but the conversations and connections made here will last long after everyone heads home.
