title: Computer Science Pitch Competition Highlight Reel
transcription: The CompSci Pitch Comp is a completely new competition at UNSW. It's the first time undergraduate students get an opportunity to pitch to the UNSW Investment Committee for a real investment. It's usually a right that is reserved to to staff at UNSW or to post-graduate students in special circumstances, um but it's never been done before for undergraduate students. Classroom performance can only do so much when it comes to assessing the talent, the grit, and the creativity of our students. Before it was sort of assumed that like, you know, the students wouldn't have anything mature enough to to be able to fund or or the ideas would be too nascent or whatever. But what we've discovered is that, you know, um there are some great ideas and they're quite mature as well. So I'm really excited to to go a bit further on that. Every 11 minutes in Australia, someone suffers a stroke, which means by the time we wrap up the two next pitches tonight, someone's life will change completely. I I remember growing up and feeling like sort of powerless to the world and like the whims of how things were happening around me. But I'm very excited to be able to do something that I think can actually make an impact. It's actually one of our biggest milestones to just being able to pitch to investors and really learn from their opinions and be able to take this even further. This opportunity means a lot to us, because not only the money, right, but also where it's coming from, like, startups, yeah, UNSW Founders has dealt with thousands of startups that have faced the exact issues we are trying to mediate for people. The education system in Australia is changing. What are we doing for our students to ensure that they are the best so that they can graduate, get a job, or better yet, create their own job? I think it's saying to the world, "Yes, they're getting a world-class education here, but we're also wanting to prepare them for the real world by showing them that they actually are in charge of their own destiny."

title: The Perfect 60-Second Startup Pitch (Investors Will Remember)
transcription: The perfect 60-second startup pitch. Imagine you step into an elevator with your dream investor. You have exactly 60 seconds before the doors open. Would you know what to say? Most founders make one big mistake. They try to explain everything about their business. The truth is, your goal isn't to close the investment in 60 seconds. It's to make the investor want another conversation. Here's a simple framework that works. First, start with the problem. What pain are you solving? Keep it simple and relatable. If the investor doesn't understand the problem, they won't care about the solution. Next, explain your solution. In one sentence, describe what your company does. Avoid technical jargon or long explanations. If someone outside your industry can't understand it, it's probably too complicated. Then, explain why now. Why is this the right time for your business? Maybe a new technology has made your solution possible. Maybe customer behavior has changed. Maybe the market is growing rapidly. Investors want to know why this opportunity exists today, not 5 years ago. After that, share your traction. You don't need millions in revenue, but you do need evidence that you're making progress. That could be paying customers, user growth, partnerships, pilot programs, or even a growing waitlist. Traction reduces uncertainty and builds confidence. Finally, finish with the opportunity. Don't end by asking for money. Instead, leave the investor wanting to learn more. Give them a reason to schedule a second meeting. Remember, a great pitch doesn't answer every question. It answers just enough to create curiosity. If an investor walks away wanting to know more, you've done your job. The best founders don't overwhelm investors with information. They tell a clear story, communicate confidence, and make their business easy to understand. Because at the end of the day, investors don't invest in the longest pitch, they invest in the clearest one. title: The 5 Things Angel Investors Look for Before They Invest
transcription: How angel investors actually decide to invest. Imagine you've spent months, maybe even years, building your startup. You finally get a meeting with an angel investor. You walk in, deliver what you think is the perfect pitch, and they pass. So what happened? The truth is, angel investors aren't just investing in ideas. They're investing in founders. They're investing in execution. And most importantly, they're investing in the probability that your business can succeed. Here are the five things they're really looking for. First, the founder. This is by far the most important factor. Investors know that startups rarely go exactly according to plan. Markets change, products evolve, and unexpected problems come up all the time. They're asking themselves one simple question: Can this founder figure it out? A great founder is resilient, adaptable, and able to execute even when things don't go as planned. Second, the problem. Is it a real problem that people genuinely want solved? Or is it just a nice idea? The bigger and more painful the problem, the more valuable the solution becomes. Great businesses solve expensive problems, not minor inconveniences. Third, the market. Even an incredible product has limited potential if it's built for a tiny audience. Investors look for large growing markets because they want companies that can scale. If the opportunity isn't big enough, neither is the return. Fourth, traction. One of the biggest myths is that you need massive revenue before investors will take you seriously. That's simply not true. What investors really want is evidence that people care. That could be growing users, paying customers, partnerships, a waiting list, or strong engagement. Any sign that the market is responding positively reduces the risk of investing. And finally, why you? What's stopping another company from copying your idea tomorrow? Maybe it's your experience, maybe it's your technology, your network, your community, or simply your ability to execute faster than everyone else. The strongest startups don't just have a great idea. They have a compelling reason why they're the best team to bring that idea to life. At the end of the day, angel investing is all about reducing risk. Every customer you gain, every milestone you hit, and every problem you solve gives investors one more reason to believe. Because investors don't invest in certainty, they invest in confidence. title: Choosing the Wrong Person to Pitch Your Startup | Chinese Competition Reality
transcription: A lot of international entrepreneurs, they underestimate how important the applicant actually is for Chinese startup competitions. The applicant can make or break the deal. You can either succeed through this or you just fail. We had startups that applied twice to one competition, one year one applicant, the other year another applicant, and we figured out that it is extremely important who applies and the background of the applicant. Some startups, they choose to let an intern or a manager apply to the competition, but the problem here is that they do not have the relevant background to get through the entire process. What Chinese startup competitions usually want to see is the CEO or at least C-level applicants that have a substantial amount of equity in the startup. There are certain startup competitions, usually most of the competitions, they require at least 30% of equity in the startup. Not at this time, but usually in the process of the establishment of the startup, you should have had at one point 30% of equity. There are some competitions that do not require this. We usually highlight this in the process of supporting you to get through the startup competition, but these competitions are usually rare. And sometimes it's not really important that the CEO applies, because if your education background is not top-notch, so you don't have a master degree or a PhD, then maybe another person of your business should apply to the competition. Because usually the higher the the degree, the better the chances of getting through. So, if you have someone in your team that you can trust with the establishment of the entity in China, then you could choose a PhD manager in your company to apply to this competition. transcription: Hi, my name is Carl Gunther. I'm the founder of Seven Castle Cider. We are a beverage company from Western New York producing non-alcoholic sparkling apple cider made from our locally sourced upcycled apples that would otherwise be thrown out. Our flagship product is a modern 12 oz can made with just fresh apple juice and carbonation. No artificial additives, no added sugars, no preservatives, none of that nonsense. The non-alcoholic beverage industry is growing rapidly, but sparkling cider is being left out. Most options are seasonal, sold in large bottles, or made from concentrate. Seven Castle Cider reimagines cider as a year-round, everyday social beverage, something that belongs at dinners, weddings, celebrations, gatherings, parties, anything without alcohol being a barrier. Our mission is to create inclusive social spaces while also helping the environment and our local economy. Whether someone doesn't drink for health, faith, or personal reasons, they still deserve a drink to feel celebratory. We validated this demand through in-person tastings, parties, and over 200,000 organic social media views before launch. Operationally, we are ready to launch. We have our scheduled processes all complete. We have one last inspection for our 20-C commercial production license, and we have our sales tax authority for New York State. We are also in the talks with local co-packers so we can get our beverage produced at large scales through them. We have MSRP at 2.99 can, which gives us room for profits and growth. We are bootstrapped, we are value-driven, and we are built for sustainable growth, and we are not just a beverage. We are selling a more inclusive way for people to gather. title: Inside the VC Mindset: What Makes a Pitch Win
transcription: Hi everyone, this is Jaden Chow. Welcome to the Shark Tank PHS virtual club space. Today we're answering an important question. What is crucial if you want a VC to fund your business idea? First, what is a VC? VC stands for Venture Capitalist. A VC is someone who gives money to new businesses they believe can grow big. Instead of getting paid back like a loan, they receive part ownership of the business. If the business succeeds, they succeed, too. Because of that, VCs don't invest in just any idea. They invest in ideas that are clear, realistic, and ready to grow. That's where the winning pitch formula comes in. First is the problem. You must clearly explain a real pain point people actually have. Second, the solution. What is your product or service, and how does it work? Third, the value proposition. Why is your solution better or different from others? Fourth, the market. Who is this for, and how many people need it? Fifth, the business model. How does your idea make money? Next is traction. This is proof that people want your idea, like users, sales, or strong interest. Then comes competition. Other solutions exist. Explain who they are, and why your idea can win. Next are financials. You don't need perfect numbers, but you need to show you understand costs and revenue. Then there's the ask. How much money are you asking for, and what are you offering in return? Finally, vision and scale. Show how your idea can grow bigger in the future. If you can clearly explain all 10 of these, a VC is much more likely to listen. Thanks for watching. See you in the next lesson.

The speaker explains the concept of Venture Capitalists (VCs) and details the 'winning pitch formula' required to secure business funding. He systematically breaks down the pitch into ten key elements: identifying a clear problem, presenting a solution, defining the value proposition, identifying the market, explaining the business model, showing traction, acknowledging competition, outlining financials, making the ask, and demonstrating vision and scale. He concludes the lesson by thanking the audience and teasing the next session as the music swells slightly.

title: Why Didn't Robinhood Blame AI for Layoffs?
transcription: Why didn't Robinhood blame AI for layoffs? Robinhood is still cutting about 290 jobs, even as the company reports growth, and CEO Vlad Tenev left AI out of the memo entirely. That omission is the story, because plenty of tech companies now use AI as the reason for shrinking teams. The layoff note came from CEO Vlad Tenev, and he did something unusual for a tech chief right now. He made no mention of AI. That matters because Robinhood is not hiding behind a productivity story. The company is still shrinking its workforce while saying the business is growing, so the message is blunt. The cuts are about the company's structure, not a public AI excuse. That silence stands out because many tech companies have started using AI language in layoff announcements. Amazon, Block, Coinbase, GitLab, and Intuit have all used similar logic around leaner teams, less bureaucracy, and fewer silos. Robinhood chose not to join that script. Instead, the note pointed away from AI and toward a broader internal reset. That analyst view reinforces the point. According to Citizens JMP Securities analyst Devin Ryan, AI-driven efficiency was not the main driver of the reduction, because Robinhood has long been aggressively leveraging artificial intelligence across the organization. In other words, if AI was already part of the machine, it could not be the easy excuse for the cuts. The company's internal message had to point somewhere else. This is why the Robinhood memo is getting attention beyond one company. Tech firms are under pressure to justify layoffs at the same time AI tools are being sold as efficiency machines. Robinhood's choice suggests that the AI blame game may be losing credibility fast. If a company already uses AI broadly, saying AI caused the cuts starts to sound like a cover story, not an explanation. Robinhood cut 10% of its staff, about 290 jobs, but skipped the AI script that many peers now lean on. The real takeaway is simple. Companies are being pushed to explain restructuring more directly, especially when AI is already part of their operations.

title: States scramble to redistrict after Supreme Court limits Voting Rights Act
transcription:
Tonight, new political turmoil. Alabama and Tennessee are the latest states rushing to redraw congressional districts after a Supreme Court ruling that further weakened voting rights. CBS News Congressional Correspondent Nicole Killion has the latest. Nicole.

Six months out from the midterms and the redistricting wars are intensifying for control of Congress after a recent Supreme Court ruling rolled back a key part of the Voting Rights Act. The Supreme Court's 6-to-3 decision to strike down Louisiana's congressional map hits right in the heart of Cleo Fields' seat. The district was created, first of all, Louisiana's minority population, black population, is over a third of the state. The Democrat represents the sixth congressional district, which slinks from Shreveport to Baton Rouge. But the high court ruled the newly drawn majority-minority district was an unconstitutional gerrymander since it was based on race. Congressman Troy Carter represents the other majority-minority district in New Orleans. It can wipe out both of our seats. We can, realistically, end up having six congressional districts with no African-American or Democratic representation. Ahead of early voting this weekend, Louisiana officials suspended House primary elections slated for November until the state can redraw its map. I don't think that it's going to result in a loss of minority representation, and I think that we have to give the—the people a chance to draw their districts the way the people want to see them drawn. Before the Supreme Court ruling, at least seven states had already passed new congressional maps as part of mid-decade redistricting. Now, several Southern states are using the High Court's decision to justify changes before the midterms, including Florida, Alabama, and Tennessee. It was really not about, you know, that little seat in Louisiana. It's about redistricting all over the nation. It's about the voting rights of people all over the nation. While these new moves by Southern states could potentially net more Republican seats, Democrats are vowing to fight back and are looking to other blue states that could possibly change their maps in the 2028 cycle. Jericka. Nicole Killion, thank you so much.

title: Supreme Court appears skeptical of mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day
transcription: The Supreme Court just finished hearing arguments in a major case that raises questions about the legality of mail-in voting. And the conservative justices appeared skeptical about allowing states to count ballots that are mailed on time, but arrive after Election Day. The court's ruling could upend the voting process in more than a dozen states just months before this November's midterm elections. NBC News legal affairs reporter Gary Grumbach joins us now. So, Gary, this case stems from an election law in Mississippi, so walk us through it and what we've heard so far from the justices. Yeah, the oral arguments were supposed to be about whether postmarked ballots by Election Day could be accepted after Election Day, but it really turned into a debate on a variety of different election-related topics, from who is actually delivering that ballot to the state, topics about like ballot harvesting, to conversations about potentially people being able to recall their votes. For example, if you were to send something in via FedEx, could you tell FedEx, "Oh no, I actually want that back"? And then there was conversations about the length of time the state allows a voter to be able to get their ballot in and have it count. So, for example, some states do a week, some states do 21 days. Conservative Justice Samuel Alito, predictably, was pretty upset about all of this. He said, "We used to have Election Day, now it's election month or election months," guys. Gary, if the Supreme Court does rule in favor of the RNC and Mississippi's GOP, what does that essentially mean more broadly for the rest of the country when it comes to these midterms? So, Mississippi was the state that was arguing this and defending their own law, but there's 13 other states that have similar laws, so this would be a very significant thing for almost half the country here in terms of whether or not ballots would be allowed to be counted after Election Day. You have a map there that shows states, both red and blue states, that we're looking at there. And it also specifically relates to some of these military ballots, right? Folks that are serving overseas in our military, especially right now, uh may not be able to get their ballots in on time even though they are postmarked by Election Day. We will have to see exactly how the justices write this opinion, which we should be getting it by the end of June. We thank you for watching, and remember, stay updated on breaking news and top stories on the NBC News app or watch live on our YouTube channel.

title: Supreme Court weakens the Voting Rights Act after 61 years
transcription: The US Supreme Court dealt a blow to the landmark Voting Rights Act on Wednesday after knocking out a major pillar of the law that had protected against racial discrimination in voting and representation. In the six decades since it was signed, the Voting Rights Act became one of the most consequential laws in the nation's history, preventing discrimination against minorities at the ballot box. It also helped elect Black and Hispanic representatives at all levels of government. But on Wednesday, the Supreme Court hollowed out the landmark civil rights era law by striking down a majority Black congressional district in Louisiana. That ruling could provide an open door for political mapmakers to undermine minority representation. The Voting Rights Act was signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson on August 6, 1965, five months after the Bloody Sunday attack on civil rights marchers in Selma, Alabama, gave momentum to the bill. Wherever there is discrimination, this law will strike down all restrictions used to deny the people the right to vote. In recent years, AP reporter Gary Fields sat down with some of the people who were pivotal to the birth of the Act. After having talked to these individuals and to a number of other people about why voting rights was so important, the reason for why they were so important then hasn't changed now. In a democracy or a republic such as ourselves, the vote is the thing that you have that is the coin of the realm that allows you to say I'm a full participant in this society, in this endeavor that we call the United States of America. The question now is what comes next for minority representatives and the communities they represent.

Afterward, a male speaker with an American accent elaborates on why voting rights are so crucial, explaining that the vote is a powerful tool that allows individuals to feel like full participants in society. Finally, the female speaker returns to conclude the video by raising a question about what lies ahead for minority representation.

title: Supreme Court Steps In After Judge Orders Trump Arrested Live—Emergency Appeal Changes Everything.
transcription:
The sealed 94-page leak: What nobody is connecting yet.

A sealed 94-page federal grand jury transcript leaked Tuesday night, and the legal fallout is already escalating. Federal grand jury testimony is classified as secret under Rule 6 of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure, meaning this document was never supposed to exist in the public domain. Yet, at 11:47 p.m. on Tuesday, the full unredacted transcript hit ProPublica's servers. Someone on the inside broke protocol to leak it, which is a federal felony in itself. However, the true significance lies within the contents of the testimony, specifically, brand new sworn statements provided by former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson during an undisclosed session in January 2026. Unlike her previous public appearances, this fourth session under oath involved different prosecutors, different targets, and crucial documentary evidence. On page 12 of the transcript, when asked if she maintained personal knowledge of White House communications, Hutchinson revealed that she kept a personal record comprising text message screenshots, calendar entries, and three handwritten journals. Because these were maintained as personal records, rather than official government property, they fall outside standard executive privilege claims and cannot be shielded as easily. Hutchinson essentially created her own paper trail, which has now become central to the prosecution's case. The transcript lays out a detailed timeline of post-election strategy. Page 18 introduces Exhibit 47, a November 9, 2024, text message from Mark Meadows instructing Hutchinson to establish a direct line with former DOJ official Jeffrey Clark and then Michigan Senate Majority Leader Mike Shirkey. Page 23 details a November 11th conference call arranged by Hutchinson featuring Donald Trump, Mark Meadows, Jeffrey Clark, Mike Shirkey, Rudy Giuliani, an Arizona State Senator, and Hutchinson herself. According to her testimony, the explicit topic of the call was developing strategies to delay election certification in Michigan and Arizona, focusing directly on disrupting the certification process, rather than pursuing standard court challenges.

title: FBI Investigates Deaths and Disappearances of 10 US Scientists
transcription: This morning, members of Congress are set to take on a deepening mystery after at least 10 American scientists, all with ties to US nuclear or space research programs, have died or disappeared. Does appear that there's a, a high possibility that something sinister is taking place here. On Monday, the House Oversight Committee saying it will investigate the string of incidents, writing, "If the reports are accurate, these deaths and disappearances may represent a grave threat to US national security." It comes just days after the FBI launched its own probe. The agency telling NBC News it is working with the Department of Energy, Department of Defense, and state and local law enforcement to find answers. President Trump even said he was briefed on the matter last week. I hope it's random, but we're going to know in the next week and a half. The mysterious deaths and disappearances began in 2023, when Michael David Hicks, a scientist who worked with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, died at the age of 59 with no cause of death publicly released. Between 2024 and 2025, seven other scientists were reportedly killed or went missing, including 60-year-old NASA engineer Monica Reza, who vanished while on a hike near Los Angeles. And earlier this year, my husband is missing. William Neil McCasland, a 68-year-old retired Air Force general, disappeared after authorities say he left his Albuquerque home on foot. The wave of deaths and disappearances sparking a slew of suspicion and conspiracy theories online. This is not just a coincidence, this is absolutely a pattern. Now, the cases are getting even more attention as federal investigators and lawmakers look for a potential link. And it's unclear how long the investigation could take to complete, though a senior FBI official says it will likely take longer than the week and a half the president had suggested. Craig? Ryan Nobles for us there in Washington. Ryan, thank you. Hey, thanks for watching. And don't forget, you can catch The Today Show every morning on NBC, or take Today when you're on the go. Just follow The Today Podcast on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you listen.

title: How Indie Creators Are Building Shows With Shorts
transcription: Vertical short-form animation used to feel to me like this weird side quest. Like something you did for the algorithm, but not for your actual career. But lately, I've been seeing indie animators use shorts to quietly build entire worlds. Characters, shows, fan bases, momentum. So today, I want to break down the storytelling formats that are actually working and how you can use them for your own projects. Because here's the truth: most of us don't get to make a full series right away. We don't get handed a season order and a budget and a team. We build things slowly. And shorts are how a lot of creators are doing that right now. They help you test ideas, grow an audience, prove there's really something there. They're not throwaway content. They're like micro-pilots, proof of concepts. I've been doing this storytelling thing for a while now, in studios and independently. And the creators who are really winning in short form aren't just posting random clips. They're actually telling tiny, strategic stories. Hi, I'm Emily Brundige, and I create cartoons for a living. Over the past decade, I've pitched and sold eight original animated shows. Most recently, I created my own original animated show, Goldie, for Apple TV. It's been nominated for two Emmys, including Best Writing. When I look at the shorts that turn into long-term fandoms, I see the same three storytelling models that really work. They seem simple, but structurally, they're doing something very smart. Let's start with the most classic storytelling format. Self-contained stories. Mummy Joe is a great example of this. Every short is its own tiny episode: beginning, middle, and end. Nothing carries over, so you can click on any one, and you're not lost, you're just in. Why does this work? You don't need context, you don't need lore. You just click and you're watching a whole story. You feel satisfied.

title: Audio Files: Lessons NOT YET Learned
transcription: The Tech on Demand podcast brought to you by GrowerTalks. Audio Files Episode 76. Lessons Not Yet Learned. From the February 2026 issue of Green Profit magazine, written by Bill McCurry, narrated by Bill Calkins. Lessons Not Yet Learned. Philip quadrupled his dad's operations during his 23-year term as CEO. He invested in new operations, dramatically improving results. At 46, Philip died unexpectedly. Alex, his 20-year-old son, assumed control of the organization. Not everyone felt this was the right choice. Alex dismissed those who wouldn't get on board. He wisely continued the investments in new technology, results in even greater success than his father had achieved. By the time of Alex's unforeseen death at 33, the organization was 10 times the size it had been at his father's death. 5 years later, that organization had deteriorated to substantially smaller than when Philip ran it. Alex was toasted and written about as one of the greatest leaders in history. He was probably the first PR-based autocratic personality with no true leadership beyond misleading publicity and fear. Beginning in 343 BC, Aristotle tutored Alex for 3 years. Today we call him Alexander the Great. Based on the outcomes for his organization, team, and citizens, he should be called Alexander the Goof. At his deathbed, generals asked Alexander, "Who shall lead us?" Alexander replied, "Whoever is the strongest." The reality is Alexander would leave behind only fighters and no trained leaders. None of the generals were taught anything but rampaging, knocking heads, and killing. They had no understanding of negotiation, compromise, or leadership. The generals fought each other for elevation to Alexander's position. As a result, that era's Greek empire withered away in civil wars, rebellions, disintegration, and loss of power and influence. Alexander didn't expect to die young and didn't plan or train for succession. His leadership style was complete control. He neither trained his possible successors nor shared any information with them. His iron-handed rule gave no thought for the future.

title: How to Use Google NotebookLM (Full Tutorial)
transcription: In this video, I will show you how to use Google's NotebookLM step-by-step. NotebookLM helps you turn PDFs, notes, websites, and videos into an AI-powered research assistant. It can summarize your content, answer questions, generate mind maps, and even create AI-generated podcasts based on your sources. I'm Kevin, and I'll show you everything you need to know to get started. Let's dive in. First, head to the NotebookLM website. You'll find a link right here at the bottom of the screen. For this tutorial, make sure you're signed in with your Google account. Once you're in NotebookLM, click on Create New in the top right. This drops us into a new notebook. Think of a notebook like a workspace for a specific project or topic. For example, you might create one for meeting notes, research, studying, or in my case, a new product launch. At the very top, give your notebook a name. We're launching a new cookie for my small business, the Kevin Cookie Company. So for this, I will call it the Galactic Marshmallow Explosion Launch. Now, between you and me, I think the marketing team got maybe just a little bit carried away with the naming. Next, let's add some sources. If you don't see this pane, you can click on this icon to toggle it on or off. These are the documents, websites, notes, and videos that NotebookLM uses to understand your content and answer questions about your sources. Right here, let's click on Add Sources. This opens an overlay where we can start adding sources. Now, first, I will drag and drop in a PDF document with our launch plans. And there, we now have our very first source. Let's add another one. Right up here, let's click on this again. Next, I'll add some meeting notes from Google Drive. Over here, I'll click on Drive, and there are those meeting notes. I'll select this, and then click on insert. Let's add a few more. Right up here, let's click on Add Sources. And this time, I'm going to add a website. And let's also add a YouTube video. And here, I'll click on insert. I now have four different sources in this notebook. Let's also try searching the web for additional sources. I'll click here. And let's try searching for dessert trends 2026. And over here, let's run that. It looks like NotebookLM found a number of different sources. Now, let's preview them before importing. I'll click on view. This shows me a full list of all the different sources that it found. I can click on this icon to preview the source. Now, I think this one looks good. So, I'll jump back to NotebookLM and let me uncheck all the sources and just select this one that was relevant. Down below, I can now click on import. And there on the left-hand side, it added that source. If you want to look at any source in...

transcription: Thank you for taking the time to listen to this brief video. I'm Tom Perone from New England Consulting Group, president and founder. We work with business owners with 5 to 50 employees for the purpose of financial clarity, creating financial clarity for them to plan their estates, their business growth, and economic wealth for the future. And in this short little video, I'm going to explain a little bit more about what we do and how we do it. The three major things that we do in our planning to help business owners get financial clarity is to help them avoid paying any more taxes than they already are. We help them protect against the erosions of their estate and their wealth through taxation, probate, over, uh, overtaxation, not utilizing some of the tax code, especially under the new big beautiful bill, where there's so many opportunities for business owners to create more wealth and pay less taxes, uh, at this point. And if you've done any planning before January of 2026, we should have a discussion because it's probably out of date. And the third thing we do is we prevent businesses from having what I call a transition failure. You know, only about 10% of the businesses actually sell, and only about 16% of business owners have a succession transition plan. So, this is where your wealth is, and this is where we want to help you the most. So, there's three threats to business owners, as I have mentioned: owners paying more taxes, erosion of their wealth, and the transition of their business being a failure. So, this is where we spend most of our time, and our systems are set up to touch each one of these areas, and obviously, more depth. We developed the GWT system years ago, we use it today. It's a very good system because it's, there's got brevity to it, it's a three-step system

title: Scientists studied doomscrolling. Here’s what they found.
transcription:
What does the science actually say about whether social media is ruining our attention spans? Personally, I'm finding it a lot harder these days to sit down and read a book or watch a movie without scrolling on my phone, and it's those short vertical videos that feel particularly addicting. So, how much of that is my ability to focus actually getting worse versus me just worrying about losing my attention span? All of these fears are fairly new, so there's not a ton of high-quality studies that have been done, but there are a few. And recently, the science YouTuber, Joss Fong, posted a really great explanation on her channel, How To, where she dove into what the existing science can tell us about whether that brain rot is real, or if it's all just in our fearful heads.

In this conversation about attention spans, there's a phrase that I keep hearing, which is "brain rot". What do we actually mean by that phrase "brain rot"? What are we actually thinking is happening to ourselves and what is happening to ourselves?

I think what people mostly mean when they talk about brain rot is a kind of low-quality internet content on mostly algorithmic social media feeds, probably primarily these short-form video feeds, but also things like on Reddit or Twitter. I think people imply a low quality, but also they're implying a certain effect that they have on, that this is having on our minds.

So it's the content and the impact of the content.

I think so, yeah. And, and for me the question has been, if I'm spending more and more of my life consuming this kind, this kind of media, is that having an impact on my brain? And I think what we hear from a lot of people is, "I used to be able to read books and now I can't. I used to be able to watch movies, um, and now I can't." And so the implication with brain rot is that it's not just our environment changing and the fact that we have this device that's constantly distracting us, but there's actually a change happening in our brains. And that was the question that I really wanted to chase down, is whether that's actually true.

So, you went digging into an enormous amount of research, and I love what you found, because there are actually people who have done scientific studies, rather than just us thinking this is our perception, they've actually gone through and they've kind of measured what is happening. Um

title: World's First Car | Who invented the Car? | History of the Automobile Invention | Dr. Binocs Show
transcription: Oh, are you enjoying the race, little kitty? Absolutely, it's amazing. Salute to the person who invented the first car. Well, not exactly. The car wasn't invented by just one person. It was actually the result of a long, competitive race between inventors, all trying to build the future. Let's travel back in time and explore the story behind one big question: who invented the car? Zoom in! The story starts in 1769 with a French engineer named Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot, who built what is widely considered the first self-propelled vehicle. It was a steam-powered machine designed to haul cannons for the French army. It worked... sort of. It was slow, heavy, and even crashed into a wall during a demonstration. Still, it proved something revolutionary: vehicles didn't need horses to move. This idea sparked a technological race, as inventors across Europe experimented with steam, electricity, and eventually, gasoline. The real breakthrough came later in the 19th century with the development of the internal combustion engine, an engine that burns fuel like gasoline to create motion. This changed everything. Instead of bulky steam engines, vehicles could now be smaller, faster, and more efficient. That's when Carl Benz, a German engineer, entered the race. In 1885...

He explains that the invention of the car was a collective effort rather than the work of a single person, taking the listener on a historical journey. He details the creation of the first self-propelled, steam-powered vehicle by French engineer Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot in 1769, describing its limitations and revolutionary impact. The narrative then shifts to the development of the internal combustion engine in the 19th century and introduces German engineer Karl Benz in 1885. title: Cessna Crash Layton Utah, Southwest Flight 512 Honolulu Diversion, Beijing Tower Crash Deliberate
transcription: Welcome to Aviator DB News Briefing. Today is Sunday, August 2nd, 2026. Here are today's top stories. Layton, Utah plane crash, two hospitalized after Cessna flips on SR-193. Southwest flight medical emergency diverts flight 512 back to Honolulu. FAA launches science-based marijuana fitness review for pilots, controllers. Beijing tower crash was deliberate, Chinese authorities confirm. Now for the details. Two people were hospitalized in stable condition after a small plane crash landed and flipped on State Route 193 near Fort Lane in Layton, Utah, late July 31st, 2026. The incident occurred shortly before midnight adjacent to Hill Air Force Base, KHIF, according to reports from KUTV and KSL. Emergency responders from the Layton Fire Department said the aircraft, identified as a Cessna 172, lost altitude rapidly before the engine cut out, then landed on the highway and flipped inverted. Both the pilot and passenger self-extricated from the wreckage before being transported to a local hospital. Crews contained a fuel spill at the scene, and no post-crash fire occurred. Layton police said the aircraft likely departed from Ogden and may have been attempting to land at Hill Air Force Base when the accident happened. Authorities told Univision that wind may have been a contributing factor, though the precise cause remains undetermined. The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board, NTSB, have been notified and are leading the investigation. This incident follows a series of recent general aviation accidents in Utah, including a fatal Cessna 172S crash in Box Elder County and an emergency landing near Smithfield. The NTSB typically releases preliminary findings within two weeks. Final reports can take significantly longer. A passenger medical emergency forced Southwest Flight 512 to return to Honolulu on Tuesday night after departing for San Diego. The aircraft had left Hawaii around 9:00 p.m. when crew declared an emergency following an undisclosed medical issue aboard.

title: History Buffs: The Odyssey Impressions
transcription: Hey, history buffs, it's Nick Hodges here. Now, I know my niche is reviewing historical movies and TV shows, but today, I'm going to make an exception. I just got back from Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, arguably the most talked about movie of 2026. People were already divided on it before they'd even seen it. Well, now I have, and I'm going to answer the question everyone's asking: Is this a movie you're going to like? Well, that depends. How much do you care about Greek mythology, or more specifically, how much do you care about Homer's Odyssey? Do you expect this movie to follow that story beat for beat, and if it doesn't, how much is that going to bother you? Because if all you care about are the monsters, I can tell you right now you're getting the Cyclops, the Laestrygonians, the witch Circe, the Sirens, Scylla, and Charybdis. They're all there. Strangely, though, there are almost no gods. Okay, we're probably entering spoiler territory here, but if you don't mind minor spoilers, Odysseus never speaks to Hermes, Aeolus, or Poseidon. The only god he ever interacts with is Athena, and even she is presented more like a hallucination than an actual goddess. Which doesn't really make much sense to me because there's definitely magic in this movie. Circe genuinely turns Odysseus's men into pigs. Calypso's in the movie too, but she isn't a goddess. She's just a mortal woman who rescues Odysseus and feeds him lotus leaves. There's no temptation of immortality like there is in the original story. If you're wondering how Christopher Nolan handles the gods, the answer is he mostly doesn't. Poseidon never appears. The closest the film gets is, after the Cyclops is blinded, he cries out to Poseidon, and Odysseus's crew conclude that the Cyclops must be his son. That's about as explicit as it gets. And yet, a little later, Odysseus literally travels to Hades and speaks to the dead. Tiresias is there, his fallen comrades from Troy are there, so the afterlife is definitely real. But the Olympian gods? Apparently, that's where Christopher Nolan draws the line. Now, what are the monsters like in the movie? Well, to be honest, the Cyclops is really disappointing. He never talks to Odysseus and his men, he just walks into the cave, seals the entrance, eats a few of Odysseus's men, and then goes straight to sleep, not considering these tiny humans a threat at all. In the original story, it's much more interesting. Odysseus actually talks to the Cyclops, he gets him drunk on wine, and then blinds him while he's asleep. By cutting all of that out, Nolan's Cyclops just comes across as an idiot. I

He notes that while various monsters like the Cyclops, Circe, and Scylla are included, the film largely excludes the active participation of the Olympian gods, presenting Athena more as a hallucination. He contrasts the film's portrayal of Calypso as a mortal and points out the simplified, less interactive depiction of the Cyclops, which he finds disappointing compared to the original text. transcription: ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിലേക്ക് വരുന്നതിൽ ബാഴ്സലോണ പേടിക്കണം എന്ന് പറയുന്നവരുണ്ടല്ലോ. ശരിക്കും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ വരുന്ന ഈ വർഷം, അതായത് 2023 മുതൽ നോക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഒരു ചരിത്രത്തിനെയൊക്കെ അടിസ്ഥാനപ്പെടുത്തിയാണ് നമ്മൾ സംസാരിക്കാൻ പോകുന്നത്. ആദ്യമേ പേടിക്കണോ എന്ന് ചോദിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ നമ്മൾ ഹിസ്റ്ററിയെ ബേസ് ചെയ്തിട്ടുള്ള ഒരു കാര്യമാണ് പറയാനായിട്ട് പോകുന്നത്. ഇതിങ്ങനെയൊക്കെ തന്നെ സംഭവിക്കണം എന്ന് നിർബന്ധമൊന്നുമില്ലെങ്കിലും പലപ്പോഴും ഫുട്ബോളിൽ ഈ ചരിത്രമാവർത്തിക്കുകയാണല്ലോ എന്ന് പറയുന്ന പോലെ ഒരു സംഭവത്തെക്കുറിച്ചാണ് നമ്മൾ പറയാൻ പോകുന്നത്. ബാഴ്സലോണ ശരിക്കും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ പേടിക്കണോ? ഇതാണ് ടോപ്പിക്. അപ്പൊ എന്തായാലും നമ്മൾ വിഷയം വിഷയമായിട്ട് സംസാരിക്കുന്നതിനു മുൻപായിട്ട്, നിങ്ങൾക്ക് നമ്മുടെ കാര്യപരിപാടികൾ യൂട്യൂബിൽ ഇഷ്ടപ്പെടുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ എന്തായാലും യൂട്യൂബിൽ ഒന്ന് സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്തു കൂടെ കൂടുക. നമ്മളങ്ങനെ 9000 സബ്സ്ക്രൈബേഴ്സ് ആയിരിക്കുകയാണ്. ഇനി 10 കെ യിലേക്ക് അടുത്തോണ്ടിരിക്കുകയാണ്. സോ നിങ്ങൾ ഫോളോ ചെയ്യുകയാണ്, സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്യുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അത് പെട്ടെന്നാവും എന്ന് ഓർമ്മിപ്പിച്ചുകൊണ്ട്, വെൽക്കം ടു 80 പോഡ്കാസ്റ്റ് ഫുട്ബോൾ ക്ലബ്ബ് ആൻഡ് ദിസ് ഈസ് ആർ ജെ ആറ്റപ്പൻ. ആദ്യം തന്നെ പറയാനുള്ള ഒരു കാര്യം എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് 2010 ൽ സ്പെയിൻ വേൾഡ് കപ്പ് അടിക്കുന്ന ഒരു സമയമുണ്ട്. അതുകഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ നേരെ അടുത്ത സീസൺ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിലേക്ക്, അതായത് ആ അടിച്ച വർഷത്തെ സീസൺ തുടങ്ങുന്നത് ഈ പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയോടൊപ്പമാണ്. അതായത് 2010 മുതൽ 2013 വരെക്കുമാണ് ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ ദി സ്പെഷ്യൽ വൺ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിൻ്റെ ഹെഡ് കോച്ച് ആയിട്ട് വന്നിട്ടുള്ളത്. ആൻഡ് ഇതിൻ്റെ ഇടയിൽ തന്നെ നമ്മൾ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ കുറിച്ച് എപ്പോഴും പറയുമ്പോഴും ഈ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിൻ്റെ ഈയൊരു ചെറിയ സമയം എന്ന് വേണമെങ്കിൽ പറയാം, അല്ലെ? ഒരു മൂന്ന് വർഷം. അല്ലെങ്കിൽ നാല് വർഷം എന്ന്, നാല് വർഷം കൺസിഡർ ചെയ്യാൻ പറ്റില്ല പക്ഷേ എന്നാലും അങ്ങനെ. മൂന്ന് സീസൺസ്. ഈ മൂന്ന് സീസൺ കൊണ്ട് എങ്ങനെയാണ് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ ഈ പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ മാറ്റിയതെന്ന് വച്ച് കഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ അത് ട്രോഫികളുടെ നമ്പർ വെച്ചിട്ടോ, വിന്നിങ് പെർസെൻ്റേജ് വെച്ചിട്ടോ, എൽ ക്ലാസിക്കോയിൽ അടിച്ചിട്ടുള്ള ജയങ്ങൾ വെച്ചിട്ടോ ഒന്നുമല്ല. പകരം ഹി വാസ് ബിൽഡിങ്. നമ്മുടെ ടോണി സ്റ്റാർക്ക് അയൺമാനിലൊക്കെ പറയുന്ന ഒരു സാധനമില്ലേ, ഐ ആം ദി മെക്കാനിക് എന്ന് പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ഹി വാസ് ദി മാൻ ഹു ഡിസൈൻഡ് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡ് എന്ന് വേണമെങ്കിൽ പറയാം. അതായത് രമണാ, എങ്ങനെയാ പറയാന്ന് വച്ചുകഴിഞ്ഞാൽ ആ ഒരു മൂന്ന് സീസൺ കൊണ്ട് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ ശരിയായ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡ് ആയിട്ട് മാറ്റാൻ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയ്ക്ക് സാധിച്ചു എന്നുള്ളതാണ് ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ സംബന്ധിച്ചിടത്തോളവും റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ സംബന്ധിച്ചിടത്തോളവും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയുടെ സമയം പുള്ളിയുടെ പേര് വെച്ചുതന്നെ നമ്മൾ പറയുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഒരു സ്പെഷ്യൽ വൺ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഒരു സ്പെഷ്യൽ സീസൺ ആയി മാറുന്നത് എന്നുള്ളതാണ്. അത് എന്തുകൊണ്ടാണ് എന്ന് ചോദിക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ, ഞാൻ ആ പറഞ്ഞ സമയം കൊണ്ട് തന്നെ പറഞ്ഞു വരികയാണ്. സ്പെയിൻ വേൾഡ് കപ്പ് അടിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് ബാഴ്സലോണയുടെ കാര്യമെടുത്ത് നോക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ പിന്നെ അങ്ങോട്ട് ബാഴ്സലോണ യൂറോപ്പ് ഭരിച്ചിരുന്ന സമയമാണ്. എന്ന്

Poor guy is lonely. He is out there to make friends, दोस्त बनाने निकला है वो। अब... अगर रास्ते में कहीं थोड़ा बहुत तेल मिल रहा है... उसमें प्रॉब्लम क्या है? पर दोस्ती में कोई कॉम्प्रोमाइज नहीं देखो, बिल्कुल कोई, कोई फॉर्मेलिटी नहीं करता दोस्ती में। वेनेजुएला का प्रेसिडेंट बताओ निकर-ट्रैकसूट में उठा लाया है। ये रहे यार यहाँ आके। दिल का कितना साफ़ है। कितना जो दिल में है, ज़ुबां पे है। बीच में माइंड का कोई रोल ही नहीं है। आप देखो, अरे! यार नहीं, हेलो, एक सेकंड। माइंड का क्यूँ हो रोल भी, दिल... माइंड तो बाहर है। उसकी पीआर टीम... मर गई कह-कह के। कि नहीं-नहीं, वेनेजुएला वॉज़ इन अ स्टेट ऑफ़ अनरेस्ट, उनकी गवर्नमेंट उनके लिए काम नहीं कर रही थी, डिस्टर्ब स्टेट थी, इसलिए हमको इंटरवीन करना पड़ा। कह रहा है चुप हो जाओ बिल्कुल, झूठ नहीं बोलो अब तुम। भैया, मैं बताता हूँ, इनको नहीं पता। हम उनको वेनेजुएला तेल के लिए जाना था। हमारे हेयर फ़ॉल हो रहा है, रिसीड हो रही। सीधी बात करना है, बिल्कुल कुछ छल-कपट, छलावा कुछ है ही नहीं उस आदमी के पास। आधी बात बताता है। पूरी नहीं बताता। कि, "You have to figure the fuck out."

transcription: एक तो ये बाली की जो डिस्कनेक्टिंग फ्लाइट थी यार, SpiceJet... किया है अपनी सुरक्षा में ट्रैवल? आपको पता है आजकल, आजकल पायलट इसको चालू कैसे कर रहा है? मैं चढ़ी हूँ उस फ्लाइट में पहली बार मेरे साथ ऐसा हुआ है कि मेरे अराउंड पांच बुड्ढे बैठे हैं, ठीक है, फार्टिंग नॉनस्टॉप। बिना पासपोर्ट के जर्मनी गई हूँ मैं क्योंकि जो गैस चैम्बर बना दिया था, पायलट अनाउंसमेंट कर रहा है, "Currently we are facing some turbulence from the inside of the aircraft. अरे, राजेश जी, रुक जाइए।" एयर होस्टेस इन बुड्ढों को इंस्ट्रक्शंस दे रही है कि "ये इमरजेंसी एग्जिट है, इसको खुला ही रखेंगे।" वो सेफ्टी के लिए सीट बेल्ट लगा रहे हैं... कह रही है, "आप हमारी सेफ्टी के लिए मत लगाइए। सर, उसपे और प्रेशर मत डालिए।" पता है, इन बुड्ढों ने एकदम फार्टिंग का रिले रेस बना लिया था। एक का ख़तम हो रहा था, दूसरा बोलता है, "I'll take it from here." मैं आपको कैसे समझाऊँ, गाइज़, इस फ्लाइट में अगर अल-कायदा भी होता, वो भी अपने हाथ खड़े कर लेता यार और फिर नाक पे डालता। वो भी अपने सुपरवाइजर को कॉल कर रहा है, "हाईजैक करने आये थे, हॉस्टेज बनके रह गए हैं। सौ-दो सौ ज़्यादा ले ले, लैंड करा दे भाई, जान..." पता है, आप देखोगे, आपके अराउंड जब भी बुड्ढे बैठे हैं ना, तो आपको कभी कोई ज़रुरत ही नहीं पड़ेगी उनसे कुछ पूछने की। वो खुद ही अपना चिट्ठा आपको बताने लगते हैं। ऐसे कह रहे हैं, "बेटा, हम तो एयर फोर्स में काम किया करते थे।" अंकल, आप एयर फोर्स हैं। काम तो आप ज़बरदस्त कर रहे हो यार। अचानक से एक अंकल की तबियत बहुत ख़राब हो गई पीछे। ऐसा लग रहा है उनको हार्ट अटैक जैसा कुछ आ रहा है। तो पायलट कह रही है, "Any doctors? Any doctors, please come help." Next thing we heard, guys, was the absolutely worst thing we could have heard.

transcription: मैं तो CBSE में पढ़ा हूँ right तो CBSE में 6th class में algebra हमारा introduce हुआ है तो हमारी class teacher maths पढाती थी वह अपना लगी हुई है। बच्चों से लेकर teacher तक किसी को X नहीं मिल रहा है। अपना लगी हुई है। तो मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा है मेरे को ऐसा लग रहा है कि जब X मिल जाएगा बता देगी यह। तो मैं अपना अपने दोस्त से बात करनी शुरू, मैंने अब मैं बात करनी शुरू करी ही है, मैंने तो hello का 'है' बोला, 'है'। मेरे यहाँ आकर चौक बजा चौक। रविंद्र जडेजा ने मुझे खड़ा किया। मुझे मुझे मुझे मैडम ने खड़ा किया। मुझे खड़ा करके कहती, कहती, 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो?' मैने कहा 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो' का क्या मतलब है? बात इसलिए कर रहे हैं क्योंकि man is a social animal. बिना बात किए उससे रहा नहीं जाता, societal construct है यह। यह अभी तो पढ़ाया मैडम moral science में। मैम however obviously in absolutely no mood for any sort of explanation, मैडम ने मुझे 5 मिनट पूरी class के सामने अच्छे से झाड़ा है जो है। और 5 मिनट डांटने के बाद मुझसे कह रही, 'You have wasted 5 minutes. There are 60 students in the class. You have in total wasted 300 minutes.' मैने कहा 'मैम, मैम, time has been wasted in parallel. Not in series. मैम, you have disturbed 60 students. I was at max going to disturb one. That too for 5 seconds only. ओए टिफिन बचा है? नहीं बचा, ओहो that's it.' तो मैम, maths भी ख़राब है, logic भी ख़राब है आपका। और moral science के तो हाल हम देख ही लिए हैं। Zero civic sense. I believe that the Indian schooling system is horrible. या तो गलत पढ़ा रहे हैं या unnecessary पढ़ा रहे हैं। English हमें गलत पढ़ाई हुई। अंग्रेजी मुहावरे आधे अधूरे पढ़ा के छोड़ रखे हैं। I recently got to know that 'Jack of all master of none' is an incomplete proverb.

I think it's a matter of getting used to it. If I see two guys kissing, I'm in defense mode, I'm ready to rumble. You ask for your social distance. No, I'm going to close the gap between social distance with a job and then a hook. They also believe that Jesus is black and you guys can get into that, but I actually was going to say that I have some evidence that he wasn't. What's your evidence? A picture? Well, if he was black, then he would have turned the water into Henny. Is that not true? Who do you prefer as an actor? Christian Bale or Carlos Gonzalez de la peta con ganso son seck and felta fezablanzo? I can't say I know the second one. Oh, really? He's one of the biggest Mexican people. Wow. He's a huge Mexican guy. Are you trying to argue on marry a 12 year old? No, I don't want to marry anybody right now, I'm focused solely on business, I just see people getting shit online, like, why did you talk to that 12 year old woman? It's like, well, I don't know, why did they? They're a woman? Yeah, that's a bad look for me, let's move on. Do you think public schools should implement AI-driven robots to sit in the back of the class and scream to replace retarded kids once they are removed by Eugenics? No. Why? Do people ever confuse you with VanossGaming since you're both OG Asian YouTubers? rather than who I am, which is Nigahiga. Well, I know it's the N-word, but isn't that kind of what you named it after? I tried looking into that, but I could never get an official answer. Yes, yes. What advice would you give a mentally deranged person pointing a gun at you? Please, please don't point that gun at me. The question wasn't what you would tell the guy, it was what advice you would give him. Oh. Like life advice. It is never good, as a mentally deranged person, to point a gun at somebody. What are you looking at, you? Put the phone out, daddy, to record it. You scared the shit out of me. Do you think the funniest female comedian is funnier than a crow who knows several phrases? Um, I think I'd have to see the crow.

title: Dhurandhar Film Joke | Stand-up Comedy Clip| Ft. Amit Maharana Saini
transcription: धुरंधर देखी है आप लोगों ने? हाँ लगभग सभी ने, हाँ ठीक करा देख ली। मैंने भी देखी थी, इतना झूठ दिखा रखा ना उस पिक्चर में भाई। सही में शुरू में तो मुझे पता ही नहीं चला था। मैंने देख ली थी ऐसी ही, कि चार-पांच एक्टर हैं तो बढ़िया ही होगी पिक्चर और बढ़िया लगी मुझे। पर फिर एक दिन ऐसा हुआ, मेरा एक दोस्त है, नदीम उसने मुझे ध्रुव राठी की वीडियो भेजी और मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा, अबे वीडियो देख जो मैंने भेजी तुझे है। वो तो एक प्रोपेगैंडा फिल्म है, कुछ भी सच नहीं दिखा रखा उसमें। मैंने कहा सच नहीं दिखा रखा? तो भाई मैंने देखी वो जर्मन सिटीजन की वीडियो। वो खुद झूठ बोल रहा है उसमें। कह रहा बर्फ में कत्लेआम दिखा रखा बर्फ में, भाई पूरी पिक्चर में एक भी सीन बर्फ में लड़ाई का नहीं है। बर्फ वो सिर्फ गिलास में डाल रहे, और कहीं बर्फ नहीं और ये मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा तुम्हारा तो कोई भी काट देता है अंधभक्तों। मैंने कहा भाई इसमें काटने वाली क्या बात है, हमें तो बढ़िया लगी पिक्चर और रही बात काटने की तो सुन भाई नदीम। देख हमारा तो बचपन में नहीं कटा अब तो क्या ही कटेगा। नहीं कुछ बच्चों के साथ होता है स्कैम ये। देख वो रही चिड़िया, वो रही, वो रही, वो रही, ए उड़ गई, उड़ गई, नीचे साँप। अरे! भाई तुम समझ नहीं रहे। देखो दो साल का बच्चा है छोटा सा, उसके हाथ में डेढ़ लाख का मोबाइल है महंगा मोबाइल है ३०-३५ हज़ार की सिर्फ डिस्प्ले है। अब उसके हाथ से लेना हो गिरा ना दे तो क्या करना पड़ेगा? तब चिड़िया ही काम आती है। हाँ, तुम कहीं और पहुँच गए थे। पर फिर भी मुझे बुरा लगा यार कि मैं कैसे नहीं पकड़ पाया वो झूठ। तो मैंने दुबारा पिक्चर देखी वो। कितना झूठ दिखा रखा भाई आदित्य धर ने उसमें। पाकिस्तान में गलत दिखा दिया बताओ डांस। पाकिस्तान में! हैं? और वहाँ पे वो गार्ड रणवीर सिंह को रोक के बोलता है अन्दर सिर्फ कपल की एंट्री है।

transcription: अनंत अंबानी पदयात्रा पे जा रहे थे। गुजरात, यहाँ से बॉम्बे से गुजरात वो जा रहे थे पदयात्रा पे। अपना वो ग्रुप के साथ रात है ना, देखा होगा आपने पदयात्रा की थी उन्होंने गुजरात तक। तो अपनी पूरा उनकी टीम थी, काफ़ी सारा कैमरा थे, पीआर था, काफ़ी कुछ था। पीछे वो मेस्सी रस्सी में बंधा हुआ चल रहा था। है ना, ये मेस्सी अभी आया जो उसके साथ जो हमने किया। एड शीरन की रूह काँप गई कि अभी ये भी बाकी है इस देश, ये मेस्सी के साथ मैं ट्रू स्टोरी, ओके? नन ऑफ़ दिस इज़ आउट इन पब्लिक, बट दिस इज़ ट्रू। क्योंकि मेरा एक बहुत ही करीबी दोस्त जो मेस्सी का इवेंट हुआ यहाँ वानखेड़े में, जहाँ वो है ना, गोल ग्राउंड में अलग-अलग इवेंट्स चल रहे थे। तो वानखेड़े में जो दो-तीन घंटे का प्रोग्राम हुआ, वन ऑफ़ माय वेरी क्लोज़ फ्रेंड्स वाज़ वन ऑफ़ द फाइव फोटोग्राफर्स ऑन ग्राउंड इन द इनर रिंग ऑफ़ मेस्सी, सो ही सॉ थिंग्स अप क्लोज़। एंड दिस इज़ समथिंग व्हिच ही सॉ एंड 100% ट्रू। मेस्सी वहाँ पे ग्राउंड में इधर-उधर उसको ले जा रहे थे। यहाँ बच्चों के साथ फुटबॉल खेल रहा था, यहाँ पे कोई एनजीओ था या वहाँ कुछ डांसर थे, फिर वहाँ पे फर्स्ट इन्फ्लुएंसर महाराष्ट्र वो आई मेस्सी के साथ ऐसे च्युइंगम चबाते हुए उसने फोटो लिया। फिर पूछा, "अच्छा, तुम्हारा हैंडल क्या है? मैं टैग कर दूँगी, तुम्हारे फॉलोअर बढ़ जाएंगे थोड़े, बताओ।" तो ये सब चल रहा था। तो मेस्सी को इधर-उधर हम लोग दौड़ा रहे थे उस ग्राउंड में। उसी समय महाराष्ट्र के एक बहुत सीनियर पॉलिटिशियन आए, आई वोंट नेम हिम बिकॉज़ आई वांट टू लिव हियर, बट एक सीनियर पॉलिटिशियन आए अपनी पूरी है ना, वो कोटरी के साथ और पीछे-पीछे वो आ रहे थे, वो मेस्सी के साथ

title: EVERYTHING You Need To Know About The New WEGOVY PILL
transcription: It's 6:20 in the morning. You're half awake. Your brain is chanting one word: coffee. Now, plot twist: your new weight loss pill looks you in the soul and says, "Not yet. We need 30 minutes alone with water." Welcome to 2026 where Wegovy is now a tablet, needle-free, but it's not rule-free. Today, we're doing the great trade: the weekly shot versus the daily pill. Not which one is better online, which one fits real humans with real mornings and real habits. Quick note: this is education, not personal medical advice. Talk with your clinician before starting or switching any GLP-1 medication. And one more thing, as an obesity medicine doctor, most of my patients have been successful with weight loss by simply going low-carb, keto, or carnivore, but the reality is there are some people who need help, and that's why I made this video. All right, five rounds, scoreboard style, and I'll drop lesser-known facts that most influencers won't mention. Fast, clear, and practical for you. Round one, let's talk about convenience. Weekly shot: once a week, any time of day, with or without meals. Daily pill: once a day, but it comes with terms and conditions. FDA label rules in human language: empty stomach, morning, water only up to 4 oz, swallow whole, then wait at least 30 minutes before food, drinks, or other oral meds. Lesser-known fact: the tablet includes an absorption helper called salcaprozate sodium, abbreviated SNAC. Score: shot gets round one for pure convenience. Shot, 1; pill, 0. Round two, compliance. Will it actually do this? The coffee test: can you delay coffee for 30 minutes most mornings? If yes, the pill may fit. If your coffee is basically your therapist, the weekly shot may be your peace treaty. Lesser-known fact: the pill has a three-month ramp to maintenance. Day 1 through 30, 1.5 mg. 31 through 60, 4 mg.

transcription: In this video, I will show you exactly how to use Claude AI step-by-step. Claude is an AI assistant that helps you write, analyze information, and create things you can actually use. I'm Kevin, and we'll start with the basics, like writing, summarizing information, and working with files. Then, we'll move on to more powerful features like artifacts, projects, connectors, and skills. By the end, you'll know how to use Claude to actually get work done, not just chat with it. Let's get started. First, head to the Claude website. You'll find a link right here at the bottom of the screen, and then sign in. It's completely free to get started. Once you're in, this is the main screen where all your conversations happen. Here, in the middle, you'll see the prompt box. This is where you type what you want Claude to do. Over on the left-hand side, you have what's called the sidebar. From here, you can start a new chat, you can also access more advanced features, and down here at the bottom, you can also view your recent chats so you can always come back to your work. Let's start with something simple. I'll ask Claude to write a professional email. Then, right over here, let's run that. Here, you can see Claude created a full, professional email with structure. We even have some bullet points and all the details we would need to send this to a supplier. Now, in most cases, this is already pretty good. But I didn't actually specify the type of cookie. Here, it looks like it assumes it's chocolate chips since that is the most popular type of cookie, although I had oatmeal raisin in mind. I don't have to start over if it's not perfect. Instead, I can refine it. Down below, I'll type in a prompt to modify this email so it's for oatmeal raisin cookies instead, and then let's run that. Right up on top, we can now see the updated email message, and down below, we can see a summary of all the different changes that it made. And, of course, I could keep going from here. I could ask it to make the email shorter, maybe make it more friendly, or just give it more context like let's say who the email is for or maybe what tone I want. This back and forth is really how you get the best results.

His voice is clear, friendly, and enthusiastic, with a well-paced delivery suitable for instructional content. There is no background noise, resulting in a crisp and clean audio experience. Kevin begins by explaining Claude's capabilities and outlining the tutorial's progression from basic to advanced features. Finally, he demonstrates a practical example: generating a professional email, and then refining the prompt to specify "oatmeal raisin" cookies instead of the default "chocolate chip," illustrating how to interactively improve the AI's output.

title: Give me 5 minutes. I'll Fix your Hips. (5 simple steps)
transcription: The ground will rewild your body back to its natural form. It's simple, free, and a better teacher than any mobility coach or influencer's flexibility plan. People have been using it for thousands of years. Here's how you can free your body for no cost and just a little effort. Katie Bowman is a renowned biomechanist who's literally wrote the book on natural movement. She's a proponent of using the connection to our natural environment to bring back our mobility. She uses this cool analogy of orca whales in captivity. Their dorsal fin starts to collapse because it lacks the natural forces of the ocean. Wild orcas do not collapse. Aren't humans the same? We need the natural forces of gravity and the ground. Soft chairs and couches give us less feedback and we become stiff. Ironically, the hard ground keeps our body softer and more pliable. Sitting cross-legged on the ground, just like when we were kids, can start to restore natural levels of hip and spine mobility. I mean, look no further than yogis, the most flexible people in the world, who spend hours sitting cross-legged in meditation. Back in 2015, I was stiff as a board. I read Katie's Move Your DNA and I started to do some computer work sitting on the ground. It didn't happen overnight, but my hips were gradually restored from all of the heavy lifting and hours of chair sitting I put them through. You can do the same. Start with using a pillow under your hips to make it more comfortable, especially if you're stiff. Just a few minutes at first, and then gradually up the time and work it into your life like I did. Kneeling on the ground with the feet flat against the floor is an ancient Japanese position used by samurai warriors. It's been used for meditation, tea ceremonies, and simply having a meal. This position starts to loosen the ankles, knees, and hips, and fully bending the knees becomes lost to many older folks. This position ensures you keep it. The feet and ankles become rigid as we age because of soft shoes and repetitive movements. This position keeps them soft and pliable, but to heels was too much for my 2015 body. I started with a prop to raise my hips slightly. Start with 30 seconds here, then reach 1 minute. Then turn it into a habit throughout your day. Changing the foot position takes this position even further. When the toes extend, we strengthen the first ray and this is our connection to the ground. This influences the way that we walk and move and working on this often restores the plantar fascia on the bottom of the foot. It also improves dorsiflexion, the ankle's ability to bend forward. Toes extended is way more intense. Start with a few sets of 10 seconds and you can also explore reps like I'm doing here. You'll be surprised at how restoring the hips, feet, and ankles with those first three positions naturally leads you to a more relaxed deep squat. We've talked so much about deep resting squats here. I'll just hit the main benefits. Restore hip and ankle mobility, improve diaphragmatic breathing and digestion, decompress spine after sitting or standing for a while. The squat is much more than an exercise, it's a natural human position used for rest, play, and function. Spending time here daily is almost a non-negotiable. title: JD Vance Addresses His Past Comments About Donald Trump | The View
transcription:
**Speaker 1**: So, Mr. Vice President, in your new book, Communion, you write about your personal evolution with faith from Evangelical to Atheist to Catholic convert. And you also explain your evolution similarly on Trump, from calling him America's Hitler to America's best hope. Now, as someone who has admitted to chasing ambition, which you write about in in the book, in the past, but now says your faith brought you back to your priorities, I have to kind of use your own words that sit with me from 2016.

**Speaker 2**: Sure.

**Speaker 1**: Fellow Christians, everyone is watching when we apologize for this man. Lord help us. And I think about that all the time, because as a fellow Christian, that is something that weighs on my heart as I watch this country and the leadership at the top, because it's also something I have to explain to my kids, which I know we also share, this idea that our greatest privilege and responsibility are these young people we're raising.

**Speaker 2**: Of course.

**Speaker 1**: So, help me find the words to explain my children what they're witnessing right now.

**Speaker 2**: Well, you know, first of all, it's it's been well covered that I was a critic of Donald Trump back in 2015 and 2016. Now, obviously, I'm sitting here as the Vice President of the United States in in the Trump administration.

**Speaker 1**: Well, what happened?

**Speaker 2**: Well, Joy, a little humility, actually. I I think that when you make predictions and those predictions turn out to be false, you got to ask yourself, well, what what made me wrong about that? What did I not understand or not appreciate? For example, I said that Donald Trump's economic policies would not lead to wage growth. They did in the first term. That was actually a major, major thing. I said that we couldn't bring back any of those factory jobs because I kind of had given in to this idea that those jobs were disappearing. But actually, Donald Trump, you saw a manufacturing boom during that administration. So, so, there's a certain point, let me just let me just let me just finish. So, so, there's a certain point where you say, you know, I I made predictions about this, I ended up being wrong...

**Speaker 1**: Yeah.

**Speaker 2**: ...and in politics and anything, I think it's important just to say, you know what, I got some things wrong and I was wrong about him. He was a very successful president, it's one of the reasons why I've been so supportive of him.

**Speaker 1**: But you go on in the book to explain that good policy was maybe one of your justifications, but the quote and when you tweeted that or or X'd it, was not about policy. It was what Christians were willing to excuse. And that's the part I can't get past. What are you willing to excuse in the name of power?

**Speaker 2**: Well...

title: UNESCO Video Message | Youth Summit & Conference 2026 | Colombo, Sri Lanka
transcription: Good morning to all distinguished guests, experts, policymakers, and especially the young leaders gathered in Colombo. It is a privilege to join you for the Grace Island Environmental and Marine Conservation Summit 2026. I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to Grace Island and the Kolkata Society for Cultural Heritage for creating a platform that brings together stakeholders from across South Asia to confront our shared environmental challenges in a spirit of cooperation and urgency. Sri Lanka has a coastline of approximately 1,340 kilometers, a striking natural asset for a small island nation. This extensive coastline supports rich biodiversity, fisheries, and coastal livelihoods, but it also places the country at the forefront of climate change impact, such as sea-level rise, erosion, and marine pollution. These coastlines and marine and coastal ecosystems are not only of immense value for heritage conservation, but also play a vital role in fisheries, tourism, and a wide range of socioeconomic activities that sustain communities and contribute significantly to national development. Sri Lanka also holds at least 88 square kilometers of mangrove ecosystems, which are among the most important blue carbon habitats in the region. These mangroves play a vital role in storing carbon, protecting shorelines from erosion, and serving as nurseries for marine biodiversity. Sri Lanka's marine and coastal ecosystems are among its most valuable natural assets. They sustain livelihoods, protect biodiversity, and support national resilience. Yet, these ecosystems, like in most other places in the world, are undergoing pressure from climate change, pollution, and the ongoing degradation of critical habitats. Meeting these challenges demands more than awareness, and it requires coordinated, science-based action at every level.

title: Ryan Short | Keynote Speaker on Place Branding | CivicBrand
transcription: There's this Latin phrase, probably won't say it right, but I think it's "esse quam videri." It means "to be rather than to seem." Said by Cicero a long time ago. In 1893, North Carolina made it part of their seal and their motto. And I think the spirit of it is hopefully pretty obvious, but it's like, it's not something you say. It's something that you do, right? If you say you're about something, it should show up in your, your policies and your budgets and your actions, not just your marketing campaigns and the words that you say. I was talking to director of Arts and Culture Department for a city, and they, he, they had done a council workshop. It's kind of day-long thing where they're going to, you know, like councils do. The whole first half of the day, budget cuts. What are we cutting? Public art, zero. His department just got gutted, ripped apart, everything. "Where can we cut? Where can we cut? Where can we cut?" to where he's like, "I don't even have anything left to cut." Because there's, there's important stuff: fire, safety, public safety, like real things that like, we can't cut those things, so we're going to cut the art and the culture and some of these things first, right? These are the nice-to-have things, and times are tough, nobody wants to do it, but we got to be adults. We got to, you know, make the hard choices. And people get that. I think smart people get that. But then at the close of the council workshop, "Let's end on a positive note. Budget talk wasn't fun. Let's have a new mission statement, vision statement for the city." They kind of brainstormed ideas. What are we all about? Art and culture was front and center. "This is what we're about: art and culture." And he stood up, he's like, "Are you kidding me? We just spent the whole day gutting arts and culture, our reality, to then just go put it on a little poster and say, 'We're about arts and culture.' That is the opposite of "to be rather than to seem." That is, we want to seem like we're about arts and culture, but we're not really about arts and culture.

This creates frequent pauses and audible gasps in his speech. He explains the meaning of the Latin phrase "Esse quam videri," which translates to "To be, rather than to seem." He shares a story about a city's arts and culture department, whose budget was gutted during a council workshop, yet the council later decided to make "arts and culture" the center of their new mission statement. He uses this irony to argue that a place's actions should match its words and that places that loudly proclaim to be welcoming or innovative are often the least so. The room has a slight resonance, indicating a closed, quiet space with no background noise.

title: Changing the Way DFL Politicians Speak to People Is Only the First Step
transcription: Hi, and welcome to another episode of Better Minneapolis. I'm your host, Terry White. If you're interested in what we're doing here and appreciate it, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Today's episode is called, Changing the Way DFL Politicians Speak to People is Only the First Step. Real programs that improve residents' lives, daily lives, are needed to rebuild the DFL's brand. The Humphrey Mondale Dinner Thursday night drew a sold-out crowd to the Minneapolis Convention Center. For DFL leaders and donors, it was an opportunity to network and discuss the party's path forward. Past keynote speakers have included Hakeem Jeffries, Nancy Pelosi, Hillary and Bill Clinton, and Elizabeth Warren. This year's speaker was Andy Beshear, Governor of Kentucky, a choice that carried a message. Beshear's record speaks for itself. According to the DFL website, the Beshear administration has secured more than 35 billion in private sector investment, the most of any governor in state history, driving over 60,000 new full-time jobs and supporting over 1,100 new and expanded business projects. Under his leadership, Kentucky has achieved record budget surpluses and experienced historically low unemployment rates. That's a resume most governors envy. It's also, it also gives weight to a central message. Democrats need to stop using jargon like, quote, "justice-involved individuals," end quote, and start speaking normal language, as Paula Chesley, who attended the event, shared with us. Beshear understands the reputational damage Democrats have inflicted by importing language from sociology seminars into everyday conversation. Surveys confirm it. People dislike Trump, but they dislike Democrats even more. The polling points to two areas where the DFL could gain traction with voters if they develop a coherent plan: the economy and immigration. The economy. Ditching classroom-scrubbed language for plain speech is necessary, but it's not enough. The DFL must demonstrate that it can improve people's economic lives, that working people can earn wages to raise families and afford healthcare.

title: Minimizing Tech Turnover in Conferences & Festivals | Cut E-Waste, Reuse Gear & Recycle Responsibly
transcription: Welcome. Today we're exploring how conferences and festivals can minimize technology turnover, reducing costs, extending equipment life, and supporting sustainability across every stage of event design and production. Today's events rely heavily on technology, from digital signage to mobile apps to interactive displays, all designed to elevate audience engagement. But rapid upgrading cycles push many devices out of service long before the end of their usable life. This constant replacement adds financial pressure, creating higher purchasing, storage, and transport costs. With smarter planning, events can maintain quality while utilizing existing equipment more efficiently and sustainably. Tech turnover often stems from a desire to impress with the newest gear, even when older equipment is still functional. This perception-driven cycle leads to high volumes of discarded tablets, displays, LED panels, and networking devices. Replacing equipment too frequently strains event budgets and contributes to growing e-waste streams. Each discarded device contains materials that require proper disposal through licensed recyclers to avoid environmental harm. Strong inventory management helps reduce unnecessary replacements. By keeping accurate records of equipment age, usage, and condition, event teams can clearly determine when upgrades are truly needed. Asset management systems allow devices to be rotated across multiple events, extending their lifespan. These tools also reveal when a piece of equipment can be repaired or refurbished instead of being replaced outright. With better visibility, purchasing decisions become smarter, more cost-effective, and more sustainable. Modular equipment is one of the most valuable strategies for reducing turnover. Interchangeable components allow lighting, audio boards, and AV systems to be repaired easily without replacing entire devices. Firmware upgrades can also extend the useful life of older equipment. Interoperability ensures older and newer devices function together, preventing unnecessary full system upgrades. Planning for modularity reduces both long-term costs and the environmental footprint of constant tech replacement. Not every event requires brand-new technology. Many attendees care far more about meaningful content and clear audiovisual output than the generation of the device being used.

title: International Women’s Day 2026 Theme | Rights. Justice. Action. | Give To Gain | UN Women
transcription: As we stand in the second quarter of the 21st century, women are still not equal before the law. Not in 1926, not in 1976, and still not in 2026. Today is not a celebration. Today is not about flowers, slogans, or hashtags. Today is about power and who has it and who still does not. As we stand in the second quarter of the 21st century, with advanced technology, global institutions, and centuries of progress behind us, one truth remains deeply uncomfortable. Women are still not equal before the law. Not in 1926, not in 1976, and still not in 2026. Right now, in 2026, women hold only 64% of the legal rights that men hold worldwide. 64%. This is not a statistic from the past. This is not history. This is now. If progress continues at the current pace, it will take 286 years to close the legal protection gaps between women and men. 286 years. That is not a timeline, that is surrender. In no country on earth have women and men achieved full legal equality, not one. Across fundamental areas of life: work, money, safety, family, property, mobility, business, healthcare, and retirement, the law continues to systematically disadvantage women. And where the law fails women, justice fails women. Every year, 12 million girls are pushed into early or child marriage. Not because they lack potential, but because the law allows it, because systems look away, because justice is denied before life even begins. The S&P 500, the Nasdaq, and the Dow all surged right out of the gate, washing the financial news networks in a sea of green. Retail traders immediately rushed in to buy the dip. They saw the falling prices from the week prior as a discount, completely ignoring the active military conflict choking off international trade routes. This sudden burst of buying is a classic psychological trap. It covers up severe structural rot with a thin layer of tech-driven optimism, tricking investors into thinking the worst of the crisis is already over. Two specific headlines drove this morning's euphoria. First, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang took the stage at his company's developer conference. Crude futures dropped $5.26, settling at $93.35 per barrel, driven entirely by the hope of safe passage.
