title: Shettima Urges Governors on Economic Growth | Senate Approves E-Transmission | 2026
transcription: This is Megastar Magazine TV. Hello and welcome to Megastar Magazine TV. My name is Monique Agbey. In the news, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged governors of the 36 states, ministers, and other public officials to pursue an inclusive economic growth model that filters down to the everyday lives of Nigerians. Shettima spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the opening of the National Economic Council, NEC, conference, a two-day retreat of governors and key stakeholders aimed at strengthening national economic coordination and accelerating inclusive growth. The Vice President warned that the government's mission would remain incomplete if progress does not translate into dignity, opportunity, and hope for citizens across the country. The Senate has approved the electronic transmission of election results to the Independent National Electoral Commission's results viewing portal, while permitting manual collation to serve as a backup where technology fails. The decision followed a reconsideration of a disputed clause in the Electoral Act Amendment Bill during an emergency plenary on Tuesday. The upper chamber stopped short of making electronic transmission compulsory and also rejected the provision for real-time upload of results. Under the reviewed section, presiding officers at polling units are to electronically transmit results to the IReV portal after voting and documentations are completed. The amendment, however, provides that where electronic transmission cannot be carried out due to communication or network challenges, the manual results sheet, form EC8A, will become the primary basis for collation and declaration. The Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja held that the Senate acted within its powers when it suspended the lawmaker representing Kogi Central, Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, for misconduct. The court held that the suspension did not violate the senator's parliamentary privileges or her constitutional rights. The court set aside the contempt proceedings and the 5 million Naira fine earlier imposed on the lawmaker over an unprofessional apology she directed at Senate President, Godswill Akpabio.

title: Archaea are Highly Prevalent in the Small Intestine
transcription:
My name is Maria Jesus Villanueva Millan and I am project scientist at MAST program, and I am presenting a poster at DDW 2022, which is entitled "Archaea are highly prevalent in the human small intestine and the absolute abundance of Methanobrevibacter is associated with older age and greater microbial diversity."

Archaea are part of the microbiomes, but once they were underestimated. But now we know that they have beneficial and detrimental properties. For example, Methanobrevibacter smithii is associated with constipation and obesity, but also appears in more abundance in centenarians. Most of the studies are focus on stool, but we want to do this study to know what happens in the small intestine. And also, we wanted to use absolute abundance to have a real idea of the potential biological impact of these microorganisms.

To achieve this, we collected duodenal aspirates from human subjects that were in the REIMAGINE study. And these subjects underwent EGD without colon prep. Once we got these duodenal aspirates, we extract the DNA and do shotgun sequencing, and then we calculated the absolute abundance of these microorganisms, the archaea, in the human small intestine.

343 subjects were analyzed in this study, and one of the main results were that the most prevalent and abundant archaeal phyla were the phyla Methanobacteriota and Thermoproteota. And about the genera, what we saw is that the the genus Halorubrum and Methanobrevibacter were the most prevalent and abundant. And when we wanted to see the abundance

title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Nonlinear Optical Properties
transcription: Hi, my name is Gamrich, and I'm here to talk about our GECCO project called the Multi-objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Non-linear Optical Properties. So, NLO materials are essential for mainly telecommunications infrastructure, and we look at specifically the device called an electro-optic modulator, which modulates a beam of light. So, we're looking at NSGA-II, MAP-Elites, MoAM, mu-lambda, and then simulated annealing. So, a mix of QD and multi-objective optimization algorithms, and then some single-objective ones. How we encode molecules is using SMILES. We limit our molecular search space to organic atoms, and we employ these seven mutation operators, and we do not use crossover in our evolution. And you can see how symbols are used to encode molecules. We evaluate the properties which we're optimizing using quantum chemistry, and specifically the Hartree-Fock level of theory with the PySCF library. So, our multi-objective algorithms maximize the beta over gamma ratio, which is important for frequency conversion. We target a range of 100 to 500 atomic units for linear polarizability. Our HOMO-LUMO gap, we target a range of 2 to 4 electron volts. And then our energy per atom, we try to minimize, and this promotes stability in the molecule. And then our single-objective algorithms simply optimize the beta-gamma ratio. So, each algorithm evaluates approximately 2,000 molecules across 20 independent seeds. Our main metric for performance here is the global hypervolume. As you can see, we have two variations of each of the QD algorithms. We have an F and a C. That simply means fine and coarse-grained binning. So, the F is fine, C is coarse. And that's because we have a 10-by-10 and a 20-by-20 archive based on the atom count and the bond count, which the atoms range from 5 to 30 and the bonds from 4 to 32. So, the MoAM with the fine-grain binning, so MoAM F, does the best in our global hypervolume, and you can also see in the final Pareto fronts here.

Axolotl, you can remove 30% of its heart and it grows back perfectly. Humans are very different. If you suffer injury, a heart attack, lung disease, liver disease, you will go through a heavy inflammation period followed by heavy scarring. And this can perpetuate and become chronic disease. transcription: Hi, I'm Gabriela Leite from Cedars-Sinai Medical Center at MAST Program, and I'm here to present my poster, which is Levels of serum antibodies to cytolethal distending toxin B, or CDTB, in human subjects predicts SIBO by small bowel culture and an altered small intestinal microbiome by shotgun sequencing. Sorry, acute gastroenteritis is associated with IBS, and is often caused by species such as Campylobacter jejuni and Escherichia coli strains that encode a toxin called CDTB. SIBO is also linked to IBS, and small bowel microbial whole genome sequencing indicates that Escherichia coli and Klebsiella species, such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, are the species dominant in SIBO. Interestingly, immunizing rats with Campylobacter jejuni CDTB caused SIBO and IBS-like traits. Antibodies anti-CDTB is a validated IBS marker, but the link between antibodies anti-CDTB and SIBO in humans is unclear. Thus, we investigate the relationship between antibodies anti-CDTB and SIBO by applying a quantitative shotgun sequencing to duodenal microbiome samples from human subjects undergoing standard of care endoscopy. title: Beyond Silos: Transformative Change for the Caribbean
transcription: Across the Caribbean, environmental pressures are no longer unfolding separately. Climate instability, biodiversity decline, rising food dependence and economic vulnerability increasingly collide, amplifying risks across ecosystems, livelihoods and communities. For small island developing states, the consequences are deeply interconnected. So, from food security right through to spiritual well-being, ability to heal and restore, biodiversity plays a critical role. So, this sector needs to go beyond the symptom, the symptoms of the crisis. We have to go deeper. And these are things that I think the environmental sector has avoided for too long. At the second Caribbean regional trialogue, participants repeatedly returned to one central idea, interconnected crises cannot be solved through isolated action. The discussions challenged traditional approaches that treat biodiversity, climate, food systems and development as separate policy areas. What the nexus assessment did is very different from a lot of the previous assessments. It sought to move away from the piecemeal approaches and the siloed sectoral thinking to looking across different sectors: health, food, climate, biodiversity, to find response options that will deliver multiple co-benefits at scale. The conversations also reinforced that these systems extend beyond national borders. As a region, as a Caribbean, it forces us to contemplate how we treat with our neighbors.

title: What Brings Matter to Life? — A Physics of Life Film
transcription: For over a century, physicists have pushed the boundaries of our understanding, revealing the hidden structures of the world around us. Through these discoveries, we've unlocked the secrets of the tiniest particles and mapped the far reaches of the cosmos. And yet, physics holds a mystery that remains unsolved: the phenomenon of life itself. At Physics of Life, we explore what brings matter to life. Our goal is to reveal the physical principles that govern the complex organization of living organisms. We are bridging scales from molecules to cells and tissues, and combining experiments, theory, and simulations. We learn by dissecting living systems, and also by rebuilding them. What physical mechanisms enable cells to perform functions? Why do embryos develop so robustly? And what are the equations for life?

transcription: I found out that I was being physically surveilled by the following method. Um, we, my ex and I realized, my ex-boyfriend and I realized that people had been breaking into our apartment while we were gone together in the same vehicle. And so like, I'm in the apartment, I'm about to go to work and I'm like, why don't you take out the trash and scope out the parking lot and make sure it's okay before I go to work. So he goes out there and he's like, there's this weird fucking Lexus. It's like a silver Lexus, this is a shitty apartment, like, why is there really fucking really nice Lexus in the parking lot? And it has tinted windows that are not street legal, like just totally dark, totally black tinted windows that are not possibly street legal. And so we're, he comes back in and we're standing in our bedroom window looking at the Lexus and talking about it. And I say out loud, maybe we should walk over there later and take a picture of the license plate. Because the Lexus is across the parking lot from us, but is backed in so you can't see the license plate. Within 2 minutes of me saying, "Hey, we should walk over there later and take a picture of the license plate." We were still standing there at the window looking at it, talking about it. And a Eastern European looking motherfucker with a black beanie, dressed all in black in his 50s or 60s walked out of the apartment directly across from ours holding a license plate. And he opened the trunk of the Lexus and he took out some tools and he changed the license plate right in front of our fucking faces. And then he walked back to his apartment and he put the old license plate on the front patio and went inside, left it outside. And it was literally like, "Come get the license plate, I have more, I have more where this came from, come get the license plate." And then after that, the Lexus started tailing me, and every time I saw the Lexus, it had a different license plate. It would be like Alabama plates, a different state plate, it would be random dealer plates, none of which were local, just like cardboard temporary dealer plates, none of which were any local dealers. Every time I saw it, it was different plates.

title: Towards Calibrating Prompt Tuning of Vision- Language Models - CVPR 2026
transcription: I am presenting our work, towards calibrating prompt tuning of vision-language models. This work focuses on improving the reliability of prompt-tuned CLIP models. Our main goal is not only to improve accuracy, but also to make the model's confidence more trustworthy. Prompt tuning is widely used because it adapts CLIP efficiently without updating the full model. However, most existing methods mainly focus on classification accuracy. In real-world applications, accuracy alone is not enough. A model must also know how confident it should be. If a model gives high confidence to wrong predictions, it becomes risky in areas such as medical imaging, autonomous systems, and safety-critical AI. Therefore, models' predicted confidence should equal to the true likelihood or model predicted accuracy. This will ensure that the model's predicted confidence is calibrated. Post-hoc calibration can adjust confidence after training, but it cannot prevent embedding drift caused during prompt tuning. Our key observation is that prompt tuning creates a dual miscalibration problem. For base classes, the model often becomes underconfident because the logit margins are reduced. For novel classes, the model becomes overconfident because the margins become inflated or unstable. The reliability diagrams and margin analysis show that margin behavior affects base and novel classes differently. Therefore, we need a train-time method that controls both logit margins and text embedding geometry, which preserves CLIP geometry by preventing prompt-induced semantic drift and stabilizes class relations, reducing overconfident wrong predictions, thereby lowering calibration error. To solve this, we propose two complementary losses. First, the mean variance margin loss stabilizes the logit gap between the ground-truth class and the strongest incorrect class. This helps improve confidence separation. Second, the text moment matching loss preserves CLIP's original text embedding geometry by matching the distribution of tuned text embeddings with frozen CLIP embeddings. The total loss combines cross-entropy, margin regularization, and moment matching. Together, they reduce base class underconfidence and novel class overconfidence. Margin loss alone is useful, but it can still create high-confidence wrong predictions, especially on novel classes. This happens because if the model predicts the wrong class, increasing the margin can make that wrong prediction even more confident. Moment matching solves this by preserving semantic geometry. So, margin improves discriminability, while moment matching prevents semantic drift. Their combination gives better calibration, especially for novel classes. We evaluate the method on 11 datasets: ImageNet, Caltech-101, Pets, Cars, Flowers...

The speaker explains the risks of miscalibrated models in safety-critical applications like autonomous systems and medical imaging. He highlights a "dual miscalibration problem," where base classes become underconfident and novel classes become overconfident. To address this, he proposes two complementary losses: the "mean variance margin loss" and the "text moment matching loss," explaining how they work together to stabilize logit margins and preserve text embedding geometry. Finally, he mentions evaluating the method across 11 datasets, including ImageNet, Caltech 101, Pets, Cars, and Flowers. The audio is high quality, with no noticeable background noise.

title: Plaud Note Pro - before you buy
transcription: Let's talk about the PLAUD NOTE and the PLAUD NOTE Pro which I actually have right here. This is an AI note-taking device and I'm going to be honest right off the bat and tell you that you probably don't need this. This is not a device that I'd recommend to everybody. But for the right type of person, this could be pretty useful. And I did drop an affiliate link in the description below. So at first, I wasn't going to make this video. PLAUD actually reached out to me and offered me a review unit and I said, "No, I don't think that I would use this." And then I started seeing their ads everywhere and curiosity got the better of me and I thought, "You know, what the heck. I'll try it out. I'll give it a shot." So I forked over $189 to buy the top-of-the-line PLAUD NOTE Pro. So after 3 months of using this, I love it. And I've even upgraded to a minutes subscription which I'll talk about later in the video. The PLAUD NOTE has become a big part of my professional workflow. So let's talk about what this thing is. At its core, the PLAUD NOTE is a tape recorder. It has four microphones and a button. The Pro version has a tiny screen showing you battery life and has better recording capabilities. It can record up to 16 ft away. It also has a magnetic adapter for MagSafe and other phones that you can stick to your phone and it will even record phone calls in the phone mode. But the true magic happens in the app transcription. PLAUD uses a combination of AI models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to transcribe your recordings, and the transcriptions are excellent. Of all the AI transcription tools and apps that I've used, this consistently ranks among the best. When you're done recording, it syncs to the app over Bluetooth with the option of using Wi-Fi for a faster connection. You then have the option to generate a transcription and summary. You can either use the auto-generation which I think works best for most recordings or use a custom template like meeting minutes or a special analysis template, and then after a few minutes, it will deliver the full transcript and summary. You also have the ability to label individual speakers which I find super helpful. And the summary has an AI chat feature so you can ask it questions about the recording and even do things like ask it to provide infographics, which is pretty cool. Personally, I don't use the app and chat features a whole lot. I mainly use this just for transcriptions. I press a button, it starts recording, it syncs to my app and transcribes,

title: Wearable Technology Helps Local Father Born Legally Blind See with 20/20 Clarity!
transcription: Oh, well, good morning and welcome back. A local father from the San Fernando Valley was born legally blind, but all thanks to eyewear technology, he can now see with 20/20 clarity in real time. Here to tell us about the life-changing technology that allowed him to see his children's faces clearly for the first time is local dad Cosmo Moor. Good morning, thanks for joining us. Good morning, thanks for having me. Tell us about being born legally blind. How impaired was your vision before wearing this technology? I was born with optic nerve atrophy, and so it's uncorrectable because glasses fix eyeball issues. This is the nerve that connects the eyeball to the brain, so nothing can be done. Stem cell research maybe one day, but we're behind on that. So my vision's 20 over 400. What a normally-sighted person can see at 400 feet, I have to get up at 20 to see. And, for example, my phone has the accessibility turned up to maximum text. I still have to hold it an inch away from my face to see it. And so with these glasses, it has a camera here, feeds it to the screens. It can zoom up to 24 times and with it, I can see 20/20. That's incredible. You found the creators of eSight, which is a wearable technology, by the way, you see it on your face now, and suddenly you were able to see your children's faces clearly for the first time. Take us back to that moment and how you said at that point, "I got to be all in with this company and I'll work with them." Yeah. Um, I tried out the first generation eSight in 2013. It was much bigger, the controller was wired and it was huge, and it was $15,000, and so I passed on that, but I stayed following the company and in 2017, that's when I got an eSight 3. This is the fifth generation device. Wow. And, to see somebody's face, well, I need to be 18 in away, and that doesn't happen very often other than my wife. And so the first time I put this on and I could zoom in and see their faces clearly, one of my favorite memories was going to the zoo with my then 3-year-old, and he got on the merry-go-round. And normally, I just waved to daddy, "Yeah, I can't see you. I hope that's you." And I could track his face the whole way around when he went to the merry-go-round and that was cool seeing the joy

title: Reclaiming the lost art of listening to music
transcription: To Connor Knighton now and an invitation to just listen. And we're going to ask that when we drop the needle we refrain from any conversation. This is a listening environment. Seattle Shibuya Hi-Fi is a listening bar. Our guests can chat and sip cocktails in the lounge. They then leave their drinks and their shoes behind as they settle into the back room to enjoy full-length albums in a communal setting. An evening might feature anything from Björk to David Bowie. I love David Bowie cuz I've got, oh my gosh, my Bowie tattoo. I had to be here. It's the closest thing I could get to a David Bowie concert. These curated sessions, around 80 a month, regularly sell out. People are buying $20 tickets to listen to albums they could hear at home for free. That seems to me to be something that people are really rediscovering, that pleasure and the beauty of focus and intentional listening. Quentin Ertel is the co-owner of Shibuya Hi-Fi, which takes its name from a neighborhood in Tokyo. In Japan, listening bars, often called jazz kissas, started gaining popularity back in the 1930s. But similar venues have exploded in the US in recent years, popping up everywhere from Minnesota to Missouri to Colorado. There is a new wave of like these kind of listening bars especially in the West. Oh, cool. Artist and engineer Devon Turnbull designs high-end, handmade audio equipment for his company Ojas. While his speakers often end up in private living rooms, he's also created larger public listening rooms. The Smithsonian's Cooper Hewitt Museum in New York is currently showcasing what Turnbull has deemed his Hi-Fi Pursuit Listening Room Dream No. 3, installed in what was once Andrew Carnegie's private library. Pursuit is a really important part of the title. I am not here to say that I have made the ultimate sound system. This is about my pursuit as a builder, as someone who's passionate about building audio equipment and listening to music through it. Turnbull works out of a warehouse in Brooklyn's Navy Yard. His interest in all things audio traces back to an early age.

title: Investigative Journalist Tom O'Neill on CIA's MKUltra Mind-Control Program
transcription: Almost 50 years ago, the last congressional hearings into MK-Ultra took place just a short walk from here in the Dirksen Senate Office Building. At those hearings convened in August and September of 1977, representatives of the CIA told Congress and the American people that its 25-year effort to control human behavior had been a colossal failure. Because I believe Congress was never told the truth about what this program actually achieved. In fact, I believe the agency misled Congress in 1977 when it characterized MK-Ultra as a failure. My name is Tom O'Neill and in 1999, I was accepted, I accepted a magazine assignment to write a story about murders committed by a group of hippies called the Manson family. For those unfamiliar with this horrific episode of American history, in the summer of 1969, four young people acting on the orders of a cult leader named Charles Manson went to the home of movie director Roman Polanski and murdered everyone they found there, including his eight-and-a-half-month pregnant wife, the actress Sharon Tate. The victims were complete strangers to the, to their killers. The following night, Manson's followers murdered another couple in the same grisly fashion. At the time I accepted the assignment, I had never heard of MK-Ultra, and I wouldn't for another two years, after I'd missed countless deadlines, lost the assignment, and fallen down a nightmarish rabbit hole trying to answer the question I couldn't quite shake. How had Manson, a barely literate ex-con, acquired the ability to persuade ordinary young people to murder complete strangers simply because he had told them to? The pursuit of that answer, the pursuit of the answer to that question led me to Dr. Louis Jolyon West, known to his friends as Jolly. West was one of the most influential psychiatrists in America. During his career, he crossed paths with some of the most controversial events of the 20th century, including the Patty Hearst kidnapping case and the aftermath of the John F. Kennedy assassination investigation.

transcription: Okay, in California, Democrats are taking heat for a new bill they're pushing that one lawmaker has now dubbed the "Stop Nick Shirley Act." Some people are arguing that the proposed legislation effectively criminalizes investigative journalism. GOP Florida Senator and member of the Homeland Security Committee Ashley Moody joins me now. I mean, they're they're basically saying you can't go out and investigate in the way that Nick Shirley did in Minneapolis. Yeah, this doesn't surprise me at all. A lot of, you know, we're uncovering in these comic criminal havens, let's call them. You know, they've their policies have bankrupted their states and they've built that in to these structural deficits like California, I think Massachusetts is struggling with deficits. All of these policies that they're implementing don't drive real market-driven prosperity. In fact, it wrecks true markets and the ability of of a state to thrive like Florida, right? Compare and contrast, we run a deficit every year. So then they go and cry to the federal government, we need all these grants, we need all this money, and they push that money out to these NGOs and other organizations, which through all kinds of grants, health grants, uh, you name it, you saw some of the stuff coming through COVID or even green energy during Biden, just pushing out billions and billions of dollars. And then when you have Americans like Nick Shirley showing up and saying, "Where's my taxpayer money going?" you're using so much of it to shield and cover up what you're pushing to, I would say illegally, to illegal immigration or other things. title: Report: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro applied pressure to indict Democratic lawmakers over video
transcription: There's brand new reporting in the New York Times this afternoon about the turmoil inside the Department of Justice when it came to that failed attempt to indict six Democratic lawmakers who released a video reminding the men and women of the military that they do not have to obey any illegal orders. According to that reporting in the New York Times, in mid-January, the inquiry into the lawmakers had no sense of urgency, and that when lawyers for the lawmakers were contacted by federal prosecutors, they were told that they were not told of any law that had been broken, according to six people familiar with the matter. Times goes on to report that everything changed two weeks later when, quote, "Janine Pirro abruptly instructed her team to seek an indictment of the lawmakers." Her prosecutors then faced a decision that many in the Department under Trump have confronted: comply or resist. They chose the first. That attempt to indict, of course, failed last week, but as the New York Times notes, it stood, quote, "as an example of the chaos that has roiled the Department as it has grappled with the President's increasingly erratic demands, even in the face of little evidence." Want to bring in New York Times investigative reporter Mike Schmidt, whose byline is on that reporting we read from. Also joining us, former acting assistant Attorney General for national security at the Justice Department, Mary McCord. Um, Mike, first take us through what you and your colleagues are reporting today. Well, basically, what we're trying to show is that when this investigation started, these prosecutors reached out to the defense lawyers for the six lawmakers and said, "Look, uh, we're in the early stages, we're not even sure if we're in the first inning yet, we're not even sure what law we're investigating this under, not even sure if it's an investigation. Uh, you know, could could one of the lawmakers come in and talk? You know, would one of the lawyers want to come in and talk to sort of get this thing going?" That is as informal a way of starting an investigation as possible, especially after the President of the United States has called for them, you know, essentially called for them to be investigated for this and raised the possibility that they could be punished, you know, up you know, up to um you know, Seditious conspiracy. Seditious conspiracy and execution. So, it had a very, very informal feeling to it. And within two weeks, they there was a prosecutors before grand jury trying to indict them.

title: BREAKING: Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment, REFUSES to answer Rand Paul
transcription: Senator Paul's obvious obsession with calling for my prosecution, his repeated slanderous comments about me, and recently, his publicly releasing my unredacted personal diary, aimed at embarrassing and intimidating me, the only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up in his words, quote, "behind bars," unquote. Any reasonable person who has followed his unhinged obsession with me would readily come to the same conclusion. Therefore, although it pains me to do so, because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of government, and my decades-long record of cooperating with Congress, under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution to refrain from answering your questions. Thank you. We will now uh begin a round of questioning. Uh, Dr. Fauci, your testimony today is compelled by a lawful subpoena. As you know, it's a crime under 18 U.S.C. Section 1001 to knowingly make a material false statement to Congress, with a penalty of up to five years of imprisonment. Understanding that you are under oath, the American people would like to understand your reasoning, your rationale for why you chose to fund uh the research in Wuhan. There have been, um, you know, intelligence agencies, the CIA, the FBI, the DOE, have all come to the conclusion that more likely than not, the virus came from the lab in Wuhan. And so we'd like to know what was the rationale, what was the discussion, how, you know, what went behind the decision to fund the research uh in Wuhan? Um, how did you come to the conclusion that a totalitarian country would be capable of doing this in a BSL-2 lab, a lab that lacked the security? What was the reasoning, and are you are you sorry, basically, for making the decision? Would you, you know, like given another chance, say, "Well, gosh, circumstances now as I know it, maybe it wasn't a wise thing." Can you explain to the committee why you chose to fund this dangerous research in China? On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution.

title: Investigation reveals DOJ withheld Epstein files mentioning Trump
transcription: A new NPR investigation reveals the Justice Department withheld portions of the Jeffrey Epstein files that contain allegations involving President Trump, including material tied to claims that Mr. Trump sexually abused a minor, and that some pages mentioning him were removed from the public record. Democrats on the House Oversight Committee called that out today, saying the DOJ's withholding of information could amount to a crime. For more on that and the surrounding fallout, we're joined now by Julie K. Brown, investigative reporter for the Miami Herald, whose reporting helped expose much of the Epstein network. Julie, welcome back to the program. It's great to have you. Thank you. I want to start with this NPR reporting that the Justice Department withheld some Epstein files related to allegations that President Trump sexually abused a minor, which we should say the White House denies. What stands out to you about this? Well, I think what stands out is that we don't have the reports, even though we know they exist. This stems from an interview that they conducted that came out of a tip to the FBI about this woman who has said that she, when she was 13, that she was sexually assaulted by Donald Trump. Now, her one of her interviews is contained in the Epstein files, although it is heavily redacted so it's hard to know exactly what she told the FBI. But as a result of that, we were able to see some of the the report numbers and the Bates stamps on it. And an independent journalist, actually named Roger Sollenberger, was the person that real that found out that compared that number to the documents that the Southern District of New York prosecutors gave to Ghislaine Maxwell's lawyers as part of her criminal case. You broke this story 8 years ago with your investigative reporting. With the benefit of time and hindsight, what do you see more clearly now about how power insulated Jeffrey Epstein, and how much of that protective structure still exists?

title: Nolan Wells' death: FBI probes threats
transcription: Welcome back. The FBI is investigating threats against the people who were with Nolan Wells in the hours before the Mississippi teen vanished and was found dead. Wells, 18, disappeared July 4th after joining friends on a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. Search crews scoured the area for two days before a National Park Service Ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip on July 6th. Wells' friends returned to the mainland that July afternoon without him, but Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter previously said investigators believed Wells chose to stay on the island. It wasn't until later that night that his mother learned that he was missing from one of Wells' friends and reported it to authorities. Mississippi's Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said Wednesday that the FBI is investigating threats made against public officials, the people who were with Wells before he vanished, and their families. Michelle Thomas is now joining us here on LiveNOW from FOX. Michelle, thank you so much for taking the time to talk with us. Thanks so much for having me. So, we talk about this case. The FBI is now investigating threats connected to the case. So, what kind of threats can become federal crimes, and why would the FBI get involved here? Well, anytime there's a threat regarding anyone's person, placing them in immediate harm, there's going to be an investigation. But here, they may also be looking for racially charged threats, given sort of the backdrop of what we've heard about in the public scrutiny, in the public eye, and with the backdrop in history of Mississippi. People are concerned about this case because of sort of the racial makeup and so forth. So, if there are any kind of threats along those lines, there's going to be an investigation, and possibly a federal one. And when we talk about authorities, you know, saying that witnesses, public officials, even family members have received some type of threat here or there, how can that affect an active criminal investigation that can be happening? Well, any kind of law enforcement is going to follow any leads and they're going to try to track any any type of threat because they don't want there to be either witness intimidation or witness coercion. They want to make sure that they're able to preserve the evidence and witness testimony, and that persons with knowledge are able to come forward without feeling fearful. So, it can taint an investigation, and possibly a forthcoming trial, if there are constant threats and people are afraid to come forward with the information needed to solve what happened to Nolan Wells.

title: 'GOBSMACKED': Nicolle reacts to BOMBSHELL new report about Trump family's brazen self-dealing
transcription: Each deeply reported account of self-dealing from the Trump White House seems to get more brazen than the one that came before it. The New York Times has now reviewed a number of federal filings and is out with an extraordinary piece of investigative reporting that details the latest way that Donald Trump's family and allies appear to be profiting off Donald Trump's policy decisions as president. It involves a billion-dollar mining deal with Kazakhstan and one that both Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's sons stand to profit from. In a meeting last September, Donald Trump and Howard Lutnick secured a deal with the leader of Kazakhstan to give a little-known American company now called Kaz Resources access to one of the world's largest untapped reserves of tungsten. It's a crucial rare earth mineral. Here's where the apparent self-dealing comes in, according to the New York Times. Weeks after that meeting, quote, "investors with a firm called Dominari Securities, which is housed at Trump Tower in New York and partly owned by the president's two eldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, joined with other partners to take a 20% stake in the corporate entity related to the Kazakhstan project." Around the same time, Cantor Fitzgerald, an investment company controlled by Howard Lutnick's family and overseen by his sons Brandon and Kyle Lutnick, helped one of the lead investors working with Dominari on the Kazakh deal raise $210 million in new capital for a related entity. Such rounds of fundraising typically net Cantor millions of dollars in fees. The deal was, quote, "ultimately signed on November 6th, six days after the investment involving the Trump sons and their partners, which was not publicly disclosed at the time." As the New York Times reports, this continues a pattern of self-enrichment in the Trump administration that has few precedents in American history. When asked for statements, both the White House and the Commerce Department rejected any suggestion that the Trump administration was improperly mixing government actions with family business. Trump's sons both denied being involved in the specifics of the deal. Eric Trump claimed they were passive investors. A Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said that company's executives were not involved in discussions related to government funding.

transcription: The United States and Saudi Arabia now have joined forces to strike Iran-backed terror sites in Iraq after the regime launched a surprise missile attack on American troops in the region who were traveling to Jordan. CENTCOM released a statement saying, "At 5:45 p.m. Eastern Time today, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on US forces based in the Middle East. All Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted. US forces remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness." The United States has not yet responded to that attack, but overnight, US and Saudi planes conducted a series of airstrikes against Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq who were responsible for 30 drone attacks over the past three days. On those strikes, CENTCOM said the unwarranted attacks against US forces were not successful. From February through April 2026, there were more than 600 attempted attacks on US citizens and facilities by Iran-aligned terrorist militias in Iraq. The IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response. This kinetic action in the Middle East comes as reports indicate Iran has rejected an Omani proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. On Tuesday, President Trump held a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as the pair decide the next steps in the war with Iran. Look at this regime today. It's attacking everybody in sight. It's attacking Saudi Arabia. It's attacking uh Kuwait, it's attacking uh uh Bahrain, it's attacking uh UAE and others. It's attacking everything in sight, and it murdered and maimed tens of thousands of its own citizens. This is what this regime in Iran does today when it doesn't have nuclear weapons. Now imagine what they will do to the world if they had nuclear weapons. And that's what we have to make sure that we prevent.

title: Trump ISSUES WARNING to Houthis after hinting at MAJOR Iran move
transcription: After almost two weeks of daily strikes against Iran, the past two nights have been remarkably quiet. This as President Trump warned earlier this week the US is locked and loaded if tensions reach a tipping point. Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst is live in Tel Aviv with the latest. Trey. Yeah, Peter, good morning. For now, the United States has halted strikes against Iran, as tension remains high across the Middle East. White House officials have indicated that many options remain on the table, including a military option for President Trump, as he explores solutions involving force and diplomacy. And every once in a while, they're going to set some things up, but they don't have much left, and by the way, they are talking to us right now. They'd love to make a deal. I don't think they're ready to. I don't think it's time yet, but I'm willing to listen, but they cannot have a nuclear weapon. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung told Fox News Digital that President Trump has always been consistent in saying he prefers a diplomatic solution, but he continues to retain all options if Iran continues terrorist activities in the Strait of Hormuz or against allies. The US naval blockade remains in effect, as the economic pressure is being felt inside of Iran. The economic situation is much worse than previous years. If we take inflation into account, it may have nearly doubled. Incomes have fallen, and the value of our currency has declined. All of this has an impact, and life has become a bit more difficult. As US and Iranian officials say, diplomatic efforts are ongoing to reach a deal that could end the current escalation. The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen are once again in direct conflict with Saudi Arabia after attacking two Saudi-owned oil tankers last week. The Saudis responded with heavy airstrikes against the Yemen-based proxy group. The Houthis then ramped up attacks on Saudi oil refineries, launching new missiles over the weekend. Days ago, President Trump issued a warning to the Houthis, saying that if these attacks on vessels in the Red Sea continue, that both the Houthis and Iran would pay a military price. There are a lot of moving parts right now in the region, but an ongoing US military buildup continues to give President Trump a variety of options moving forward. Peter. Trey Yingst, thank you. Let's now bring in former CENTCOM Deputy Commander and retired US Navy SEAL Vice Admiral Robert Harward. Admiral.

এখানে আধার নাম্বার বসিয়ে ক্যাপচা বসিয়ে আপনি সার্চ বাটনে ক্লিক করবেন। এবার যদি এরকম শো হয় যে নো রেকর্ড ফাউন্ড ক্লিক হেয়ার ফ্রেশ এনরোলমেন্ট এই ক্লিক হেয়ার অপশনে ক্লিক করবেন। ক্লিক হেয়ার অপশনে ক্লিক করে দেওয়ার সঙ্গে সঙ্গে তারপরে ইকেওয়াইসি পেজ কিন্তু ওপেন হয়ে যাবে। হয়ে যাওয়ার পর তারপরে আধার নাম্বার দেওয়া আছে এবার ভেরিফাই অপশনে ক্লিক করবেন, ঠিক আছে? And so, we went all over, I mean, you name it, everyone's office you can think of, um, and dropped off these books with these leads flagged, and hopefully we'll see... title: How to Tell What's Real and What's AI-Generated on Social Media
transcription: Midnight souls again? Come on, Gus, people are sleeping. Has your social media feed started to look a little off? Tell me I'm not hallucinating right now. Fake celebrity endorsements, news reports, doorbell camera footage and more that all look real at first swipe, but have a certain eeriness. Or maybe you've seen videos that are a bit more overtly fake. Yep, it's really me, Bigfoot. Like the many clips of animals doing seemingly impossible things, these videos generated by AI tools from Meta, Google, OpenAI and more are spreading on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and X at a rapid pace. Every other scroll, it is some AI-generated like influencer. Dubbed AI slop, some of these clips are meant to make us laugh, like Marilyn Monroe here. While others are out to spread misinformation in a world already struggling with claims of fake news. You will be fooled by an AI photo this week, and you probably already have been and you didn't know it. We have not come to terms with what this means for society. Celebrities like Keanu Reeves having to grapple with AI deepfakes. How disconcerting is that for you? Um well, I mean, it's not a lot of fun. Even Al has been the target of AI videos trying to dupe shoppers. Reversing my hypertension in just 3 months. I don't have hypertension. It can be easy to spot the more outlandish AI clips, but what about something more believable? Like a dog cuddling up to a baby, a grandma dancing at a barbecue, or a harrowing bodycam video. I got you. Pull your leg, pull your leg. Even AI fakes designed to make you feel good, to tug on your heartstrings. These videos are turning feeds into a mix of real life content and computer made footage, and some users are tired of it. I don't know what the solution is, but this technology should never have existed in the first place. So how can the average social media user separate fact from fiction? So, we're going to show you what is out there, what is fake. The team at Corridor Digital, a production studio with more than 7 million subscribers on YouTube, put some special people to the test.

title: BREAKING NEWS: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers! | First Take
transcription: We have breaking news here on First Take. According to Shams, LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $80 million deal with a player option. This comes after more than 20 days since he announced that he will be leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to play the next chapter of his career somewhere else. Stephen A., we knew it was coming soon, we did not know it was coming today. Your initial reaction to LeBron joining forces with Jaylen Brown and company in Philly? Shock, because I thought that if he was going back East, he would go home. That he wouldn't dangle his pres- his- his availability in the face of the Cleveland Cavaliers, and then go somewhere else. For him to choose the Philadelphia 76ers, this is a shock amongst shockers. And I think that this speaks to Bob Myers, the for- the architect, the former four-time champion executive for the Golden State Warriors, being in Philly now and having him there, who went out and pulled off a heist as far as most of us are concerned in getting Jaylen Brown. So now you got Jaylen Brown, okay, who's big-time, obviously, with Tyrese Maxey, who's big-time, you got him with VJ Edgecombe, who is uh who shined as a rookie and got tremendous potential. And now you're looking at it, if Joel Embiid is 50%, I mean, if he can give you anything during the playoffs, the Philadelphia 76ers could win the championship. I think this right here puts the Philadelphia 76ers right there with the New York Knicks as the favorites in the Eastern Conference to come out of the East and represent the Eastern Conference in the NBA Finals. That's how big this move is because LeBron is a savant, his basketball IQ is off the charts, and you combine that with the greatness of a Jaylen Brown and a Tyrese Maxey, with the leadership that Bob Myers has emanating from above as the executive for this team. I don't think there's any question, Philadelphia 76ers, I'm shocked by this. The Philadelphia 76ers are now in play to be a championship favorite. You know, one of the top four teams in, San Antonio, okay, Oklahoma City, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers. And not necessarily in that order. They're the top four teams.

title: President Donald Trump speaks with Jenny Taft ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup™ Final
transcription: Mr. President, thank you so much for your time. Thank you. Hard to believe that the FIFA World Cup is coming to an end. You played such a role in bringing it here. What have been the highlights for you? Well, I think my first meeting with Gianni. He's fantastic, the job he's done. And he had this idea and I said, "That's crazy, we're not a soccer country." And it turns out we are a soccer country. We're a football country, but we don't want to get it confused. But, uh, I don't think there's ever been anything like what's happened with, uh, the whole World Cup. It's been beautiful. It's a beautiful thing to watch, and I really give Gianni the credit. It has been so special to see fans from around the world fall in love with our country, with America. How proud does that make you? Well, I watched it started with Scotland, and all of a sudden, they're doing things that nobody's ever seen with the bagpipes, and it was beautiful, and it just went to every country. And they're realizing what a great country this is. Uh, we're the hottest country in the world right now for, this helped, but for a lot of other reasons. We have trillions of dollars being spent in the United States. They're coming from all over the world, and they're spending their money here. And we've never had a period of, I call it the golden age of America. It's amazing. Uh, but I'll tell you, the World Cup, uh, you know, this is your deal, right? The World Cup. But the World Cup has really helped. It's been, uh, it's been tremendous. It's gotten the world, the word out, Mm. and nobody thought it was possible. I heard numbers that it's, uh, many times what's ever been done before, so that's great. Uh, you're such a sports fan. We just had UFC at the White House, we have the Olympics coming, and a big one on FOX, the Freedom 250 Indy car race. How much are you looking forward to it? Well, Roger Penske is a friend of mine, and he's been trying to get this race for 25 years, and he's had no luck in Congress. Congress is a tough place. And he said, "I've come here 212 times," or some, some massive number like that, uh, over many, many years, and he always went home empty-handed. He's not used to that. He came to see me. He said, "I saw Trump for 15 minutes, and we had a deal done." And not only done, it's going to be the best track you can imagine, down Pennsylvania Avenue, around the Capitol. That race is going to be something, and I think they have 400,000 people already signed up. And we had UFC, which was their record. They've never done, I think it was the all-time fight record, in front of the White House, at the front door of the White House. And some fights that were incredible. When you look at, uh, those last couple of fights, they were incredible, actually. Back to this FIFA World Cup, I got to ask: Argentina-Spain, Yeah. give me a prediction. Well, I knew you were going to ask, so I thought about it very, very, I thought about it a lot. I knew that was a question. I hate to get involved, even though, politically, it doesn't matter so much. Uh, the head of Argentina's a friend of mine, he's done a terrific job. But, I would say that it's hard to bet against Messi. I watched that pass, I guess you'd call it a pass, it was exactly perfect. title: Trump VOWS to strike Iran ‘VERY HARD’
transcription: President Trump warning the Iranian regime that it will hit them very hard if Iran doesn't come to the table and strike a deal to end the war. Trump says those strikes could happen as soon as this weekend. And Trump's renewed threat comes as Iran has launched a new wave of attacks against US military bases in the Middle East. The US military, in response, maintaining that naval blockade against Iranian ships. CENTCOM says so far they have redirected 30 vessels. Meanwhile, Iran is threatening to attack US and Israeli energy infrastructure if the US launches that next round of strikes. And this morning, the US Embassy in Jerusalem says US citizens in the region should consider leaving. Alex Hogan is in Bridgewater, New Jersey with more. Alex? Hi Brian, so the White House says that a new round of strikes could take place on Iran as early as this weekend, and that it would last at least several days. The president is here in New Jersey at his golf club this weekend. Yesterday, he was at Camp David, where he held the first ever televised cabinet meeting there, pointing to a renewal of heavy strikes, signaling that there is no off-ramp to this conflict yet. We're in there for five months, you know, I know people like to say because we did a much bigger job, much more important job than we originally anticipated. So we're in there for five months, and if you look at Vietnam, they were in there for 20 years. You look at Afghanistan, they were in there for many years. Democrats argue the longer this goes on, the list of Iranian threats only continues to grow. Remember he said help is on the way? Um, getting rid of their proxies. The Houthis are still shooting, in fact, they're more engaged than ever. We have a younger, angrier Ayatollah 2.0 in charge of the country now, permanently ending any path towards a nuclear weapon. Meantime, new efforts to end the conflict between Israel and Hamas. President Trump says the US and Israel are aligned on plans. I suspect it will. I mean, there is no evidence that the Iran regime, which is essentially being controlled by the IRGC, um, that this is the radical element of the military. They have been given no indication, they've been tapping the president along. We've seen that every time the president is hopeful that because of his threats, that there will be some breakthrough in negotiations, that the Iranians just continue to fire on again in the strait. I think that we're at a point, Mike, where we really need to get Admiral Cooper, the head of of the operations, in front of President Trump to say, "Look, Mr. President, there are risks in in escalating this military conflict, but I can mitigate those risks and give the president those options," because I do think expanding the number of targets, including energy infrastructure, you got to hit the things that the IRGC does not want us to hit, and that's exactly what it is.
I want to play a clip from retired Brigadier General Mark Kimmitt, and then I'll get you to weigh in.
Patience is what the Iranians are using against us. They hear about we need to, we don't like forever wars, we want to get out of this quickly, we want to get this done quickly. But that's not how you defeat the Iranians. You defeat the Iranians by going patience against patience. If you say we want to get this done quickly, they'll just strap in their seat belts and say, we win by not losing. We can take the bombing, you'll leave, and we'll have what we want.
Jake, what's your assessment of where we are in this conflict?
Mike, for the United States, this conflict is a strategic distraction. For the Iranians, it's an existential conflict. So, you have an asymmetry between what's really important for both sides. And that means that Washington is concerned with bigger issues like China, Russia, the Ukraine war, the economy, the Indo-Pacific. Uh, Iran, the regime, is just trying to stay alive. It's trying to survive. So, the problem that we have here is the United States right now is trying to accomplish three strategic objectives that don't necessarily reinforce each other. It's trying to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, it's trying to eliminate Iran's nuclear program, and it's also trying to prevent escalation of a broader war in the Middle East. All of those objectives don't necessarily fit nicely together. And in fact, sometimes they actually work against each other. That's why strategic messaging is so important, and this back and forth about imminent attacks coming and then pulling it back for a potential deal are not helpful. title: Trump needs to 'FINISH THE JOB' with Iran, Rep. Crawford argues
transcription: Right now, the investigation is underway into cyber attacks at water systems in at least seven states, including Minnesota. Some utilities now forced to switch over to manual operations, but President Trump is rejecting the idea that Iranian hackers are behind these attacks. The president is blaming instead Minnesota and its governor Tim Walz despite federal agencies days ago warning that Iranian hackers were targeting the same kinds of systems. We'll talk about nuclear, and we'll be in there talking about nuclear for 7 hours, I say why is it, why do you need 7? You can take 10 minutes, you have 5 minutes he said so. But 7 hours, and then they'll go out, and I'll say they discussed nuclear, and they'll go out and they'll say we never discussed nuclear, and I'll say why, why do they say that? All they do is make me angry, you know, they just make me angry. President Trump there, reportedly ordering a fresh round of strikes on Iran that could start as soon as today or tomorrow. For more, let's bring in House Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford. Chairman, thank you so much for joining us. You bet. Um, I want to ask you about what we might see happen over this weekend. We are waiting to find out if strikes are imminent. What do you think the president should do with Iran? Well, I think he should finish the job quite frankly. I think what we see here is, he has given them tremendously leash diplomatically speaking, and it's been met with complete disrespect, as you heard him say, he talks about nuclear disarmament and then they come out and say we never discussed nuclear disarmament. I believe that President Trump is giving them every opportunity diplomatically to resolve this issue and they refuse. So, there's really nothing more to do. I think that the red lines have been crossed, he's given them every opportunity and they're showing no willingness to do it. So, I support the kinetic action that's being undertaken now. There's also this idea that potentially striking them hard in one big wave would do us better, especially because there's these reports out. I'm sure you've seen of our missile defense missile capabilities, a shortage of those stockpiles when it comes to the THAADs and the Patriot missiles. This is a Wall Street Journal op-ed. I want to read to you here. They write "If the US really is running out of missiles and interceptors, that should be a 5 alarm fire. Mr. Trump should be calling on Congress to skip its recess and do something about it immediately. But if the missile gap is being floated for political purposes by officials who want Mr. Trump to stand down, then the president should banish those voices from the Situation Room."

Orders have already been given. Despite the tensions, Iran's state media says the regime's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is in Oman for negotiations. His focus is reportedly on the safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Araghchi saying, Iran has so far kept its word unlike the so-called US Treasury Secretary who is violating paragraph nine of the MOU. That violation follows other violations and missteps by the United States. Reality check, there can only be mutual compliance. Iran's state media is also reporting the Supreme Leader will issue a message in the coming hours regarding the funeral of the late Ayatollah Khamenei. Charlie, Rachel and Griff. All right, Madeline. title: DETAILS: US deploys laser tech against Iranian drones
transcription: Iranian Shahed drones pose a real threat to US forces and our Gulf allies, so the Pentagon is now deploying new laser technology to help take them down. Brian Llenas joins us live from our London bureau. Good morning, Brian. Good morning, Lawrence, Ainsley, and Brian. You know, the US Navy is equipped with two laser systems that are capable of taking down these Iranian drones, the ODIN and the HELIOS. Now, the ODIN was spotted in a CENTCOM video that was released at the beginning of Operation Epic Fury on board the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer. You can see it there in that box. Now, the ODIN blinds drones, firing an infrared beam that overwhelms drone sensors, causing it to crash or fail. There are at least two destroyers in Epic Fury that are equipped with the ODIN. Now, the HELIOS is a high-energy laser beam with a high-powered sensor that tracks, blows up drones and missiles in the air by igniting the fuel. Now, the HELIOS is not confirmed to be deployed in Epic Fury. It's only known to be on a US ship that was last seen in the Indo-Pacific in Japan. Now, these technologies are vital in defending against Iran's drone attacks. Iran has fired off four times as many Shahed drones as ballistic missiles attacking our Gulf Arab allies. Now, Iran's biggest advantage is that these drones cost $35,000 to make, but one Patriot missile fired to shoot down these drones costs $4 million per missile. Now, these laser technologies cost pennies per shot and perhaps they're part of the reason why the US says it is not concerned about running out of munitions in this war. title: Why Christopher Nolan shot "The Odyssey" on IMAX film

The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar, Dunkirk, and Oppenheimer. With each new film, the scale and ambition of Nolan's storytelling seems to reach new heights. So, it's only fitting that his latest coming to theaters this July takes on a nearly 3,000-year-old Greek epic, The Odyssey. Let's go! Matt Damon plays King Odysseus in The Odyssey. This is his third film with Nolan. I think what separates him from other directors is the stories he wants to tell are incredibly ambitious and the way he wants to tell them is incredibly ambitious because he wants to do it all in-camera. In this case, he wanted to do it 100% in IMAX, which had never been done. And that wasn't even announced because we didn't know if we could do it. The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely with IMAX film. Each frame has resolution or image quality up to three times higher than digital. Action! The IMAX camera has to stop and be reloaded every two and a half minutes or so. Thank you. Because the format is so large, that's the most film the camera can hold at one time. title: EA SPORTS FC 27 | Official Gameplay Deep Dive
transcription: More player control, more fluidity, and more changes led by you. There's so much that's new to gameplay this year. We addressed AI defending, reinvented corners, reworked attacking runs, dribbling under pressure, and fluid one-twos. And of course, retuned fundamentals to reduce intercept-backs, rebalance play styles, and deliver on more of the improvements you care about most. Let's dive in, starting with something you've called out over and over: AI defending. Your feedback is clear: manual defending should be the best way to stop your opponent. So we've tackled that from a number of angles this year, taking power away from the AI and giving it to you when you are defending. You'll feel the difference as soon as you take control. Your player will jockey more responsively. You'll also have a larger tackling range, a larger interception range, and a larger blocking range when defending manually. For example, the AI isn't quick enough to cut off the angle and can't quite reach to make the interception. But when you take control, that quicker jockey can get you into position and you're able to reach farther to win the ball. We've also minimized AI auto-tackles in competitive gameplay. The AI will still be able to win the ball if your opponent dribbles right into them, but they'll almost never lunge for the ball or reach into a challenge. And, we've loosened teammate contain and team press in the defensive third. The AI will still get into solid defensive positions, but taking manual control will give you more tools to stop your opponent. We've also reinvented corners to reduce luck and continue to reward skill. In FC 25, corners are split into two phases. One to prepare your pass and one that gives you creative control over your run. Pick your spot and power up your cross. Then, you'll have a few seconds to lose your marker so you can time your run to arrive at the perfect moment. This unlocks so much set-piece creativity, and equal amounts of set-piece chaos we see in leagues around the world. In attack, you'll have more control over how your

transcription: Here we go! Yan ang pwersa na taglay! Grabe ito mga idol. Apat na beses pinabagsak ni Fajardo ang isang knockout artist sa loob lang ng isang minuto. Out of Agusan del Sur, Philippines. It's Miel Fajardo. Yabuki Masamichi! Laging sundan, huwag magpapahuli, pag-usapan ni Pakbakan. mga idol, tapos na ang paghihintay dahil may isa na namang Pinoy boxer na lalaban para sa World Championship. At hindi ito ordinaryong challenger, tahimik siya sa labas ng ring, hindi mahilig magsalita pero kapag nagsimula na siyang umatake, sunod-sunod ang bumabagsak. Mayroon siyang 14 na panalo at 12 rito ay tinapos niya sa knockout kaya huwag kayong mapalinlang sa kanyang tahimik na kilos dahil sa sandaling tumama ang kanyang malakas na kaliwa, maaaring matapos agad ang laban. Nice! Oh! What a huge knockout! Ngayon nakatakda siyang lumaban para sa IBF World Championship pero para maging kampeon, kailangan niyang harapin ang isang tunay na knockout monster. Ang kampeon mula Japan, Masamichi Yabuki, dala ang 20 na panalo, 18 rito ay knockout, galing siya sa matagumpay na depensa kontra kay Felix Alvarado at dala rin niya ang anim na sunod-sunod na knockout victories kaya sa papel, malinaw na si Yabuki ang paborito, mas beterano, mas subok at siya ang may hawak ng championship belt. Dahil dito maraming nagsasabing dehado si Fajardo pero hindi ito ang unang pagkakataon na minaliit ang Pinoy at kapag underdog ang "Silent Assassin", mas lalo siyang nagiging mapanganib. Yan ang pwersa na taglay! Tingnan na lamang ang ginawa niya kay Tobias Jeremias Reyes, isang Argentinian knockout artist na may 18 na panalo at 16 na knockout. Nagtapat sila sa isang IBF title eliminator.

title: My name is Ryan, and I am in recovery. Continuing my work story and path to addiction. #recover

transcription: My name is Ryan, and I'm in recovery. Um, yeah, this is now part three of the work cocaine. Sorry, I didn't realize it would go on for so long. But yeah, I stayed in that job as kind of head of music overseeing the nine venues and the 25 staff for right up until COVID. Um. Just before COVID, things were definitely kind of ramping up in terms of my using. I was more and more so kind of going to work with no sleep and kind of just about functioning. The job itself, it's kind of interesting. Once now that I was kind of head of the department, I could almost kind of like not work as hard and hide it. Like, you know, you've when you're kind of doing the bookings, like booking the DJs or you're promoting the show, your work is visible, because, you know, if you don't book the DJ, there's no show. If you don't promote the show, there's not enough ticket sales. So, you can't really hide in that regard. But, my my kind of role now as kind of the head of the team was to more just oversee. Like, I would sign off programming ideas, I would sign off artwork, I would sign off marketing campaigns. I wouldn't actually be doing them myself, I'd just kind of be overseeing everything and kind of keeping the the wheels oiled. Um. And, I don't know if that necessarily suits me, like, kind of job. I feel like that I need that kind of creative input directly from myself to kind of give me that feeling of purpose. And, yeah, during this period, I was just not really enjoying my job, I was using a lot. I was using a lot at home. I had a flatmate, but I'd often just kind of come home and go into my bedroom and just use all night and go to work. It was pretty bleak. Um, COVID then came and all the venues closed. There was obviously lockdown, I got put on furlough. Um, not long after that, I had to furlough... Sorry, I had to make all of the staff redundant. Me and one other guy had to do all the redundancies over Zoom calls, which was brutal. You know, a lot of these people I'd worked with for many years and I considered a friend. So, to have to do that was really challenging mentally. Um. At the time, I was actually engaged to my ex and we were planning our wedding and we were also kind of saving for the future to like buy a house and stuff like that. And I remember asking my boss, "Do, you know, is there any chance that I'm going to be made redundant? You know, because I'm that's going to really put me in a difficult situation." And, and the words he said to me, I can still remember now. He said, "If the ship..."

title: I Needed A Healing Trip | My Christmas Retreat in Myrtle Beach Saved Me🌊| Day 2 out of 5

transcription: Okay, beautiful people, hey. So, it is day two of me raw dogging life out here in Myrtle Beach. I am feeling really good. The weather was probably like 50, 55°, but I went to the jacuzzi and it was amazing. And then we went out to eat and just chilled for the rest of the day. Today we went to the gym, my sister and my father, and I am headed to the pool again by myself. And checking my surroundings here. But yeah, I'm about to have a good time. The weather is much better today. It is going to be like 63 or so degrees at the highest, but yeah, I'm just trying to see what life has to offer me in this time of processing. Does my heart still hurt? Absolutely. You know what I'm saying? But I feel better. I'm also kinder. Being kinder and working on being kinder to myself. I had to have a conversation with myself because I said like, "Friend, if you love me, why do you keep pushing me down when I'm like, not all, not okay already?" Like, so like why do you keep reminding me of things I don't want to remember, okay? And so then I had to look at it in a non-judgmental way and say, "Okay, well, that's something that's bothering me, so let me process it." So anyway, this is day two. I got like five more of these things, okay? But I'll see y'all later. Peace.

title: Katseye FINALLY speaks up about Manon’s HIATUS, BECAUSE…

transcription: Did you notice Manon was secretly performing at Coachella? What really happened behind the scenes of Pinky Up? And what tragic moments during Katseye's performance have never been talked about? Stay until the end to know the truth. Katseye finally spoke up about Manon's hiatus. And what they revealed shocked everyone. After Manon's hiatus announcement, all other members stayed silent whenever anyone asked about her. Even during the Pinky Up promotions, the members declined to answer additional questions about Manon, but something strange happened. During their interview with Zane Lowe, a head of Coachella, he asked what it felt like to rehearse and perform without Manon. And Sophia finally answered it. She said Manon has been on hiatus and they love her so much. They know she is doing well. And at the end of the day, they all just want each other to win together. You know, Manon has been on hiatus, and we love her so much, and she's... we know that she's doing well. But that's not all. Lara added that Manon will be their sister forever and they just want to give her whatever space and love she needs. But if you look closely at the girls' faces, they looked genuinely sad when talking about it. And that kind of reaction only makes it clear that they truly miss her. But there is a bigger reason behind Manon's hiatus that they can't share yet. But while the members were showing their love for Manon, she went ahead and did something that shocked everyone. Did you notice Manon secretly performed at Coachella? After Manon announced her hiatus in February, she was nowhere near any Katseye activities. And when Coachella came, she did not appear there either. But something shocking happened. During weekend two of Coachella, PinkPantheress brought Manon on stage as a surprise guest. When someone is on hiatus for health reasons, they're not supposed to be performing on stages, especially at one of the biggest music festivals in the world. Even crazier, Manon showed up not just once. During both weekend one and two, she was also spotted watching Sabrina Carpenter's and Justin Bieber's performances, which happened on the same night that Katseye performed. So if Manon is healthy enough to be at Coachella across both weekends, what is actually stopping her from rejoining Katseye's stage? Make sure to comment with red hearts if you want Manon back. title: Creative Reminder: The Video Journal Entry
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What's up, everybody? Happy New Year. This is the first video of 2026. I'm so happy to be back on the camera. And in this video, I just really wanted to come on here and, in a way, create and post this, almost like a journal entry for myself, to like reflect on in July, and even in March, or towards the end of the year, to not give up on my work. And I really wanted to share that with you all as well. I want this to be a sign for you to not give up on your goals, your ideas, your content, your projects. And not just keep them up here, and to actually manifest them, put them out into the real space, and to really go from ideation to creation. And a lot of times, my ideas don't make it out of the basket, which is right here. They just stay in here. And then, sometimes, when I get in my moods and I reflect on that, I get sad because it's like, "Damn, I really be having some really good, dope ideas." And sometimes I get in my head because I'm like, "I don't know where to start," or, "This may be too big of a project," or, "I don't have help," or just letting things clog my brain. But I'm blessed to have community, God, just people around me who really want to see me win. And sometimes, even if I don't see it for myself, I'm happy to have those people to like remind me of who the heck I am, okay? Sometimes you need that, and I have that, and I need to be thankful for that. But I also want to be able to use that momentum to like, yeah, girl, you may have clients, you may have other people who want to work with you, or life hits hard, you know, but don't give up on the creation of everything, whether that's to intentionally rest, to read, to pause. It's like I don't want to give up on me. Like, even with right now, like creating this video, um, it's raining outside, I'm hungry, but I was like, "What better way to do it now? Your makeup's done, you got your camera, you got your lights, you got this." It's like, let's just do it, okay? Just do, because the more you do, the more you practice, the better things become. Ooh, hallelujah. Mmh. I'm challenging myself to show up

title: Diary Entry Writing | Minor Discourse 2.1 | Class 10 SSC English | LMR
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hey everyone, and welcome. Today, we're going to crack one of the easiest questions in your English exam, a question that can absolutely guarantee you full marks if you just know the secret. I know how stressful exams can be, but what if I told you there's one question that's not a trap, but actually your secret weapon for getting those marks in the bag? That's right, we are talking about the diary entry. Seriously, this can be the easiest question on the entire paper, but only if you know the simple formula that combines a little bit of format with a whole lot of feelings. So, what exactly is the diary entry? Well, think of it like you're just talking to yourself on paper. It's all about pouring out your personal feelings and what you've experienced. And because it's personal, it's always written in the first person, you know, using words like I, me and my. Okay, you ready for this? Let's dive into what I call the golden formula. It's like a simple, unbreakable code for success that's going to get you easy marks right from the start. All you have to do is memorize these five letters: D, D, T, S, B. That's it. It stands for Date, Day, Time, Salutation, and Body. This structure is your key. I mean, you'll literally be scoring points before you've even written a proper sentence. Okay, so let's break down that first part, the format. And honestly, this is where you're going to get the easiest marks in your entire exam. It is just this simple. At the top left of your page, you write the date, the day and the time, just like you see here. That's it. Boom. Instant marks in your pocket. The salutation is just as easy. You always, and I mean always, start with Dear Diary, followed by a comma. Don't try to get creative here. This is the way. All right, with the format locked in, let's move on to the most important part, the body. This is where you actually tell your story, and it's where your feelings are going to earn you the big marks. Now, you don't need to write a whole novel here. Just keep it short and focused. Two or three paragraphs is perfect. And in those paragraphs, you just need to do three things: describe what happened, express how you felt about it, and explain your reaction. And here it is, the most crucial point of all: you have to use emotional words, words like happy, sad, excited, nervous, proud. This is what separates a pretty good answer from a perfect, full-marks answer. So remember this: feelings equal full marks. Okay, enough talk. Let's actually put this all together. We're going to build a perfect, full-marks entry step-by-step, and you'll see just how simple this is.

He provides a step-by-step guide on how to write a diary entry for an English exam to achieve full marks. He introduces the acronym "DDT SB" (Date, Day, Time, Salutation, Body) as a formula for success, explaining the layout on the page and the importance of using emotional words in the body to convey personal feelings. The background has very low noise, ensuring the speaker's voice is highly audible and easy to understand.
