title: Dear Leese | Loneliness [Visual Diary Entry #1]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I think that there is a loneliness epidemic. Loneliness is definitely something that's universal but not really talked about. And, it's interesting because a lot of people describe themselves as outcasts. But if everyone's an outcast, doesn't that mean that everyone is technically left out? So, it kind of made me think about my past, and it was really hard for me not to equate loneliness with being alone. I actually had a pretty tough time with making friends. Um, as social as I am and extroverted as I am, I felt like I was wasn't liked for who I was. And, that made me feel like no one wanted to be my friend, like no one enjoyed me genuinely, like me being myself. So, it made me shameful and embarrassed to be alone. So, in order to protect myself, I decided to reject them. I didn't want them to reject me. So, if they left me out, I would just block them entirely and kind of put myself in a position where it's like, "I'm going to be a loner by choice so then I don't have to get hurt by you." So, growing up, I used to be a competitive swimmer, so I used to swim two times a day, 2 hours in the morning, 3 hours at night. And, it was kind of insane, but it was pretty ironic that I didn't have a friend group or felt like I belonged in the swimming community, even though I say saw the same people like 5 hours a day. I think, eventually, I started to feel embarrassed about not having friends because I based my value as a person as how much I was able to make others happy. Because I was so scared of being rejected, I just kind of stayed on my own and thought that this would be best, um, just out of fear, I guess. I think I had a longing to belong somewhere. In high school, um, and even like a little bit of college, I never had a friend group

title: QUIET ORBIT | A Depression Anthem | Official Lyric Video
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I stop picking up the phone, stop explaining where I go. Every crowded room gets smaller till there's no more left to breathe. Too many voices hit at once, every sound becomes too much. I can feel my patience burning before I know what set it off. So I leave before I say something angry I didn't mean. I go quiet, close the distance, keep the damage far from reach. They call it cold from where they stand, but no one ever asks me why. Did you ever think I just disappear to stay in control? Did you ever ask what the noise was doing to my soul? I need a room where the world goes still, where nobody pulls at what I can't give. I need the space to come back down whenever every voice becomes too loud. Don't mistake my distance for goodbye, I still care from the other side. And if you've ever had to disappear just to feel your lungs again, I know why you choose the distance.

title: Diary Entry Writing for Class 7 | Full Explanation
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hello my dear students, aaj hamari English ki class mein rehne wali hai diary entry. Diary entry kya hoti hai? Diary entry hoti hai jo bhi aapke sath poore din mein vyateet ho chuka hai, usey aap ek diary mein likhein pratidin, aur ek format ke sath. Usey kehte hain diary entry. Toh aajiye aaj hum iska format samjhenge jo ki diary entry ko sahi tarike se likhne ka dhang hota hai aur isse aap exam mein full marks paa sakte hain. Aajiye format padhne ke liye. Date, Date jis din aap apni diary entry ko likh rahe hain, usi din ki yahan pe date daal denge. Uske baad day, aap isse milaan karke rakhiye, check karke rakhiye ki is din jo bhi date hai usi ka day hona chahiye. Time, jis samay aap likh rahe hain, woh time likhenge is par, jaise ki 9:00 baje abhi aur is par p.m. aur a.m. lagana mat bhoolna, jaise shaam ko likh rahe ho toh p.m. laga dena, subah likh rahe ho, subah ke samay mein toh a.m. laga dena. Uske baad aayega apna line space, line space aap exam sheet jo aapki rehne wali hai usme line space mat likhna L.S. karke, kyunki ispe aapke number cut sakte hain, teacher samjhega pata nahi kya bawal cheez likh di isne. Aap is jagah ek line chorr doge, maine aapko samjhane ke liye yahan pe L.S. likh diya hai aur line space, isliye aap ek line chorr dena single. Uske baad aap daaloge, Dear Diary, pyaari diary, aapki diary hai toh pyaari hi rehne wali hai. Uske baad aayegi hamari heading, heading jaisa aapka question rahega us hisab se aap apni heading daal denge isme. Phir aa jata hai hamara content, content bhi question ke hi... question se hi nikala jata hai content, jaisa ki aapko question diya gaya hai usi hisab se aap apna content likhenge. Content mein hamesha I ka use hota hai, woh ki aati hai first person mein, first person I ka use karoge aap hamesha content, kyunki aapki diary hai, aap khud likh rahe ho, kisi aur se toh likhvaoge nahi, khud likh rahe ho toh I ka use karoge diary mein toh I ka use karna hota hai. Uske baad aa jata hai, isme tense ka kaunsa use karna hai? Isme tense use hota hai past indefinite, aap poochoge ab ki past indefinite kyun hota hai? Past indefinite isliye hota hai kyunki aap jo diary mein likh rahe ho, woh pehle beet chuka hai, aapke sath woh ho chuka hai woh likhoge aap.

title: Are You Happy?

transcription:
They ask me are you happy
Like it's something I should know

Or let something good go

title: Carry My Soul - Meditation Music • Authentic Living • Mindfulness • Personal Growth

transcription: Barefoot on the stones, drawing in my palms. I fold my worry into a small gold coin. The river says go slow, the pine trees lean in. I hear a soft yes under my skin. Oh, lift me. Oh, carry me. A holy hush in the reeds, a silver thread between you and me. Carry my soul. Carry my soul. Spirits stay close. Carry my soul. I hum with the sky. You answer me low. Spirits stay close. title: Unexpected Clarity  A Prison Memoir of Mental Liberation #journeeman #prisonlife #mindfulness
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
I've got something to say,
something that sticks in my throat like iron.
I miss my prison cell.
Not the wires, not the count, not the smell of bleach and sweat and locked metal.
I don't miss West Wing tier,
I don't miss Seg unit,
I don't miss cell 68.
I love my wife, my kids, my desk, the open sky when I step outside.
If you handed me the keys tomorrow and said 'Go back,' I'd burn them.
But listen,
there's a part of me that still walks those three meters by two and a half,
that still feels the quiet drop when the unit locks down.

Picture it.
Green door, heavy bolt,
grey vinyl-covered cabin wood,
tiny desk, bench that bites your spine, bed thinner than regret, toilet right there, no hiding.
Sink, small curtain with its ten-centimeter rule so they can always see you breathing.
Church guitar leaning against the wall like it's waiting for permission to sing, that's it.
That's the whole kingdom. And yet, when the day died and the televisions faded to mumbles, some footsteps echoed and then stopped, that box became still.
No notifications,
no opinions screaming from screens, 
no endless choices pretending to be freedom,
just me
and my mind.
They controlled everything else.

Time,
light,
movement,
who I spoke to,
when I ate,
when I pissed. Razor wire outside, laughing at the sky. But the mind, they couldn't touch it.
In that cage, my thoughts got room to stretch, to roam, to question everything I ever preached from a pulpit, to sit with doubt instead of burying it under sermons. Meditation wasn't an effort, it just happened like breathing,
like the fan humming, low light when the heat creeping through the pipe, a summer sweat turning the air to soup. I'd joke with the boys heading back to my chalet, make them laugh, 'it's a bloody cell, Malcolm.' Yeah, I'd say.
But tonight, it's my university.

title: David Wilcock’s Last Words REVEALED: UFO Expert’s 911 Call EXPOSES Hidden Struggle Before Death
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The final moments of David Wilcock are now coming into focus, and they paint a deeply troubling picture. According to reports from TMZ, Wilcock made a 911 call on Monday morning, just hours before his death. During that call, he spoke about serious financial problems and ongoing health issues. At one point, he told dispatch, quote, "I need to leave, I will be to the left of the house." Authorities say he refused to clarify whether he was armed or planning to harm himself. Dispatchers, meanwhile, treated the situation as urgent. In audio obtained by TMZ, officers can be heard describing the situation in real time, labeling it a potential suicide. Moments later, the situation escalated. As deputies arrived at his Colorado home, they approached with caution. The threat level was unclear, and backup was called in. Just before officers reached him, Wilcock said something else, quote, "I'm sorry to put you through this." And then, he hung up. Seconds later, deputies saw him outside the residence with a gun to his head. They took cover immediately, issuing commands to drop the weapon. But then, a single gunshot rang out. Authorities say Wilcock shot himself in front of responding deputies. No one else was found on the property after a search. He was pronounced dead at the scene. He was 53. Now, with details from that final call emerging, the tragedy surrounding David Wilcock is being seen in a new light, one shaped by personal struggles that remained largely hidden until the very end.

title: Assam Floods 2026 Explained: Why Is the State Drowning? | Current Affairs |  Drishti IAS
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: दोस्तों, परिस्थितियां सबके लिए एक जैसी नहीं होती और दूसरी बात यह कि प्रकृति से ज्यादा ताकतवर कुछ नहीं होता। यह बात असम के मामले में बिल्कुल सही साबित होती हुई दिखाई दे रही है। 12 से ज्यादा जिले प्रभावित हैं, 70 के आसपास मौतें हो चुकी हैं और 7 लाख से ज्यादा लोग उस असम में बाढ़ से परेशान हैं और अभी भी कई जानों की जाने का डर बना हुआ है और वहां के मुख्यमंत्री तक ने यह कह दिया है कि यह बड़ी चिंता की बात है। इतनी तेजी से बाढ़ पहले असम में नहीं आई थी। तो आखिर असम में इस तरह से बाढ़ अचानक से क्यों आ गई? तेजी से पानी कैसे भर गया? क्या मानसून जो कि बारिश का मौसम चल रहा है, इस वजह से हुआ है? तो क्या सिर्फ बाढ़ आने की जिम्मेदारी पूरी मानसून के ऊपर है या हमारा, आपका या हम जैसे कुछ लोगों का दोष है? चलिए सारी बातों को समझते हैं इस वीडियो में लेकिन सबसे पहले एक जरूरी जानकारी कि आपके लिए एक स्पेशल कोर्स आ चुका है IAS GS फाउंडेशन कोर्स। इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि अगर आप दिल्ली से या नोएडा से दृष्टि आईएएस की क्लास नहीं कर सकते और आप यही वाली क्लास ऑनलाइन करना चाहते हैं तो IAS GS फाउंडेशन लाइव ऑनलाइन कोर्स है। अब इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि 3 साल तक इस कोर्स की वैलिडिटी रहेगी। आप जितनी बार चाहें क्लास को उतनी बार देखिए। स्टडी मटेरियल हार्ड कॉपी में आपके घर पहुंचाया जाएगा तो आपको पढ़ने में भी मजा आएगा और इसके साथ ही आपको टेस्ट सीरीज प्रिलिम्स और मेंस की मिलेंगे और उसके साथ ही आंसर राइटिंग की प्रैक्टिस भी कराई जाएगी। इस वजह से यह आपके लिए बड़ा ही फायदेमंद है क्योंकि बेसिक से एडवांस तक सरल भाषा में आपको पूरा GS पढ़ाया जाएगा। आपको इसके बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी चाहिए तो वीडियो के डिस्क्रिप्शन में लिंक है, उसे क्लिक कर लीजिए या सीधे हमें कॉल कीजिए 87501 87501 पर। अब आते हैं हमारे टॉपिक पर। यहां पर सबसे पहली बात हम खबर को समझते हैं कि क्या है। देखिए, 66 से ज्यादा मौतें हो चुकी हैं, आंकड़े बढ़ते जा रहे हैं, 7 लाख लोग प्रभावित हैं, 856 गांव जो कि 12 जिलों के हैं वो प्रभावित हैं और 50,000 से ज्यादा लोग अभी राहत से वंचित हैं यानी कि वहां तक अभी भारत की सरकार या हम कहें असम की सरकार, सेना नहीं पहुंच पा रही है तो वह अभी इंतजार में हैं, ऐसे लोग भी हैं और इसके साथ ही असम राज्य आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण के अनुसार अभी और ज्यादा मुश्किल आने की इस डर बना हुआ है। अब अगली बात आती है कि ये सारी चीजें कैसे शुरू हुई? तो 19 जून को बाढ़ का पानी तेजी से खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है और जब वो खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है तो वो आसपास के इलाकों में बहना शुरू होता है और जिससे तीन सबसे ज्यादा शिवसागर, चराईदेव और जोरहाट, ये असम के ऐसे ऊपरी जिले हैं जहां पे सबसे पहले पानी बढ़ता है। क्यों? क्योंकि पानी ऊपर से ही नीचे आ रहा था तो जो ऊपर के जिले हैं वो प्रभावित होंगे और शिवसागर एक बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण शहर है जो पानी के चपेट में यानी कि बाढ़ के चपेट में आया। कई लोग राहत शिविर में हैं, बहुत सारे काम चल रहे हैं लेकिन मैंने क्या कहा, इंसान प्रकृति के आगे एक छोटा सा खिलौना मात्र है, उससे ज्यादा कुछ नहीं।

transcription: गुड मॉर्निंग भाई लोगों! हाहाहा। तो किन-किन को लगता है कि मैं आप लोगों के कमेंट्स नहीं पढ़ता हूँ? अरे, कैसे नहीं पढ़ता हूँ भाई? रुको। अरे भाई मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ। हाँ, तुम पहले बोल लो। अरे मैं क्यों नहीं पढूंगा आप लोगों के कमेंट्स? अरे मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ गाइस। और अभी जो है, बहुत सारे कमेंट्स आ रहे हैं अलग-अलग वीडियोस के अंदर, अलग-अलग चीजों को लेकर। लेकिन एक कमेंट जो कि आप लोग सबसे ज्यादा कर रहे हैं, वो यह है कि सोनू भाई कहाँ हैं? सोनू भाई का क्या हुआ? तो भाई लोगों, एक बात बताऊं सच्ची-सच्ची? सोनू भाई है ना, उन ग्रेटेस्ट बंदों में से एक हैं जिन्हें मैं जानता हूँ या जिनसे मैं मिला हूँ। सोनू भाई सच में एक बहुत बहुत बहुत अच्छे इंसान हैं। और कमाल की बात पता है क्या? अब तो सोनू भाई ने भी अपना एक नया यूट्यूब चैनल बना लिया है गाइस! हाहाहा! मज़ा आ गया गाइस! तो सबसे पहले तो सोनू भाई को उनके नए चैनल के लिए हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं, बहुत बहुत बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मैं तो आपसे भी यही कहूँगा कि जितना सपोर्ट और जितना प्यार आप लोगों ने आज तक हमारे लिए किया है ना, जितना प्यार हमें दिखाया है, गाइस उतना ही प्यार आप सोनू भाई के लिए भी दिखाइएगा, उतना ही सपोर्ट आप सोनू भाई को भी कीजिएगा। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मज़े की बात क्या है? सोनू भाई भी साइंस के बैकग्राउंड से आते हैं। तो आई होप कि सोनू भाई भी साइंस से रिलेटेड अच्छी-अच्छी वीडियोस आगे फ्यूचर के अंदर लेकर आएं, अच्छे-अच्छे एक्सपेरिमेंट्स करें। तो एक बार फिर से सोनू भाई को बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और गाइस आप लोग भी सोनू भाई को नीचे कमेंट्स के अंदर बहुत सारी बधाइयां जरूर देना, उनके चैनल पे जाकर भी, और ढेर सारा प्यार दिखाना। और गाइस एक बात बोलूं, एक और? देखो, अह मेरा मानना यह है कि हर इंसान को अपनी लाइफ के अंदर अपनी जर्नी, अपना रास्ता, अपनी मंज़िल चूज़ करने का पूरा-पूरा हक होता है। और ऐसा करना भी चाहिए। और जब आदमी है ना गाइस, अपने डिसीजन खुद से लेता है...

title: Noah Kahan - Willing and Able (Official Lyric Video)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Oh, and when I left the room, did you take a deep breath? I stole the beer, drove home, there was only one left. And are you still feeling you're still thinking about that? Wide awake in your room, just seething about that? When I make my fight, I'm the devil. But would I stay the night for a drink? And we stay up and fight about the childhood lie that we both had the courage to leave. I'm within and able. If you want to kick this rock around, if you've got a bone to pick with me. If you've got a flag, plant it in the ground, I'll stay here till morning. Or we can fight like we used to fight, bony limbs, red-faced and teary-eyed. Under the glow of the TV light, I'd be willing and able. Look at you leaving again, it's all you know how to do. Go ahead, take the last of the drinks, the world belongs to you. They all say you're light, all I see is the shadow. And...

title: Steelers select Navy’s Eli Heidenreich in emotional 7th-round moment | 2026 NFL Draft
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: And Eli Heidenreich is here. You see the emotion hitting him. He is Navy's all-time receiver, all-time leading receiver. He was a zero star recruit coming out of high school. Valparaiso, Davidson, Slippery Rock offered him finally, his dream school. Grandfather was a naval officer, his uncle was a Navy corpsman and in the Marines. And Eli, now eligible with the new rules to defer his military service to pursue a career with the Steelers. I got goosebumps right now, Reese. I do. This, going into the draft, this timing is insane. This is my favorite player in the draft. Reese mentioned some of it, a running back, but only by position. The stats and positions right now compare nothing to what we're looking at here. Tears, the Naval uniform, the hat, the theater here in Pittsburgh going absolutely nuts. Hey, he had nearly, nearly 1,000 yards receiving in this Navy offense with stats. Well, Kyle mentioned it, that he had some Navy receiving records. This is my favorite stat of any prospect that we had in the draft. He had six receiving touchdowns in 2024. No player in the Naval Academy's history has ever had more than that. Just six, it's all it takes to make history. Six touchdowns in Navy is like 30 at LSU. Correct. God bless them. He's basically the Jamar Chase of Naval Academy wide receivers. But, what I love is his versatility. He's a runner, he obviously has great speed as well, the versatility here. He was good against good competition when they had those opportunities as well. One of the best players, no hyperbole, to come out of Navy in the last quarter century. What about against Air Force? The 8 catches 243 yards, those are records. Unbelievable, three touchdowns, but he was utilized in different ways they would line him up. Kyle, you watched him. I did. Dynamic. I grew up on the Severn River. The banks of the Severn River, Naval Academy, love the Naval Academy. Beautiful, right? That's right. Nice place, American life, Severn River. It's true. You see him back there, they go out to the slot, he catches it down field. And of all the places, Steelers, the hometown story. God bless these people in the Steelers draft. We're not only clapping, we're saluting. This is really cool, really cool. Really couldn't have scripted it any better too. We still had some picks to go, we still had things to do. But, you want to put an exclamation point on this draft in this city? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I mean, look, this is one of the most iconic cities in, in, in the National Football League. It's just tradition rich. And you saw all the, you saw the, I mean, there was just genuine respect within the Pittsburgh Steelers draft room right there. It does give, gives me goosebumps. This is a great game, this is a great profession that we're involved in.

समझ नहीं आ रहा। है ना? तो बहुत कुछ सिखाने-समझाने की कोशिश करेंगे बट नथिंग इस गोइंग टू वर्क आउट। अगर आप लोग शादीशुदा हैं तो प्लीज जरा सावधान रहिएगा इस समय पे, क्योंकि ऐसा बहुत फ्रीक्वेंटली हो सकता है कि आप कोशिश तो बहुत करें कि चीजें सुधर जाएं, चीजें सही हो जाएं पर वो इवेंचुअली ना सुधरें और ना ही सही हों। नाउ बिकॉज़ ऑफ़ दिस, लाइफ कैन बी अ लिटिल टफ फॉर यू। आप लोग यू नो, हो सकता है कि आप सोचें कि चलो भाई, सामने वाले के लिए कुछ कर दिया जाए, सामने वाले को कुछ रास्ता दिखा दिया जाए, पर उसका व्यवहार आपके प्रति ऐसा हो कि, यू नो, नाउ यू थिंक लाइक ये तो किसी चीज के लायक ही नहीं है, इसके लिए कुछ करने की जरूरत नहीं है। तो, दिस कैन बी अ ह्यूज इश्यू फॉर यू। आपकी कुंडली के पहले घर में शुक्र यानी कि वीनस डेबिटिलेटेड रहेंगे, यानी नीच के रहेंगे, तो इसकी वजह से आप लोग इस महीने खुद पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, अपने प्लेजर्स पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, दूसरों के ऊपर बहुत ध्यान दें, ऐसा हो सकता है। नाउ, अगर आप ऐसी इंडस्ट्री में काम करते हैं जहां दूसरों के लिए आपको बहुत कुछ, यू नो, यू हैव टू डू फॉर देम, फिर तो समझ में आता है, जैसे अगर आप डॉक्टर हैं, आप फार्मासिस्ट हैं, आप लॉयर हैं, जहां पर आपको दूसरों के लिए ही कम्पलीटली अपना जीवन लगा देना है, देन इन दैट पोजीशन थिंग्स डोंट सीम बैड, आपको बहुत ज्यादा काम करने को मिलेगा, आपको बहुत हार्ड तोड़ मेहनत करनी पड़ेगी, दैट विल बी, यू नो, अ वेरी डिफिकल्ट थिंग टू डू। तो, आपको अपने लिए बहुत ज्यादा टाइम नहीं मिलेगा, इनफैक्ट अगर आप सोने की भी सोच रहे होंगे तो नींद में भी आपका काम आपके दिमाग में चल रहा होगा। सो, दैट कैन डेफिनेटली बी एन इश्यू हियर, जिसकी वजह से आप लोग ढंग से सोए नहीं, ढंग से अपने ऊपर ध्यान ना दें। सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के मन में ज्यादा हो सकती है, एक तो सोओगे नहीं, ऊपर से ऑब्वियसली जब सोते नहीं हैं तो ग्रॉगी सा फील होता है, खराब सा फील होता है, तो आपको लगेगा कि अरे यार, कुछ मुझे हो तो नहीं गया? कोई प्रॉब्लम तो नहीं है? तो ऐसी सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के अंदर जरूर देखने को मिल सकती है, उसका आप लोग ध्यान दीजिएगा। डोंट अलाउ इट टू रन योर लाइफ। हालांकि, अगर हम ओवरऑल देखें, तो आप लोग कार्यक्षेत्र में अच्छा कर सकते हैं, ऐसी कोई बहुत बड़ी प्रॉब्लम नहीं है। आप लोग अपना बेस्ट देने की कोशिश करेंगे और जिन भी लोगों के साथ आप काम करते हैं, उनको ये डिफरेंस जरूर महसूस हो जाएगा, दैट यू आर पुटिंग इन मोर देन योर 100% और उसके लिए आपको सर्टेनली अवार्ड्स, रिवार्ड्स जो भी हैं, वो भी जरूर मिल जाएंगे, तो परेशान होने की जरूरत नहीं है। कई बार आपका जो इंट्यूशन है, वो बिल्कुल टॉप क्लास रहेगा, आपको एग्जैक्टली पता रहेगा कि कहां पर क्या करना है और आपके जो सीनियर्स हैं, जूनियर्स हैं, जिनके साथ भी आप काम करते हो, वो इसको जरूर एप्रिशिएट करेंगे।

title: Alysa Liu reacts to winning gold after free skate
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: A script that would have been rejected as far-fetched and a comeback that has brought her all the way perhaps to the Olympic podium. It is like she's just playing on the ice, not even performing anymore. The joy, the passion, and she's figured out how to compete without carrying the weight of it. She stays so loose and completely herself out there. That's the secret every athlete wants to solve. That's what I'm talking about. I can't believe it. Thank you so much. Amazing. Amazing. Those are her right? I can't even believe this. The toe was amazing, the Lutz was amazing. Guys, I don't know if you believe what you've been watching since she made her comeback. But, but through it all, she's just kind of been like, "Oh, this is fun." I've never seen a comeback like it, and I've never seen someone withstand pressure like Alyssa Liu. And she did tell us that it's a whole new world this time around because she doesn't feel like her life is on the line. She has like this nonchalance both to the way she jumps and performs. Triple Lutz, triple toe, very nice second element in the program, and it just got better from there. She is just all sunshine on the ice. If you don't watch her skate and want to get on the ice and just feel what it might feel like to race around the rink, it is childlike, beautiful joy and innocence out there. Quad God loved it. So did everybody else in this arena, including her dad, her siblings, and Alyssa as well. She really couldn't have done better. This has been incredible to watch, 2 and a half years away from competition, Lori.

title: “I Was Genuinely Freaked Out” Curry Barker, Inde Navarrette & Michael Johnston on ‘Obsession’
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hi, I'm Indiana Massara. And I'm Michael Johnston. And I'm writer-director Kirby Barker. Today we're interviewing each other for our new film, Obsession. I love you so, so, so, so, so, so much. A love only the branch of a willow tree could conjure. What was your reaction when you first read the script and how did you feel watching Obsession with a big crowd at TIFF? I got my hands on the script and I said, "What can I do to be a part of it?" Yeah, same. I mean, I loved how it wasn't all black and white. It was very gray and unclear and yeah. And then what was your reaction? How did you feel watching it in the theater at TIFF? A little terrified. Incredible. Yeah. The audience goes nuts. I mean, I could hardly hear the movie because people were screaming and laughing. I've never seen grown men jump in their seats. Because of you. Because of me? Yeah. I love you. I love you. I love you! I love you! Kirby. Yes. Drum roll, please. What was your most challenging day on set and why? Well, I don't want to give anything away, but I would say the party scene was really difficult for all of us that night. I mean, it was just late. It was an overnight shoot, a lot of pages, too. That party scene is just long. It just feels like it goes on and on. A lot of coverage to get, too. Yeah, it's just a lot. We wanted to do some slight reshoots of the party and realized that that, that house actually burnt down in the LA fire, so that exact house doesn't exist anymore. Pretty crazy. So, what we got is what we got, and it's now memorialized in the movie. Go! Indy, how did you prepare for this role and was there one unique or quirky thing that you did to tap into the creepy mode before filming? No, it's inherently inside. It just pops out. It just is there. Effortless. Don't be alarmed, we're home. Preparing the role was really, really fun. I mean, we got to watch a lot of fun movies and kind of pick and choose like a puzzle what we wanted in the film and moments that we took inspiration from and then made them our own. I think Pearl was a really big one. Bless us, oh Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord. Did I ever surprise you with a specific note while filming any of your scenes? If so, what was it and why did it surprise you?

title: Michael Jackson’s son Prince reveals his takeaway watching ‘Michael’ film
transcription: A new movie about Michael Jackson is giving audiences a front-row seat to the King of Pop as never seen before. The biopic "Michael" chronicles MJ's rise to global fame, starting from the discovery of the Jackson 5 to his transition into a solo artist, and fun fact: Jaafar Jackson, who plays Michael in the film, is the late singer's nephew. Let's take a look. I just have all these songs in my head. Gotta get them out. And joining us now is one of the film's executive producers, the eldest son of Michael Jackson, Prince Michael Jackson. Prince, so great to have you on the show. Thank you. Thank you so much for having me. Happy to be here. So your dad having been such a public figure and icon, really, a lot is out there about him already. What can people expect to learn about the King of Pop in this film that they don't already know? I think one of the most magical things about this film is, for those of us that were lucky enough to grow up with the Jackson 5 and the Jacksons, hopefully, it will re-instigate that feeling of nostalgia and fun and family. And for those of us like myself and younger that never got to experience that, I hope that it contextualizes the growth and the rise to stardom and the hard work and effort that my father put into it, my father and my family, and overall just be a really fun, entertaining time for children of all ages from 9 to 90, you know? And I imagine that the making of this film was very personal and tough at times. It was also Jaafar's first acting gig. What was the process like in telling your dad's story? Um, I mean, first and foremost, authenticity is the biggest challenge in any story, and especially my father having such an incredible life that spans five decades of him being at the top of his career, we wanted to approach it from a way that audiences, again, of all ages could understand who he was as a person. We all know the story of the King of Pop, but I think this was our goal, was to tell the story of Michael, how he started from the small home they grew up in in Gary, Indiana, to arrive at the biggest stages and the biggest platforms all around the world. And the research that we started off, when I met Graham King in 2019 and beginning of 2020, sitting down and speaking with various family members or people who worked with him and knew him, and I had heard a lot of these stories growing up. title: What Reading My Old Journal Taught Me About Growth
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I read my journal from a year ago and cried, in a good way. So, I did something kind of embarrassing last week. I went back and read my journal from a year ago and I cried, and I want to tell you why that was actually a good thing. The journal was from about 12 months ago. I'd completely forgotten I even had entries from that period. It was one of those stretches that just kind of blurred by. Nothing dramatic, nothing memorable, just a lot of Tuesdays. But I picked it up on a slow Sunday and started from the beginning. And here's the strange part. I didn't recognize the person writing it, not because they were sad or doing badly, but because I had completely forgotten what that version of me was worried about, what they were hoping for, what felt impossible, and what felt small. And reading it felt like getting a letter from someone I used to know. Some of it was small. I'd written about a coffee that was really good, about being annoyed at someone in a way I couldn't even reconstruct now, about a plan I had that I was nervous about, and looking back, I know it worked out fine, but the version of me writing it didn't know that yet. And that's the thing that hit me. The person writing that entry was doing something really hard without knowing it. They were living through uncertainty with no knowledge of the outcome, and they showed up and wrote it down anyway. That's not a small thing. I don't think I would have remembered any of it if I hadn't written it. Not because it wasn't worth remembering, but because our brains aren't built for this. They compress time, they flatten the details, they remember the outcome and forget the journey. Here's the one that really got me. There was an entry about something I was trying to get better at, I won't go into detail, but it was something I'd been struggling with for a while. At the time of writing, it felt like I wasn't making any progress. But reading it a year later, I knew I had, not dramatically, not in a montage moment

title: How to Start Journaling as a Beginner | Daily Journaling for Self Growth & Mental Clarity
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You open your journal, you pick up your pen, and then, nothing. You stare at the blank page, and you do not know where to begin. Sound familiar? Welcome to ReadUp Daily. Today, we are solving the number one problem every beginner journaler faces: not knowing what to write. And by the end of this video, you will have a simple technique, three powerful words, and a full page ready to write. Let us begin. The technique is called stream of consciousness writing. It sounds complicated, but it is actually the simplest and most freeing way to journal. Here is how it works. You write whatever comes to your mind, no rules, no grammar checks, no perfect sentences, you just write whatever you are feeling, whatever you are thinking, whatever is sitting heavy on your heart right now, you put it on the page, and you do not stop until the page is full. That is it. That is stream of consciousness writing. Now, let us learn three words that will make your journaling more powerful and more expressive. Word one: overwhelmed. Overwhelmed means feeling like you have too much on your mind or too much to handle all at once. Example sentence: Today, I feel overwhelmed, but I know that writing it down will help me breathe again. Write that in your journal. Word two: clarity. Clarity means the feeling of being clear and certain in your mind. When the confusion clears, and you finally understand what you are feeling or what you need to do. Example: Every time I journal, I find a little more clarity about who I am and what I truly want. Write that in your journal. Word three: release. Release means to let something go, to free yourself from a feeling or a thought that has been holding you back. Example sentence: Journaling gives me a safe place to release everything I have been carrying inside me. Write that in your journal, too. Now, let us use stream of consciousness writing together. Do not think, do not edit, just write what you feel as you read along. Ready? Right now, in this moment, my mind feels...

title: Why Paper Journaling Is More Powerful then Digital Journaling
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In a world where we do almost everything on screens, you might wonder: Does it really matter whether we journal digitally or on paper? Surprisingly, it does. Writing in a paper journal can actually be far more powerful for healing, self-awareness, and changing behavior than typing on a screen. In this video, I'm going to explain why writing by hand can create deeper emotional clarity and lasting personal change. Writing by hand engages the brain more deeply. When you write on paper, your brain works differently than when you type. Handwriting activates multiple parts of the brain related to memory, emotion, and learning. Typing tends to be fast and automatic. But writing by hand slows your thinking down. That slower pace allows you to process your thoughts more carefully, which helps you understand your emotions and experiences more clearly. In other words, handwriting helps your brain move from reacting to reflecting. Slowing down creates emotional awareness. Healing starts with awareness. When you journal on paper, the natural rhythm of writing encourages you to slow down and become more aware of what you are feeling. Instead of quickly typing and moving on, you begin to notice your emotions, your thoughts, your reactions, and the patterns in your behavior. This moment of pause is incredibly powerful because you cannot change what you are not aware of. Paper feels more private and honest. A physical journal often feels safer than digital writing. It isn't connected to the internet. There are no notifications, no audience, no distractions. Because of that, many people feel more comfortable writing honestly about things like fears, regrets, anger, sadness, or uncertainty. And that honesty is essential for healing. Your journal becomes a place where you can tell the truth without being judged. The physical act of writing releases emotion. There's also something deeply therapeutic about the physical act of writing itself. The movement of pen on paper can feel grounding and calming. When emotions feel overwhelming, writing them out physically can help release that tension. Many people notice that after writing honestly about something difficult, they feel lighter, calmer, clearer. Sometimes, the page holds emotions that were too heavy to carry alone. Your journal becomes a record of growth. One of the most powerful aspects of paper journaling is that you can see your journey over time.

title: The 5-minute Journal trick that calms panic
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever been lying awake at 2:00 a.m. feeling a physical weight in your chest while your mind races through a tornado of unfinished tasks, looming deadlines and vague anxieties? That sensation signals a specific biological chain reaction taking place in your nervous system. When you perceive a threat, even something as small as a tense email, your brain's threat detection center, the amygdala, fires an alarm and floods your system with cortisol. If this stress stays chronic, neuroimaging shows that your amygdala actually grows larger and more reactive, while your prefrontal cortex, the area responsible for rational executive planning, shrinks and effectively goes offline. To break this cycle, you need a mechanism called cognitive diffusion. By taking those chaotic, swirling thoughts out of your head and translating them into physical words on a page, you force your rational prefrontal cortex to re-engage, which physically turns down the amygdala's alarm system. The worry dump is a structured, analog practice designed to create this distance. It requires putting pen to paper to begin the process of externalization. Grab a physical pen, a piece of paper, and a timer. We are going to walk through this exact process together right now. Moving thoughts onto paper provides a physiological intervention to stall cortisol and reclaim your cognitive control. Step one is to find a quiet, private space where you will not be interrupted. You need an environment where your analytical left brain can focus on the physical act of writing, giving your creative right brain the safety to wander and release everything it's holding onto. Set your timer for exactly five minutes. When it starts, your only job is to write down every single worry, task, and anxious thought currently occupying your mind. Here is the single most critical rule for this phase: you must write continuously. Do not pause to organize your thoughts. Do not prioritize the list. And do not stop to analyze why you are stressed about a certain item. Ignore your inner critic. If you stop to correct your spelling or fix your grammar, you will pull yourself out of the flow and stall the exercise. Keep your pen moving. If your mind suddenly goes blank and you run out of things to say, simply rewrite your last sentence over and over again until a new thought emerges, or until the timer officially sounds. Your output does not need to make sense to anyone else. A single word, a fragmented phrase, or a complete sentence are all equally valid forms of output. Just get it on the page.

title: Why Your Journal Sounds Fake (and how to fix it)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Have you ever written something in your journal, re-read it, and thought, "that sounds absolutely nothing like me"?
Here's a thing that doesn't get talked about enough: most people's journal entries sound like they're being written for an audience. Not a real audience—an imaginary one. Some future version of themselves who's going to judge the quality of the writing. Or worse, some hypothetical person who might one day read it. And so, instead of writing, "I'm absolutely furious, and I don't even fully understand why," you write, "today was challenging, and I'm processing some complex emotions." And then you close the journal feeling like you just filed a report rather than said anything true. This is the invisible reader problem, and it's the actual reason most people find journaling uncomfortable. Not because they're bad at it, but because they're performing instead of writing. So why does this happen? Because we've been trained our whole lives to write for a reader: school essays, work emails, texts to people we want to impress. Everything we write has an audience in mind, and we've calibrated our language to manage how that audience sees us. A journal asks you to do the opposite: write for no one. And that turns out to be genuinely hard, especially at first, because your brain keeps switching into "how does this sound?" mode rather than "what is actually true?" mode. The result is entries that are technically accurate but emotionally hollow. The words are right, but the voice isn't yours, and you can feel it when you re-read it—that slight uncanny valley feeling where you recognize the handwriting, but not the person. Honest journaling sounds a lot like how you'd tell a story to your best friend at midnight: short sentences, incomplete thoughts, words you'd never use in formal writing, repetition, contradiction, starting a sentence and stopping halfway through because you realized something while you were writing it. It doesn't have to be coherent. It doesn't have to conclude anything. It doesn't have to read well. The only job it has to do is be true.

He discusses the concept of the "invisible reader problem" in journaling, explaining how people often write for an imagined future audience rather than being completely honest with themselves. title: The Journaling Practice That Will Change How You See Your Past
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You've probably started a journal at some point and quietly given up on it. A few pages of raw feeling, then silence. You decided writing just wasn't for you. Most people assume that putting pain into words works because it lets something out, but release was never really the point. What actually changes you on the page looks more like construction than release, and it explains why some people write for years and feel exactly the same, while others rewire their relationship to a single memory in four short sessions. In the 1980s, the psychologist James Pennebaker ran an experiment that seemed almost too simple to matter. He asked people to write about their most upsetting, unresolved experiences for 15 to 20 minutes, four days in a row. No structure, no therapist, no feedback, just a blank page and permission to be honest. Some of the people in that study wrote about things they had never told another living person. Health visits dropped in the months that followed. Immune markers improved. People slept better and reported less physical pain, and none of it involved anyone hearing their story out loud. Here is where it gets stranger. Pennebaker and later researchers went back through the writing itself, word by word, looking for what separated the people who improved from the people who didn't. It wasn't how much emotion they expressed. It wasn't how many painful details they included. It was whether their language changed. The people who benefited most were the ones whose sentences shifted across those four days from chaos toward explanation. They started using more words like because, realize, and understand. Their writing stopped being a wound repeated on the page and became something closer to a story with a cause and an effect. That shift has a name in psychology: insight. And it turns out insight, not catharsis, is what your mind is actually rewarded for.

title: Lifestyle Journal: The Playbook For Health, Wealth, Strength and Purpose by Miguel Hernandez
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Welcome to Life Beyond the Covers. I'm Profilla, and today we're diving deep into the world of books to uncover the lessons in stories that stay with us long after we turn the final page. Let's start learning together. Don't forget to like, subscribe, and share. Today we're diving into some incredibly powerful ideas from Miguel Hernandez's Lifestyle Journal. Have you ever felt like you're constantly chasing this fleeting motivation only to completely fall off the wagon just a few weeks later? Trust me, you're definitely not alone. We're going to figure out how to jump off that exhausting emotional rollercoaster and start building bulletproof daily systems instead. We're talking about ditching those quick hacks and really building a true lifestyle architecture. Right out of the gate, Hernandez flips the script with this profound idea: You don't rise to the level of your goals, you fall to the level of your systems. I mean, wow, right? That completely changes the game. It shows us that real transformation isn't about hoping for some magical burst of energy, it's actually about a deep shift in your identity. It's moving from saying, "Oh, I want to be healthy," to "I am someone who prioritizes health." Your identity drives your behavior, and your systems, well, they're the architecture holding that identity up. So here's our blueprint for today. We're going to cover the architect mindset, designing your daily blueprint, the pillars of health and strength, the mortar of wealth, purpose, and connection, and finally, systems for flawless execution and your long-term vision. Let's get right into it. All right, Section 1: The Architect Mindset: Pouring the Foundation. This is where we really have to tackle that crucial identity shift. You've got to stop being a passive passenger in your own life. Think about the stark contrast between motivation and systems. Motivation is just, well, it's an exhausting emotional rollercoaster, isn't it? It's usually sparked by some fleeting event like watching an inspiring video or, you know, making a New Year's resolution. Systems, on the other hand, are your dependable, predictable daily rituals. They are what carry you forward even when you are totally drained. Hernandez really hits the nail on the head here. Small habits repeated daily create massive exponential results. You're basically building rituals that keep running even when your energy is at absolute zero. Moving right along to the floor plan of our lives, Section 2 is all about designing your daily blueprint. Hernandez makes this great point that your day is essentially a microcosm of your entire life. So if you want a well-designed life, you literally have to proactively design your day. Stop reacting to the world and take control with an ideal day flow. It kicks off in the morning, grabbing those early wins for momentum, getting some movement in to prime the brain, and reducing your cognitive load.

title: Top 5 Journaling Practices That Feel Like Therapy for Your Mind (2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever wished you could talk to someone about your deepest thoughts, but didn't know where to start? What if you could do that without saying a word? Journaling offers you a safe space to express your emotions, organize your thoughts, and process everything you're feeling. Whether you're feeling overwhelmed, stressed, or just in need of clarity, journaling can help guide you through it. In this video, we'll dive into the top five journaling practices that can feel like therapy. These powerful methods can help you work through emotional challenges, boost your self-awareness, and even improve your mental health. Let's get started. One, stream of consciousness, brain dumping. One of the simplest, yet most effective journaling practices is stream of consciousness writing, often referred to as brain dumping. The concept is easy to grasp. Take a few minutes and write whatever comes to mind without worrying about structure, grammar, or punctuation. It's all about letting your thoughts pour out onto the page freely. Set a timer for about three to five minutes and just write without stopping. Let your mind flow naturally. The therapeutic benefits of brain dumping are vast. This practice provides a powerful outlet for releasing pent-up emotions and mental clutter. Often, our minds are filled with a whirlwind of thoughts, worries, and stresses that can weigh us down. By putting these thoughts on paper, we get the opportunity to unload all the noise and clear our mental space. The act of writing helps us create an emotional release, allowing for more calm and mental clarity. But the benefits go beyond just relieving stress. Brain dumping can also help uncover hidden thoughts and emotions that we may not have been fully aware of. Sometimes, when we sit down to write, we realize there are lingering concerns or feelings that we've been suppressing. After expressing these thoughts, we often gain new insights into our feelings and situations, helping us look at things from a fresh perspective. It's almost like having a one-on-one conversation with yourself, unraveling those tangled emotions, and leaving you with a sense of peace. Another reason stream of consciousness writing is so helpful is because it's incredibly easy to integrate into your day. You can do this practice anytime you feel over-

title: This Book Made Me Question Everything
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever worked hard, tried everything, read advice after advice, and still felt like you're stuck at the same level while other people keep pulling ahead? What if I told you that the reason you're not where you want to be has nothing to do with talent, luck or intelligence? Today, I'm breaking down the single best self-improvement book that I read in 2025, the one that quietly changed how I think, how I work, and how I win. Here's the thing: The people you admire most aren't smarter than you. They're not more gifted than you. And they didn't magically figure life out earlier. They just learned one mental rule that most people never do. And once you see it, you can't unsee it. This rule explains why some people grow faster every year while others stay frustrated, burned out, and quietly jealous of friends who seem to be passing them by. And if you've ever felt like you're doing the work but not getting the results, you're about to understand why. And if you leave this video early, you'll miss the one shift that made everything else finally start working for me. I want to be clear with you. I've been exactly where you might be right now. Motivated but inconsistent, ambitious but second-guessing myself, starting things, stopping things, and wondering why progress felt so slow. In 2025, I made a promise to myself to read at least one self-improvement book cover-to-cover per month. Not to feel productive, but to find what actually works. Most books were fine, some were repetitive, one stood above all the rest. The book is Mindset: The New Psychology of Success by Dr. Carol S. Dweck. I was so inspired by this book that I created a mindset mastery playlist for the lessons I learned. And today, I'm going to walk you through a simple three-part plan based on this book. First, I'll show you the invisible belief that's holding you back. Second, I'll show how high performers think differently when they fail. Third, I'll show you how to install this mindset into your daily life starting today. Stick with me, because the last part is where most people finally break through. Why most self-improvement fails.

title: Inner Engineering - Book Overview | Between The Lines | Journal
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You know, Sadhguru's Inner Engineering has this central idea that most of us are just living life completely by accident. So in this explainer, we're going to break down his guide for how to take back the controls and really move from that inner chaos to conscious creation. Okay, so the book kicks off with this really powerful paradox, right? Think about it. We have comforts and technologies that kings and queens from just a few centuries ago couldn't even dream of. I mean, we are, without a doubt, the most comfortable generation ever. But here's the kicker, are we the most joyful? The most peaceful? Sadhguru says, not even close. So, what on earth is missing here? Well, that question gets us right to the heart of the problem that the book lays out. It's this huge massive disconnect between the amazing world we've built around us and the, well, often chaotic world that exists inside our own heads. I mean, just look at our external world. We've achieved this incredible level of mastery, right? We've engineered our environment for total control, for maximum comfort. But then, you look internally, and what's going on in there? For most of us, it feels like a total storm of thoughts and emotions. It's accidental. It's reactive. It's completely out of our control. It's like we've perfected everything outside of us, but left our inner world, our inner landscape, totally up to chance. And this points to a really fundamental mistake in how we chase happiness, doesn't it? We're kind of taught that if we just get the right job, the right house, the right partner, you know, fix our external world, then our inner world will magically fall into place. But Sadhguru says, nope. You've got it completely backwards. The quality of your life is not determined by what's happening around you. It's all about what's happening within you. Your entire experience of life, it's generated from the inside out. Okay, so if our inner state is the thing that really matters, that leads to a huge question. Who's in charge of it? I mean, who's actually the director of that movie that's playing 24/7 inside your head? The book tells this simple, kind of funny story to make a really deep point. So, a woman has a dream about this hunk of a man, right?

title: Level Up Your Life: Tracking Personal Growth with the Apprentice-Master Model 📈🛡️
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Tracking personal growth through apprentice, journeyman, master stages. Introduction. We are constantly exploring different paths in our personal development and chasing new quests. Each new search forces us to open the door to fresh knowledge. As this continues, we unknowingly find ourselves buried under piles of information, and when we get stuck, we often don't know what to do next. In this article, I want to draw attention to a method that dates back to the Roman and Hittite states and has helped shape the formation of states that still exist today. Although these organizations were created by states that owed their existence to the labor and effort of their individuals, they actually presented a structure that encompasses the individual's own life cycle. Individuals who found themselves within a ready and continuously developing order integrated into the system very easily, and growth continued uninterrupted. In short, if we want to capture the stability of the ancients while searching for direct sources for our own personal development today, we must learn how they lived and integrate ourselves within an organization suited to that lifestyle. Come, let's look at an example and see how we can adapt our personal growth as apprenticeship, journeyman, and mastery. Our goal is to maintain stability in our lives by making decisions with professional foresight and tracking them through mastery. Historical foundation. Apprenticeship as a liminal stage in medieval English guilds. This structure is most clearly seen in the guild system of medieval England. As Rhiannon Sandy states in her 2022 PhD thesis, Apprenticeship indentures and apprentices in medieval England, 1250 to 1500, apprenticeship was an important liminal stage between childhood and adulthood, during which young men and women were molded into respectable adults. Guild contracts, indentures, clarified everything. The master was obligated to teach the apprentice the secrets of the craft. In return, the apprentice promised to serve bene et fideliter, honestly and faithfully, committing to rules of honesty, confidentiality, avoiding taverns, gambling, and sexual misconduct. The master acted in loco parentis, in place of a parent, and was responsible for the apprentice's moral well-being. This system transformed the individual from a passive learner into a responsible, respected adult, exactly the model of stable growth we seek today. Martin Prak and Patrick Wallis emphasize in Apprenticeship in Early Modern Europe, Cambridge, 2019, that this framework organized both technical and ethical development across Europe. So, how can we, as adults, adapt this

title: The Power of Journaling: How Writing Brings Mental Clarity
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You know, in our crazy, fast-paced world, there's a really simple, almost ancient tool that can make a huge difference in finding some clarity. And that's what we're talking about today: journaling. It might sound simple, but it's one of the most powerful ways to cut through all the noise. So, let me ask you this: does your brain ever feel like a web browser with like a hundred tabs open at once? You're trying to do one thing, but you've got to-do lists, worries, random thoughts, all competing for your attention. It's, it's just exhausting, right? Well, the great news is there is a way to start closing some of those tabs. There's a way to find that clear signal in all the static. And that way? Well, it's journaling. But before we get into the solution, I think it's really important we understand the problem. Why do so many of us feel this way? It really all starts with the state of our modern, and often, very overwhelmed minds. And you know, there's actually some science to back up that feeling of being overwhelmed. Our minds are always, always on. But what's wild is that a huge chunk of that mental energy gets spent on thoughts that are repetitive, unproductive, and sometimes even negative. They just kind of spiral around, causing stress, but never really solving anything. So, how do we get that energy back? How do we point it in a better direction? Well, that brings us to a really simple path forward. And the best part, it doesn't cost anything, and you don't need any special gear. At its heart, this is all journaling really is. It's just this simple act of taking all that chaos swirling around in your head, and giving it some shape on a page. Think of it like having a conversation with the one person who knows you best: yourself. So, what makes it such an amazing tool? Well, for starters, there's literally no barrier to entry. It's free. Plus, it's completely, 100% private. It's a space just for you, where you can be totally honest without ever worrying about being judged. It's just a simple, powerful way to clear out that mental clutter and grow as a person. And hey, this isn't just some feel-good, fluffy idea. There's actually some really solid science that shows just how effective it can be. So, let's take a look at the proof behind the practice. And get this: you don't have to write for hours on end, not at all. Studies have shown that just 15 minutes, seriously, just 15 minutes of writing a day is enough to have a significant, measurable impact on your mental well-being. So, what kind of impact are we talking about? Well, a major analysis of a bunch of studies found that journaling can lead to a real, tangible 9% drop in anxiety symptoms. And the reason it works is pretty cool. When you write your thoughts down, you're literally taking them out of your head. You're externalizing them, which frees up so much mental space. And the benefits go even deeper. That same body of research also showed a 6% decrease in symptoms of post-traumatic stress

title: Why You've Become Hard to Read
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: People used to know what you were thinking. You were a open book. Easy to read. Easy to reach. Somewhere along the way, you changed. Now, people say you're hard to read, quiet, contained, difficult to get to. And part of you wonders if something closed off, if the openness you used to have was better than what you are now. It wasn't. You didn't close, you you learned, and there's a difference. If that feels familiar, stay with me. Becoming hard to read is usually the result of being misread too many times, not one big betrayal, just a a slow accumulation. Moments where you said the real thing and it landed wrong, you were opened up and the other person wasn't careful with it. I did this for years, said whatever I was thinking, assumed everyone operated the same way I did. They didn't. And somewhere in that pattern, I got quieter, not colder, just careful. That's not damage, that's data. Quiet isn't the same thing as as closed. They see someone who doesn't broadcast everything and read it as withholding, as coldness, as something being off. But there's a version of quiet that isn't absence, it's presence that's become more deliberate. You're still there, you're still thinking, feeling, noticing. You've just stopped narrating all of it out loud for people who weren't really listening anyway. There's a kind of openness that isn't actually brave, it's just untested. Early openness is easy, you haven't been burned yet. You don't know what happens when you hand someone something real and they don't handle it well. I overshared constantly in my 20s, thought that that was authenticity.

title: What to Write in a Journal for Mental Health
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In recent years, there's been an uptick in awareness and focus on the importance of our mental health. And I'm here to tell you that I know that one of the tools that is best to help with your mental health and strengthening you and how you think and how you feel is the power of a journal. Let's talk about it. Okay. So maybe this isn't a brand new idea for you, the idea of using a journal on your mental health journey. But what do you write and how can that be helpful for you? Well, if you want to use journaling as a tool for your mental health journey, I want to give you some simple things that you can write down and use and spend time with in your journal that are going to have big dividends and impacts on your mental health. Let me start with the first one. So, first is just to start with, write awareness. What are you seeing? What are you experiencing? What are you feeling? One of the best things that journaling can help us do is to slow down and to notice. It can be tied to or even part of kind of a mindfulness or meditation practice. But when we write it down, then we capture it in a more solid way and it helps us notice things. So, it's very helpful to just notice our feelings. What experiences did we have that day? How did that impact us? How are our relationships right now? What are we noticing that we're feeling off kilter or even really strong and capable and powerful? Just noticing as much as we can and recording that can be very helpful with and using journaling for that. Number two, gratitude. I've talked about this a lot and I'll keep talking about it. Gratitude is one of the most powerful forces that we can have to help us feel better. There's so much research around this and journaling is one of the best ways to do that because you get to write it down, you get to record what you're grateful for and even if you want to go a step further

title: The Smile Nobody Questioned (New Spoken Words 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I got really good at smiling. So good, that nobody noticed the war happening behind my eyes. I laughed loud, showed up, answered messages with "I'm good". Even cracked jokes while my chest felt like it was carrying a thousand pounds of silence. And the scary part is, after a while, even I started believing the performance. See, depression doesn't always look like darkness. Sometimes it looks like being tired all the time for reasons sleep can't fix. Sometimes it looks like staring at the ceiling at 3:00 a.m. replaying every mistake like your mind signed a contract with regret. Sometimes it sounds like, "You're not enough! You're falling behind! Everybody else figured life out except you!" And you begin to drown in thoughts nobody else can hear. That's the thing about invisible pain. People only notice broken bones, not broken spirits. So you learn survival tricks. You become the therapist friend who secretly needs saving. You become the strong one because strong people aren't allowed to collapse. You disappear into music, into work, into scrolling endlessly at night, hoping distraction feels something like peace. But silence, silence is dangerous. Because when you sit alone long enough, you meet every version of yourself you tried to outrun. The insecure child, the abandoned heart, the exhausted soul. And one day, I realized I wasn't just fighting depression. I was fighting the version of me that believed I had to earn love by suffering quietly. I thought healing meant never hurting again. But healing is actually waking up and choosing to stay, even when your mind tells you to disappear. Healing is messy. It's crying in parked cars, it's canceling plans to breathe, it's admitting, "I'm not okay." before your breaking point introduces you to the ground.
caption: In this emotionally charged audio clip, a man with a deep, resonant, and expressive voice delivers a powerful spoken-word monologue about his personal battle with depression and the true meaning of healing. His delivery is slow and deliberate, filled with raw emotion, shifting from whispered, somber tones to intense, passionate outbursts. The speech is set against a dramatic, cinematic background score featuring melancholic piano chords and swelling orchestral strings that rise and fall in harmony with the speaker's emotional state. He speaks of the facade of smiling to hide a 'war happening behind my eyes,' the exhaustion of invisible pain, and the dangerous nature of silence. The climax of the piece is both intense and hopeful, as the music swells and the speaker passionately declares that healing is not about never hurting again, but rather a messy, daily choice to stay and admit to not being okay.

title: THIS IS ADDICTION
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: This is addiction. It's a 3:00 a.m. phone call, the one you knew was coming but prayed never would. It's a doctor standing in a hallway saying there's nothing left to do. It's a mother falling to her knees like her heart just got ripped in two. It's a waiting room full of people blaming themselves for the pain, replaying every moment wondering what they could have changed. Questions you can't outrun, answers you'll never find. This is addiction. It don't just take one life. It leaves empty chairs at the table, every single night. It don't care who you are or how hard you fight. This is addiction. It steals in plain sight. It's a son and a daughter growing up trying to understand why. It's waking up to a world that don't make sense anymore inside.

title: SEMPER FI THROUGH THE STORM
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: They teach you two words the day you earn the title: Semper Fi. Always faithful. Faithful to your brothers, faithful to your country. But nobody tells you sometimes the hardest battle is the one that follows you home. Yellow footprints in Carolina sand, drill instructor shaping a man, sweating grit in the rising sun, turning boys into the chosen ones. Brothers forged through fire and rain, learning courage through the pain. Every Marine knows what that means, standing tall with the Marines. You can leave the battlefield, but the battlefield won't leave you. Semper Fi through the storm, when the night feels long, God held the line when my strength was gone. War in my mind, but my heart held on. Semper Fi, Semper Fi through the storm. The world sees a Marine and they see strength, they see discipline, they see courage. But what the world doesn't see are the battles that happen in the quiet, memories that don't fade, storms that don't stop just because the war is over. title: If I Fade First - After Everything [Official Lyric Video]

transcription:
Some things don't leave
when the door closes.
They just find quieter places
to sit.
I surveyed the room before I spoke a word.
Measure every step like the floor could give way.
The kitchen lights stayed on until morning came.
Nobody slept but nobody said a thing.
Like I could keep the peace that I didn't break.
Good at carrying blame that wasn't mine to take.
My name got tangled up in every argument
like I was born knowing something I never spent.
I spent years
trying to become smaller,
thinking less of me
would make more room for everyone else.
So why do I still flinch when somebody raises their voice?
Why does my chest lock up every time I have a choice?
I built my life around surviving,
forgot that there was another way.
I've been living like a storm was coming,
even on the calmest days.

Read the words I've never spoken, follow every pencil sign. Sometimes all that's left of me is the space between my lines. Hum... Some people see a simple sketch, a tree, a bird, a little sun. They never see the hidden roads the pencil's walking on. A broken branch, an empty chair, a window open just a crack, tiny clues left quietly for anyone looking back. transcription: We start things off tonight with breaking news. A vacant warehouse in Northwest Portland has been destroyed in a huge four-alarm fire this afternoon. This is at the Centennial Mills site on Northwest Naito, that's near the Fremont Bridge. Thanks so much for joining us, I'm John Adams. Crews were called out around 4:00 this afternoon. They say the fire was burning on the first floor and pushing onto the second. But as you can see, it didn't take long for the flames to take over that entire building. Firefighters had to shut down Northwest Naito to fight the flames. Firefighters say it wasn't safe for them to go inside and they had to fight the fire from the outside. And there was a lot of concern about the building and the water tower on top of it collapsing. And at one point, there was even a grass fire next to the building. Spot fires in this dry vegetation throughout our community, as well as in the trees, that just to the south, upon my arrival there was two- two hoses extinguishing a tree adjacent to an occupied condo complex. Graves says he expects firefighters to be on scene all night long. The Centennial Mills building was a former flour mill, but it's been abandoned for decades now. That's made it a magnet for squatters, homeless camps, and previous fires. In June, Portland police cleared squatters out of the building and arrested one person. City records show the building is currently owned by Stuart Lindquist, the same man who owns the Ice Building along the South Waterfront. A design review was approved for the building, and it had plans for nearly 300 homes and some retail space. We heard gunshot, a lot of rapid fire, it sounded like it was within a block of our house. It was dozens of rounds over multiple blocks. Chaos unfolded early this morning in one Northeast Portland neighborhood. An 18-year-old is now dead, and five other people, including a 15-year-old, are hurt after a shooting that police say started at a house party in the Cully neighborhood. Blair Best spoke with police and people who woke up to that gunfire. The shooting happened early Sunday morning. Police say it appears to be a house party gone tragically wrong. The neighborhood woken up to multiple rounds of gunfire followed by screaming. Some even tell me they saw teens running up and down the streets carrying guns. Dozens of gunshots rang out in this Northeast Portland neighborhood just after 3:30 Sunday morning. It was multiple rapid fire. Bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang.

title: Resistance grows nationwide against AI data center boom
transcription: Despite its promise, there's plenty of concern about our AI future. But in towns across America, one issue is already front and center. Here's Robert Costa. Archbald is a little corner of Northeastern Pennsylvania, where coal used to be big business. But now, there is a new boom, data centers. So we're not just looking at one, we're looking at many? Yes. Kaylee Cornell, a teacher, and Sarah Gabriel, an ICU nurse, run a neighborhood association in this community of 7,000, where a half dozen data center campuses have been proposed. What's it like living in Archbald? It is a really nice small town. It feels like home. I just really love it and I can't imagine being anywhere else. But they and others are alarmed about the possible impact on the environment, their electric bills, and the town's character. It's going to just completely change the landscape. Anywhere there's trees, there's probably not going to be any any longer. We'll stop it if we could help it. Stopping it won't be easy. Demand is huge. Tech companies say they need these massive structures full of computing power to fuel the AI revolution. So developers are rushing to build them in places like Archbald, rich in land, water, and power. But there is an intensifying debate over the scope of jobs and revenue they bring, and many communities are on edge about rising electric utility bills. Get out of here! We made up our minds! Go home! In Archbald, the push to slow things down has upended local politics, and one project has hit a roadblock. You didn't expect to fight against AI superpowers in the global economy and the development of Archbald? Yes, correct. We don't want to be. No. This wasn't part of the plan. No, not at all. And we're not against AI data centers, but because the industry is so new and unregulated, it is concerning that if we just keep moving forward, we're going to get to a point where, like, a point of no return. Elsewhere, data centers are already a way of life, with more than 4,000 and counting in operation across the country, and many more going up around the world. Here in Loudoun County, Virginia, known as Data Center Alley, these anonymous sci-fi-looking buildings seem to be everywhere. This building right here is north of a million square feet, but you can visualize it. You could park maybe not just one, but two aircraft carriers. Two aircraft carriers? Andy Power is the president and CEO of Digital Realty, which owns and operates hundreds of data centers globally. Just how big is this sector?

title: Google’s AI endgame is here… everything you missed at I/O 2026
transcription: Yesterday, Google I/O wrapped, and I was able to watch in person as Sundar and Demis laid out an ambitious vision for the future of software. And apparently, that future is Gemini hiding inside of every product like the microplastics in your bloodstream. The roadmap is basically take Gemini, append a noun to it, and ship it. Gemini Spark, Gemini Omni, Gemini Flow, and the list goes on. They're calling it the agentic Gemini era. Search is now an AI agent, Gmail is an AI agent, Android is an AI agent, your glasses are an AI agent, and as I watched the keynote, I realized something. Google is no longer trying to organize the world's information with blue hyperlinks, because search engines are now an archaic technology. Instead, Google is trying to become the interface to reality itself before Anthropic and OpenAI create better realities. But luckily, Google I/O wasn't all about AI. I didn't see any updates about Angular, but I did come across a new awesome web API that every web developer should know about. In today's video, we'll break down everything you missed at Google I/O. It is May 22, 2024, and we're watching the Code Report. Whether you love it or hate it, one thing is undeniably impressive about Google, and that's its ability to scale. Not only is it serving its core products to billions of daily active users, but in the last two years, they've gone from serving 9.7 trillion tokens per month to a staggering 3.2 quadrillion tokens per month, and that number is going to continue accelerating. In addition, Alphabet's capital expenditures have exploded, building new infrastructure to support all these stupid AI images you guys create with nano banana. You ever see a pug dressed like an accountant? No. You wanna? Uh... One thing that makes this massive scale possible is Google's TPU chip, or tensor processing unit. I remember being amazed seeing a TPU at my first Google I/O back in 2018. But this week, they announced they're splitting these chips into two distinct jobs: training and inference, with the TPU T and TPU I. In other words, Google now has one chip that's optimized to teach a robot how to think, and another chip that's optimized for it to hallucinate search results on a global scale. The headline announcement at Google I/O though was Gemini Omni, a model that takes any input, like text, video, and sound, and produces any output. Demis Hassabis, who might be the smartest guy at Google, appears to be fully world-modeled pilled, because models like this don't just generate pixels anymore. They understand language, physics, motion, and everything else in your world just well enough to simulate reality on demand. But along with this new model, comes an entirely new design system for the Gemini app called Neural Expressive. At first glance, the UI looks like a simple glow up with new icons and better gradients, but what's unique about it is that it's optimized for generating UI elements on demand, like diagrams, timelines, and even mini apps that didn't exist before your prompt. title: Macbook Neo Impressions: Reincarnated!
transcription: Alright, so Apple is doing a week of new release stuff and it's all headlined by what I saw today, which is the newest, cheapest entry to the MacBook lineup: the MacBook Neo. First of all, interesting name. We've never heard that word from Apple before. I thought when it was leaked it was maybe just a code name. I would have bet it's just called "the MacBook" but no, it's actually MacBook Neo. And the basics are this: it is a 13-inch laptop, powered by the A18 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, 256GB of starting storage, and it is a super thin and decently light all-aluminum laptop. Two USB Type-C ports on the left-hand side, not Thunderbolt. There's a headphone jack on the left as well, and then there's some side-firing stereo speakers. And it comes in four colors: Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and Silver. They all have this sort of a whitish keyboard that is kind of tinted to match the color of the laptop. In person, maybe the lighting is terrible in here, but it was kind of hard to tell when looking at a single laptop. But you can, when they're some next to each other, see that the keyboards are tinted. And there's a 1080p webcam up at the top hidden in that bezel, no notch. And most importantly, the starting price: $599. And this is really interesting. They actually hit the price. This is now, you know, the cheapest entry-level Mac laptop. It's the same price as a Mac Mini, which has actually been one of the best deals in tech for a little bit now, and I think this one's also shaping up to be pretty good value. Now, the X factor is how will the A18 Pro chip perform inside a computer? Now, in case you don't remember, the A18 Pro is the same chip that was in the iPhone 16 Pros last year, but actually, this is a binned version. This is a 5-core GPU version instead of 6-core. But I think in general, there's a lot of tasks that regular people do on regular computers that clearly don't require a ton of power. Web browsing, emailing, shopping, spreadsheet-type of stuff, right? And before I've done any testing, just messing around on this thing for a few minutes, it seems like it would be totally fine for that. I would not expect to edit videos or do anything really intensive on this thing, that would be kind of crazy. But I also wouldn't be surprised if it could handle some light photo editing, some multitasking, and just, you know, generally be a solid computer. Think of it like a Chromebook, but

title: What Does a Business Broker Actually Do? (In Under 5 Minutes)
transcription: And tell, tell us what a business broker does? You know, that's a great question, it's a good starting point because I think a lot of business owners don't realize understand what a business broker does, or even that there are business brokers out there who can help represent them through all phases of the sell of their business. So, that's exactly what we do. We are hired by the seller to represent them through every phase of selling the business. And that includes roughly four areas. So, the first area is the valuation of the business and that's really the jumping-off point. That helps business owners understand whether there's a gap between what the business is worth and what the owner needs or expects for their next phase of life. And that's really kind of the first step, that's the first informative piece for business owners to really better understand is what their business would sell for on the open market. We also help business owners assemble their advisory team, and that may include wealth advisors like Jared, transaction attorneys, accountants. And often, your broker has relationships with other people who are competent and expedient when it comes to business transactions. So, your broker will also handle all areas of your confidential marketing strategy, and that includes listing the business on all industry-leading websites, creating the marketing material, and getting that listing confidentially out there for potential buyers to see. We also have a database of thousands of potential buyers that we do send listings out to. Once those buyer leads start coming in, we start screening those buyers. And we're only going to present a seller with buyers who we feel match the criteria that they've told us that it's important to them. We're also only going to present buyers who we feel are ready, willing, and able to purchase the business. Because we really want to
