title: Leading Change Webinar Clip
transcription: Hi, and welcome. This is Leading Change from Where You Are, Empowered Strategies for Navigating Transitions. My name is Cassie Blossey. I'm the co-founder of Sageburg Consulting, I'm a nonprofit executive leader, education policy is the core of my background and experience and I love working in the community, specifically around change management in nonprofits and small businesses. One of the things that is really important about nonprofits is that they're so core to our community and, whether they like it or not, they also experience change pretty regularly, and in fact change is the only constant, right? So what I have seen in my experience is that nonprofits that set up systems to help them go through change, uh, experience much more um, long-term success and they see fewer disruptions in their actual services, and so they can meet their impact and mission. So today, we're going to talk about a couple of key areas of change. These three are the top types of change that I see in nonprofits and small businesses every day. Uh, the first one is one that we have a little bit more control over and we'll talk about the next two because they tend to give us a little bit more anxiety, so let's start with planned. Planned change has to do with change that you can anticipate, something that you know for sure is coming up. That can be a retirement, the end of a temporary role, maybe it's the end of a grant, maybe it's something that you knew you were going to start and then had a very clear end date. So when you're talking about planned, uh, change, one of the things that's really important is making sure you have really good communication systems and thinking about, "Okay, we know that this transition's going to happen in March, so we should start setting us, ourselves up for success by thinking about that transition, maybe in January, how are we making sure that everything will be successful once that change happens?" So, you have a lot more control in this area of change. The next two, as I mentioned, not our favorite, but you can still be successful. Emergent change is the unfortunate change that happens when there's something sudden, it's unexpected, sometimes it comes with additional risk, for example, sudden illness or a natural disaster.
caption:
A female speaker, Cassie Blazi, co-founder of Sagebrook Consulting, delivers a presentation titled "Leading Change From Where You Are: Empower Strategies for Navigating Transitions." Speaking with a warm, encouraging, and professional tone, she draws on her experience in education policy and nonprofit leadership to discuss the inevitability of change within the nonprofit sector.

She categorizes change into three main types, focusing on "planned" and "emergent" change. Planned change is described as anticipated events, like retirements or ending grants, where structured communication and early preparation (such as planning in January for a March transition) are key to success. In contrast, she defines emergent change as sudden, unexpected disruptions like illness or natural disasters that carry higher risks. Her delivery is well-paced and articulate, with occasional natural pauses and filler words, creating an engaging and informative atmosphere.

transcription: If you're still pasting a single headline and one block of primary text into Facebook and calling it a day, we seriously need to have a conversation. You can and absolutely should be serving up multiple diverse variations for every single ad you run. Facebook actually allows you to upload up to five different headlines and five primary text options for every single ad set. Sticking with just one option is honestly the biggest mistake you can make right now. The entire reason we run ads is to learn things fast about what actually resonates with people. You want to know which creative hooks land, which copy flavors make people stop scrolling, and which lines actually drive the clicks. Setting yourself up for variation means you learn more quality information in a fraction of the time. Here is a super practical workflow that I personally rely on to scale my ad copy effortlessly. Start by writing just one solid headline and one primary text option that you feel good about. Then immediately take that original content and plug it directly into your favorite AI tool for variations. Ask the AI for five alternate headlines, specifically requesting different tones like punchy or benefit-focused. You'll do the exact same thing for your primary text options, asking for variety in length and style. Don't forget, you can also use Meta's built-in copy suggestions right inside the ad creation interface. Be warned, though, those auto-suggested lines are truly a mixed bag of quality. Some of those suggestions are absolute gold, but many others are honestly not very good at all. That means you absolutely have to act as the final human filter for everything that comes out. Always pick the best ones, quickly tweak the rest, and be ruthless about discarding anything that feels totally off brand. If you are smart and promoting video content, the next step is pairing your copy variations with multiple creative cuts. This is exactly where a tool that automates video editing becomes a total game changer for your workflow. Forget manually trimming a long webinar or podcast episode down into just one hopeful clip. Instead, an AI finds those truly viral-worthy moments and spits out multiple short clips that work on their own. Your new workflow can look like this: auto-edit several clips from one long video source. Then, auto-schedule those clips to post at different times across your channels. Finally, pair every single clip with a range of different headline and text combinations. This process allows you to generate dozens of unique ad permutations without getting buried under the editing work. So, number one we see is business protection, with 58% of owners saying they have a plan in place to protect their business, but that means that there's a, a whole lot of other ones that do not already have a plan in place where you can come in and help them establish that. Number two was health and wellness solutions, where you can see the majority of them do offer benefits already. Key employee benefits came in at number three, where only 39% are currently offering benefits, with 65% saying they want to add more. Number four is income protection, with half of them having a plan in place. And number five would be non-medical benefits, where as you can see, there's the majority at 70% already offering those benefits. Where my team comes in is on those business protection, key employee benefits, and income protection cases. So, in order to, uh, establish what type of business they are and where they're at with their needs, we want to see what stage of business they are in. So, a new business has been around for one to three years, they're still getting established, profits are going back into the company, they have outstanding loans and lines of credit, just because they're still trying to build their business up. A growing business has been in place for over three years, they're still establishing market share, and they have large expenses like equipment, hires, maybe they're getting an office at this point with a growing revenue stream, growing staff, uh, where they may, this might be when they're first trying to round out their benefits, uh, beyond those basic coverages. An established business has been in place for over 10 years, they're consistent in their cash flow and revenue, experienced, they have strategies for business transition, buy-sell, with an established client base and relationship management team. This is the area that we are most often working in, is these established businesses, uh, because they tend to have the, the cash flow to be able to do plans like a deferred compensation plan or key person protection.

title: Sustainability Strategy Masterclass: Purpose and Key Ingredients
transcription: the purpose and the key ingredients of a sustainability strategy. A sustainability strategy is like any strategy, whether that's an operations strategy, a business strategy, a marketing strategy, the idea is to put down in one place what your organization wants to achieve and how it's going to achieve that. So, it's really important that the strategy clearly communicates what the ambition is and how the organization will get there. And a really good way to do this is to think about the priorities in your organization. So, sustainability is a very, very broad topic. In some places, water could be the primary sustainability concern. So if, for example, you're living somewhere like, um, the United Arab Emirates, which is majority desert, water is going to be much higher up your, um, priorities list than if you're living in Manchester, where I live, where it does rain most days. Um, equally, if you're in a very remote, rural community, maybe part of your sustainability strategy is your business will operate in a way that supports that local economy, um, makes the best use of local and natural resources. Whereas if you're in a city, it might be slightly different, um, ways of interacting with that community. And just as a, as a quick sort of aside, sustainability, a good way to think about sustainability is as a stool with three legs. You've got to think about the environmental sustainability of your business, the social sustainability, um, aspects, and the economic sustainability aspects. And today's webinar, we are going to have a bit of a focus on environmental sustainability, as this is mostly where Innovative Energy Consultants works, but I don't want people to forget those other aspects, because if you, you could have the best environmental sustainability strategy in the world, but if you're not helping the communities that you work in, that, those, um, good things that you're doing aren't, the benefits aren't really being felt by the people around you, and if you forget about your economic sustainability, the business won't exist after a few years, and so all of that good work will, will cease to exist. So,

title: Getting started with Claude Cowork
transcription: Claude Cowork meets you where your work happens and allows you to delegate complete tasks to Claude. If it's on your computer, Claude can find and edit it. If it's in the cloud, Claude connects through services like Google Drive, Notion, and Slack. If it's in the browser, Claude is there too, through Claude in Chrome. Describe what you need done, and Claude does it. You can watch it work, steer when it matters, or step away and come back to the results. Claude Cowork is generally available in the Claude Desktop app on macOS and Windows for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users. To get started, open Claude Desktop and click the Cowork tab. In a regular Claude chat, you work with Claude step-by-step. In Cowork, you hand off tasks, and Claude handles the rest while you focus on other work. First, give Claude access to a folder on your computer. Select the folder directory or project you want Claude to operate in. It asks permission before making changes to your file system. Claude can now read, create, and edit files in that folder directly. You can favorite the folders you go to most or select multiple folders to connect disparate data sources. Second, connect your tools. Cowork supports connectors that link Claude to services. These let Claude pull context from where your work already lives. Third, if you've set up Claude in Chrome, Cowork can use it for browser-based tasks, reading web pages, extracting data from sites, and navigating across tabs. Under settings, you can also click the Cowork tab and set global instructions that apply to every session, like context about your role or directions to create files as Word docs instead of markdowns. One thing to keep in mind, your Cowork sessions are stored locally on your device, and the Desktop app needs to stay open while Claude is working on a task. Let's start with something really simple.

Fir bhale hazar hyenas ho ya sau deers ho ya koi bhi ho beech me you will go and like get your hunt and you won't come back home until you have that. So I believe in that philosophy and I operate like that. Ek cheez hai jo hum karte hain aur sabko karni chahiye is, tum kahin bhi ho kisi bhi field me kuch bhi kar rahe ho whether job, business, podcast, content creation, anything at all. Just khudse obsessed ho jao aur khudpe hi kaam karo. Let the world say that you are obsessed, tum delusional ho, tum arrogant ho, tumhe duniya ka farq nahi padta. Let it be. Become that person. Ki tumhe genuinely farq hi na pade ki paas me agar koi office aa jaye aur uska bahut bada podcast ho toh tumhe pata hi na ho uska naam kya hai. Tum us level ke bas itne blinders lagake apne hi kaam karo. That is the best mindset shift and habit that people can have.

transcription: Welcome to SD Bio. দেখুন গতকাল অর্থাৎ ২৭/০৭/২০২৬ পশ্চিমবঙ্গ সমগ্র শিক্ষা মিশন স্কুল এডুকেশন ডিপার্টমেন্ট থেকে একটা নোটিফিকেশন দিয়েছে যে নোটিফিকেশনকে ঘিরে কিন্তু বিতর্ক তৈরি হয়েছে। কি রয়েছে এই নোটিফিকেশনে? আপনারা হয়তো অনেকেই দেখে নিয়েছেন, কিন্তু বিতর্ক যেটা রয়েছে সেইটা নিয়ে আজকে আলোচনা করবো এবং তার সমাধান কী সেটাও বলবো। এই নোটিফিকেশনে দেওয়া হয়েছে যেখানে বলা হচ্ছে সমস্ত স্কুলের সমস্ত হেডমাস্টার এবং অ্যাসিস্ট্যান্ট টিচারদের সিপিডি অর্থাৎ কন্টিনিউয়াস প্রফেশনাল ডেভেলপমেন্ট কোর্সগুলো মিনিমাম ৫০ ঘণ্টা করতে হবে। এর মধ্যে আমরা তো কেউ ৫০ ঘণ্টা, ৬০ ঘণ্টা, ৭০ ঘণ্টা করে ফেলেছি। কিন্তু সেগুলো সিপিডি কোর্স কি না সেটা আমাকে দেখতে হবে। সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু মিনিমাম ৫০ ঘণ্টা, বাকি যত কোর্স আছে আপনি ৭০, ৮০, ৯০ ঘণ্টাও অনেকে করে নিয়েছে শুনছি, কিন্তু করে নিতেই পারেন কোনো অসুবিধা নেই, যত বেশি করবেন তত আপনার স্কিল ডেভেলপমেন্ট হবে। তার সঙ্গে আর একটা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে খুব সম্ভবত ৯০% আমি যা দেখছি সারা ভারতবর্ষের সিচুয়েশন, টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে। তো যেহেতু টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে, এমন কোর্সগুলো সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো বেছে নেব যেগুলো আমাদের টেট দিতে সুবিধা হবে বা টেটের কিছু নলেজও গ্যাদার হবে, সেই বিষয়টাও আজকে আলোচনা করবো। যেমন ৫০ ঘণ্টা যেটা আছে সেটা হচ্ছে ম্যান্ডেটরি করা হয়েছে সিপিডি কোর্সের এবং এটা প্রতি বছর করতে হবে। এই বছর করে নিলাম মানে না, প্রতি বছর কোর্স পালটে দেবে তারা সেই অ্যাপস এর মধ্যে এবং সেই অ্যাপস এ গিয়ে আমাদের কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং প্রতি বছর কী কী কোর্সগুলো দেওয়া হবে সেগুলো জানিয়ে দেওয়া হবে। এনরোলমেন্ট হওয়ার শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে এবছর ৩১শে আগস্ট অর্থাৎ ২০২৬-২৭ শিক্ষাবর্ষের এনরোলমেন্টের শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে ৩১শে আগস্টের মধ্যে কিন্তু এনরোলমেন্ট করে নিতে হবে। এবং অনেকগুলো কোর্স কিন্তু শেষ হয়ে যাবে ১৫ই সেপ্টেম্বর, কিছু কিছু কোর্স কিন্তু ৩১শে আগস্ট বা জুলাই মাসেও, এই ৩১শে জুলাইয়ের মধ্যেও কিন্তু কিছু কোর্স শেষ হয়ে যাচ্ছে। তাই তড়িঘড়ি করে কিন্তু আমাদের এই কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং এই transcription: अगर आप 2026 में सीएस बनना चाहते हो या फिर सीएस स्टार्ट कर रहे हो तो इस वीडियो को एंड तक देखना। सो यस गाइस आज के वीडियो में मैं आपको बताने वाली हूं कि सीएस आप कैसे बन सकते हो, सीएस के स्टेजेस के बारे में डिस्कस करेंगे, सीएस क्या होता है यह समझेंगे, ट्रेनिंग्स क्या होती है, सीएस आप कहां से कर सकते हो, कौन से रिसोर्सेज रिफर करने हैं, एवरीथिंग। यह 15 मिनट का जो वीडियो है वह आपका आगे आने वाला 50 साल पूरा डिस्कस कर लेगा, एक पूरी क्लैरिटी मैप आपको मिलने वाली है। सो यस फ्रेंड्स वेलकम बैक टू माय चैनल, दिस इज नेहा पटेल। मैं खुद एक कंपनी सेक्रेटरी और लॉयर हूं, मैंने सीएस क्लियर किया था इन द ईयर 2020 विद एन ऑल इंडिया रैंक इन ऑल द थ्री स्टेजेस एंड ट्रस्ट मी गाइस 2020 के बाद से सीएस काफी ज्यादा चेंज हुआ है एंड 2026 में तो काफी ही ज्यादा चेंज हो गया है सीएस, क्या चेंज हुआ है वह भी हम इस वीडियो में डिस्कस करेंगे तो चलो शुरू करते हैं। सो गाइस सबसे पहले मैं कुछ डाउट्स क्लियर करना चाहती हूं। बच्चों को यह डाउट आता है कि मैं साइंस बैकग्राउंड से हूं तो क्या मैं सीएस कर सकता हूं, कर सकती हूं? तो डेफिनेटली सीएस में कोई एंट्री बैरियर नहीं है, आप साइंस से हो, आर्ट्स से हो, कॉमर्स से हो, हर कोई सीएस कर सकता है। सेकंड, एलिजिबिलिटी जो है सीएस करने की वह होती है ट्वेल्थ, ठीक है? तो यहां पर दो तरीके से आप सीएस में आ सकते हो, नंबर वन इज की आप अपना ट्वेल्थ क्लियर करके सीएस में आ जाओ, सेकंड इस की आप ग्रेजुएशन करके सीएस में आओ। तो ट्वेल्थ की बात करें तो ट्वेल्थ के बाद आपको तीन स्टेजेस करने पड़ेंगे, पहला होता है सीएसइइटी जो कि आपका एंट्रेंस है, उसके बाद सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव एंड देन सीएस प्रोफेशनल। अगर आप ग्रेजुएशन के बाद आना चाहते हो तो एंट्रेंस आपका एक्जेंप्ट हो जाता है, आप सीधा आपको डायरेक्ट एंट्री मिलती है एग्जीक्यूटिव में एंड देन प्रोफेशनल। मेरी पर्सनल रिकमेंडेशन यही होगी कि आप ट्वेल्थ के बाद से ही सीएस स्टार्ट कर लो अगर आप एकदम श्योर शॉर्ट क्लियर हो बिकॉज जब तक आप ग्रेजुएट होगे तब तक तो आप सीएस बन भी जाओगे, तीन ही साल का कोर्स होता है, दैट्स व्हाई। तो अभी हम बात करते हैं इसके पहले स्टेज की जो की है सीएसइइटी - सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव एंट्रेंस एग्जाम टेस्ट। नाउ गाइस इसमें काफी ज्यादा चेंज आया है, अगर आप 2026 के पहले सीएस करने की सोच रहे थे ना, तो सीएसइइटी आप घर बैठे-बैठे एमसीक्यू में अपने कंप्यूटर में पास हो जाते, बट अभी आपको एक्चुअल में सेंटर्स में जाना पड़ेगा और आंसर लिखना पड़ेगा। एक्चुअल में तीन घंटे पेपर आपको देने हैं, चार सब्जेक्ट होता है एंड सेंटर में जाकर आपको पेपर देना होगा, बस एक ही पेपर है सीएसइइटी का जो कि अभी एमसीक्यू बेस्ड होगा वह है लॉ का पेपर, बाकी तीनों सब्जेक्ट्स आपको लिखने हैं तो यह सबसे बड़ा चेंज आपके एंट्रेंस लेवल पर ही आया है। जो सीएसइइटी है वो साल में तीन बार होने वाला है फेब में, जून में एंड अक्टूबर में।

And it does this while remembering everything, and will hit you up on Telegram or WhatsApp as it automates your entire life. Over the last few weeks, everybody's been going crazy over it. It's racked up over 65,000 GitHub stars in record time, and caused Mac Mini sales to go through the roof, selling out everywhere. In today's video, we'll take a hands-on look at everything it can do, but its popularity has already created some problems. Earlier this week, Anthropic, a company that believes open-source AI is too dangerous for the common man, woke up and chose violence. Claude Bot sounded too similar to their beloved Claude, so they threatened to break the developer's knees with a lead pipe if they don't change the name. So now, Claude Bot is officially called Molt Bot. Actually, no, wait a minute, Molt Bot, that name sucks. Today, they changed the name once again to its final form, Open Clod. Open Clod was created by Peter Steinberger, the founder of the developer tools company PSPDFKit, AKA Nutrient. But just look at this dude's unhinged GitHub profile. It's less of a resume and more of a heat map of pure uninterrupted software obsession. What's crazy is that this guy retired and then came back for an encore by giving us Molt Bot for free, a tool written in TypeScript that wraps Claude and GPT-5 to stay alive 24/7. title: How to think like a lawyer | Zero-L from Harvard Law School
transcription: Imagine I asked you, what do you learn in law school? Well, you've decided to take this course, so maybe you're more informed than the average person. So instead imagine I asked your college roommate or your parents, assuming they're not lawyers. The image that may come to mind of law school is sun-deprived, bespectacled law students surrounded by large numbers of dusty books, reading intently so they can memorize a bunch of law cases. And don't get me wrong, we do make students read a lot from books, and there's some memorization involved. But that image of someone learning the law by just memorizing things that are already out there is not at all what law school is really about. If it were, law school would be much less fun, and also much less useful. The law is always changing. So if you just learned a number of dry rules, much of what you learned might be outdated by your fifth year in practice. The chief value of legal education is not to know stuff, but to know what stuff to look for, where to find it, how to interpret what you find, what to think when some stuff says one thing, and other stuff says another. And how to use what you find to give legal advice. Let me put this very tangibly for you. If you call up a lawyer on anything other than a very simple question, and without pausing, she quickly gives you a straightforward answer, you should fire her. She's not doing a very good job for you. She's just not thinking like a lawyer. That's a phrase you'll hear a lot in law school, and while we might over-use it a bit, it does capture something important. Law is mostly about questions, choices, and analysis, about thinking and not so much about simple answers. That is the main thing we try to teach you in law school. Yes, we want to teach you a good amount of content about the law. To use an example from a course I teach, civil procedure, we want you to know what claims without subject matter jurisdiction can get jurisdiction by way of being joined to other claims through 28 U.S.C. 1367. If that sounds a bit intimidating at first, that's very normal, it is. But by the end of 1L fall, that knowledge will be at the tip of your brain, or at least somewhere in there.

title: Admiral McRaven: The Letter His Mother Wrote Him Before He Left for SEAL Training
transcription: [Applause] I'm going to say three words which you're all going to know immediately and associate with the Admiral. Make your bed. [Laughter] Nine years ago, you made the commencement address here at the University of Texas, and that commencement address went viral. It's become iconic. Everybody can summon those words as an admonition, almost. How did that speech come to you, Bill? Yeah. So Bill Powers, when he was the president here, had invited me to be the commencement speaker, I don't know, three or four months before May. And obviously, you know, anytime you're invited to be a commencement speaker, it's quite an honor. Uh but I had a day job. So I was still I was running the university, I'm sorry, I was running the Special Operations Command. So I started writing the speech about, uh, yeah, maybe two weeks before uh I was supposed to give it, and I'd kind of been mulling some ideas over in my head. So I started writing it on the weekends, a little bit here, a little bit there. And I had this great theme and I thought I was going to pull it all together, and then the Wednesday before the Saturday that I was supposed to give the speech, I realized the speech didn't work. I mean, it wasn't wasn't a good speech. And I I went downstairs. I'd been writing upstairs. I went downstairs, I see Georgeann and I go, "Oh, my God. It, it doesn't work." [Laughter] "It's, it's not a good speech." I said, "I don't know what I'm going to do. I mean, I'm giving the speech in a couple of days." And she says to me, she said, "Well, why don't you write about something you know?" And I thought, "Well, there's an interesting concept." Um. And I told her, I said, "Yeah, but the only thing I know is how to be a Navy SEAL." And she said, "Well, write about that." But at the time, you know, you may recall there had been a number of kind of administration officials that had been, you know, scheduled to give commencement addresses and then the student population kind of voted them down and they didn't end up doing it. And I thought, "You know, if I talk about being a Navy SEAL to uh university students here and, you know, 8,000 students were graduating, I think, that year and 25,000 uh family members," I thought, "I I I'm going to be in uniform. I don't know how this is going to go."

title: Panel Discussion: Putting YOU into your Business Brand (life after "Corporate")
transcription:
Now, Susie, you mentioned that you've, you know, you've come from a different background. You worked in the corporate space, you worked in technology. Um, and you've had to shift from kind of that corporate mindset to a small business owner, someone who is now looking at corporate marketing to marketing your own brand, marketing yourself, marketing your small business. I'd love to know, like, what is one shift that you personally had to navigate making that transition? And what can you offer to other women in this room that are making that shift as well?

It was so hard. I don't know how many other folks left corporate and suddenly had to come out and start talking about themselves. So, I spent a lot of time on that messaging at my at my company. And it was the company's voice, it was the company's style, and it was the company's message. And it was great. I was good at it, right? It was awesome.

And then suddenly, the company wasn't there anymore. Social media was new when I was working in corporate. I never posted my own thoughts and feelings about the world because everything I said was going to reflect back on my company. How was how were they going to look at this, right? I was working for somebody else, it was their brand. I came out and suddenly said, "I am my brand. I can talk about anything I want to talk about because I am my brand." It was scarier than heck, I hated it, I didn't want to talk about myself, I didn't want to sell myself, I didn't want to market myself. It was really intimidating. And so, that was my biggest kind of hurdle as I came into this, right? I had to worry about my skills, I had those. I had to worry about my pricing, I figured that out. But talking about me and putting myself out there was a huge mental shift for me. And I wrote a blog post for the Sunnyvale Chamber of Commerce all about going my own experience going to get photos taken of myself and how terrifying it was and how important it was to get those photos to tell my story. And I was talking about it, I was using my voice, and it was great, and it felt good. And then I got to my about me, and I switched into, "Susie McFaddin is an internationally published award-winning photographer who blah blah blah." And the folks who reviewed it for me said, "That's great, but it didn't sound like you as soon as you started talking about yourself."

title: This Week in Review | Fed Meeting, US GDP, Eurozone GDP (July 31, 2026)
transcription: Hello and welcome to This Week in Review. This is our weekly segment that's designed to highlight a few important developments that you might have missed this week, and we'll talk about what they mean for markets, and, most importantly, the potential impact for investors. To stay up to date with our latest market insights, subscribe to our YouTube channel or visit fisherinvestments.com. Now, let's review what happened this week. First, the Fed meeting. On Wednesday, the Federal Open Market Committee, or FOMC, voted to hold the interest rate steady at 3.5 to 3.75%. This was the fifth straight meeting without an interest rate change. It was also a split decision, and three members voted to hike rates by 25 basis points. Headlines quickly seized on the story of a divided Fed, but we wouldn't really read too much into that. Differing opinions among Fed officials tells us very little about what the committee will do next, and dissenting votes don't make a rate hike more or less likely in the meetings ahead. Some investors may also worry that Chairman Kevin Warsh's decision to step back from so-called forward guidance may make monetary policy harder to predict or less transparent. We see that differently. Central banks can, and often do, change their minds without notice based on changing economic data or fundamentals. So rather than trying to guess their next move, we think investors are better served by keeping their focus on the broader fundamentals driving markets. Central bank decisions are just one of many forces shaping the global economy and capital markets, and while we believe a rate hike would be a mistake, the talk today is of small hikes. And, really importantly, even a hike or two from here would leave policy rates within a range that this bull market has already successfully navigated. Additionally, when we look around the developed world, yield curves remain steep and healthy. For long-term investors, that's perspective worth holding on to.

title: Clorox (CLX) Stock Analysis 2026 – Graphs, Risks, Opportunities & Valuation ✅
transcription: Clorox is a good example of a defensive consumer staples business that the market once priced for certainty, then sharply repriced when that certainty broke down. In the pandemic era, investors were willing to pay a premium for bleach, disinfecting and household staples because demand looked unusually strong and durable. In hindsight, that was one of the market's big mistakes. It capitalized peak demand as if it were normal demand. Then the opposite happened. The August 2023 cyberattack followed by ERP-related shipment disruption in fiscal 2024 reminded investors that even a boring staples company can suffer real operational volatility. But Clorox also had real successes. Fiscal 2024 gross margin rose to 43.8%, adjusted EPS reached $6.10, and operating cash flow climbed to $1.04 billion as cost savings and recovery actions took hold. Today the stock looks much less loved. Clorox is trading around $132.85 with a trailing PE of about 21.8x. Against management's fiscal 2025 adjusted EPS outlook of $6.55 to $6.80, the stock is trading at roughly 19 to 20x forward earnings. The quarterly dividend is $1.22 or $4.88 annualized, which puts the yield near 3.7% at the current price. For a company that historically often attracted a much richer multiple because of brand strength, resilience and dividend dependability, that is a meaningful derating. The market is no longer paying up for Clorox as a premium safe haven. It is pricing it more like a mature business that has to prove earnings quality again. The reason the multiple is compressed is not that the brands stopped mattering. It is that fiscal 2025 is messy. In Q1 FY25, net sales fell 15% to $1.39 billion, organic sales were down 15%, and gross margin slipped to 38.8% from 42.1%. Management kept full-year guidance, but said results were likely to land toward the lower end because earlier order fulfillment problems caused consumption and market share losses.

title: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) Q2 2026 Earnings Explained | Why the Market Misread the $0.95 EPS Loss
transcription: Navitas Semiconductor's second quarter 2026 earnings triggered a sharp market reaction, but the headline tells only part of the story. Investors focused on a reported GAAP loss of 95 cents per share, a result that appeared to miss expectations by roughly 22 times. At first glance, that looked alarming. However, a closer examination of the financial statements reveals a very different picture. The reported loss was driven almost entirely by a one-time non-cash accounting adjustment rather than a deterioration in the underlying business. Once that accounting impact is removed, the operational performance appears considerably stronger. The key comparison begins with two earnings figures. While GAAP earnings showed a loss of 95 cents per share, the non-GAAP loss was only 4 cents per share. At the same time, revenue exceeded expectations by approximately 7%. The difference between those two earnings figures was a $203 million, one-time, non-cash SPACC earn-out accounting charge tied to the company's 2021 SPACC transaction. This adjustment had no impact on cash flow or ongoing operations, and has now been fully recognized, meaning it will no longer affect future financial statements. Operationally, the quarter showed meaningful progress. Revenue reached $10.53 million, representing 22% sequential growth and finishing at the high end of management's guidance. Looking ahead, management projected another 28% increase in revenue during the third quarter. The operational loss also improved modestly, declining from $11.7 million in the previous quarter to $11.4 million. Viewed through that lens, the underlying business improved rather than weakened. Much of the market reaction reflected a comparison between a GAAP result and non-GAAP expectations, effectively comparing two different accounting measures. Once those figures are separated, the operating trend becomes much clearer. Understanding Navitas also requires understanding its position within AI infrastructure. While AI discussions often focus on GPUs and computing power, every AI data center ultimately depends on efficient power conversion.

title: Tesla Reports Huge Miss on Earnings for Second Quarter
transcription:
You think about what we heard from Tesla, adjusted EPS coming in at 33 cents, that is well below the analyst expectation of about 51 cents on average. It's not often that you see a miss of that magnitude for a company as mature and as large as Tesla. So, back this out for me and sort of make the math work.

Okay, Katie, I think it's, uh, it's compounded in that they beat the top line revenue by close to $3 billion. So, you have a massive top-line beat, and then you have this bottom-line, uh, huge miss. And in the car business, that's pretty straightforward math. Uh, they are falling to the temptation of feeding the top line, uh, which is a beast to continue to keep growing, with discounts. And when you discount, uh, in the form of price and in the form of the APR that people are paying, and they've done both, you see what happens to margins. They can, they can have a huge top-line beat because of course, people are going to buy a, uh, less expensive product or a below market price product, but then the profitability falls dramatically. And in this case, they missed EPS by more than a third. And I think that's the story here. This is not an AI investment story, this is a story in the base business. And the base business, I think, is giving hints that the, the product lineup is older, it's dated, and in order to move that product, you've got to discount it. And that hits, that hits the bottom line, and that's exactly, I think, what we're seeing here in these earnings.

Yeah, absolutely, a big tension there. And you think about, uh, the issues that they are having when it comes to their base business, the car business. How much of a setback is that for some of the ambitions that we know that the stock has been valued on when you think about, uh, AI, autonomous vehicles, robotics? The list goes on.

Well, I think they, the original plan was you've got a cash-flowing auto business that's going to fund you to the, then, future of autonomous cars, robotaxis, and robots. But you've got to have that cash flow, uh, and that cash flow has to be healthy, uh, and to the extent that your base business isn't funding the future, now you've got to go out and either fund it through equity or debt, uh, on top of this. And so, I think that's the question for investors, is to look forward and, and to really try to determine how much capital it's going to take to get to that future and then, uh, where that capital is going to come from. I think we see this across industries, it's one of the reasons we formed Vistashares is because the, the market tends to focus on end producers like Tesla. And the, the money's actually made in the supply chain. The supply chain has double the profit margins that Tesla has in the end. Uh, and so, although Tesla's getting squeezed by the end market, their supply chain is likely much healthier, and that's probably where investors want exposure versus betting on Tesla as an end producer here.

title: NBA Finals Game 5 HIGHLIGHTS: New York Knicks vs. San Antonio Spurs | NBA on ESPN
transcription: Game five, Knicks and Spurs, ready to do battle once again. They lost their first road game in the first round, they've won eight straight road games since, an NBA playoff record. And again, part of the reason is there's so many Knicks fans that have been traveling on the road. Towns, goes inside right at Vassell, shot blocked by Wemby. Spurs ball. Champagnie, extra pass, Wemby running the floor, throws it down. Anunoby, five of 24, goes right at Wemby, shot blocked again, got a piece of it. Three blocks already for... Castle whips it to Johnson, Johnson right off the bench, gets inside, floats it up, shot short, Wembanyama tips it in. Towns kicks it out, Anunoby gets as clean look, three-pointer's good. Knicks are 2-for-13 from the field. Harper gets in the paint, the floater's up, and good! Look at the score, and there's only three minutes remaining here in the first. Count it! A 10-point lead. For the fifth straight game, the Spurs have had a double-figure lead in the first quarter. There have been very few easy possessions for the Knicks. Brunson falling away, jumper, that goes. Fox guarding Brunson, Champagnie quickly picks him up. Shot clock winding down again. Long three-pointer. Jalen Brunson for three. And getting the Knicks multiple opportunities, because they have a second primary ball handler. Blocked by Wembanyama again! Number four already! Seven to shoot, Towns drives. Doubled, finds Shamet, Shamet goes right at Wemby, blocked again! It's a Wembanyama block party here in the first half! Towns against Castle, late in the shot clock again. Winding down, just gets it off in time and gets it to go. Towns wanted a push-off. Wemby sets, three-pointer, got it! Victor Wembanyama from downtown! It's a 16-point lead. Shot clock again winding down. Seems every possession that's the way for the Knicks. Kicks it out, good pass to the corner, Bridges knocks down the three. That's only their sixth field goal. Harper, nine points already off the bench. Pulls up, jump shot, ho ho! He is a bucket maker. Pace on that little pull-up jumper, didn't rush it. Mikal Bridges kicks it up top. Hart's open three-pointer, that goes down. Knicks starting to hit their threes now. Hart...

title: The Highest-Paid Podcasters Of 2026
transcription:
Today on Forbes, the highest paid podcasters of 2026.

When Jay Shetty started his podcast, On Purpose, in 2019, he remembers people telling him he was too late. The medium was already saturated, they said, with little room for growth. And wasn't he really just a content creator?

Seven years later, the 38-year-old self-help guru hosts one of the most popular podcasts in the world, competing not only with the biggest TV, radio, and internet-native talk shows, but blurring the lines between them entirely. Just as many people watch his lengthy interviews with celebrities, including Michelle Obama and Matt Damon, on YouTube, as listen on the iHeartMedia Network. Distribution deals that Forbes estimates paid Shetty $21 million over the past 12 months.

And when those deals expired this year, Shetty landed a new kind of contract, in which the audio and video of his show will not only be distributed by Spotify, it will also stream on Netflix, with the two companies combining to pay him an estimated $100 million over the next 3 years. Shetty tells Forbes, quote, "When I started, video wasn't normal for a podcast. Now we have the four largest streamers bidding for the show. To see that kind of interest and enthusiasm was pretty amazing, for me and for the industry overall."

The impressive thing about mega-deals like Shetty's is that, unlike the makers of movies, TV, or other forms of entertainment, podcasters retain ownership of their shows' underlying IP, meaning networks and platforms are paying millions just to license it as a distributor and ad sales partner for a set number of years. That's one reason why premium streaming giants like Netflix, Hulu, and Tubi had largely ignored the industry's rise over the past decade, allowing YouTube to grow into the largest podcasting platform in the world.

But beginning in 2025, hoping to cut into YouTube's dominance over engagement time, the streamers have made a splashy entrance. Industry dealmakers say that after Netflix's initial $1 million to $2 million bids for top podcasts were roundly rejected, the streamer adopted a strategy similar to the one it used previously to capture market share in scripted television: overpaying to lure talent away from incumbent platforms. Offers of $10 million or more per year, on a one- or two-year trial term, eventually convinced marquee shows from Spotify, iHeart, and Barstool Sports to sign on. Goalhanger, a UK-based podcast network, reportedly landed $19 million from Netflix to stream just 40 episodes of its daily talk show, The Rest Is Football, during the World Cup. Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said during the company's earnings call earlier this year, quote,

title: 2026: The Year of the SAP Business One Web Client | Interview with Darius Heydarian & Martin Gore
transcription: Hi, Darius, thanks for today's discussion. I really liked your recent LinkedIn post where you mentioned 2026 is the year of the SAP Business One Web Client, with great innovations planned for the 26.02 and the 26.08 release. As Head of Partner Enablement for SAP Business One and Computec as an ISV and SSP, I believe we we share a common goal, and that common goal is to enable partners in their journey from the desktop to the Web Client. Right. So, with that in mind, what are your enablement plans for for 2026? Yeah. Thanks first for having me, Martin, and, yeah, you're absolutely right. We are heading in the same direction here, and for the enablement plans, I can tell that there are many new features and innovations coming to the Web Client starting now in February with the FP 26.02 and also then later this year in August with the FP 26.08 release. There will be new features and innovations including like the new process map, the document generation, and the procurement confirmation wizard and many more to come. But, yeah, let me turn the the question quickly back to you, actually. What is your plan with Computec to support partners in their transformation to the Web Client? Yeah, Darius, that's a great question. Thank you. So, in in Q4 2025, Computec brought several innovator solutions to the marketplace, uh, to support partners in their Web Client journey. Uh, the first The first is the Computec Web App. This is a customization and automation toolkit. It gives partners great flexibility to adapt the look and feel of the Web Client, uh, to improve user experience. Uh, the first, for example, uh, moving fields, hiding fields, uh, adding context to user defined fields by placing them in the right logical sections, uh, as well as data validations and automations and of course with more enhancements coming soon. And then secondly, we have Computec App Engine. This is a platform which allows partners to develop tightly coupled SAPUI5 based extensions, uh, and apps for the Web Client. Uh, it also includes full lifecycle management and built-in channels for things like OpenTelemetry. Quick question for you, have you seen these solutions, and if you have, then, you know, what's your perspective on them?

title: KZN Top Business Awards 2026: Interview with Carol Ofori
transcription: Hi, my name is Chelsea and I'm from KZN Top Business and we are here today with Carol Ofori from East Coast Radio. Yeah. Carol, you are no stranger to celebrating amazing people and businesses, and speaking about that, within the KZN community. Absolutely. What excites you most about stepping into the role as MC for KZN Top Business Awards? Well look, I'm always excited to do the KZN Top Business Awards. I think it is such a motivating space for businesses. Um, KZN the landscape we've had so many challenges, socio-economic and these businesses stand the ground, they provide employment which in turn provides dignity for our people. So anything that does something like this and uplifts our community, I'm always excited to be a part of it. And I've been doing it for a few years now, and I'm always honored and like, surprised when I'm called back, because it means I'm doing something right. So the KZN Top Business Awards celebrates community improvement, sustainability, resilience. Um, why do you think that it's important that we recognize and celebrate the businesses thriving of our province? I think it's so important, you know, um like I said, for businesses in KZN to continue to show up, to continue to provide employment, to continue to encourage because when people, young people see businesses thriving, we know that unemployment is so rife in our country, in our province. And when businesses employ and they win awards, it gives others encouragement to go out there and start their own businesses because entrepreneurship is a space where we going to create employment, but not wait for employment. So it's it's really a space that just says to, to, to so many that it's possible. Yes. I mean, when your neighbor owns a business, when your cousin owns a business, when you hear these businesses are driven by families. It's so encouraging and so uplifting. So yeah, it's, it's great. So, these awards bring businesses of all sizes under one roof. Yeah. Why do you think that the impact of that is important? I think it's important because the smaller businesses can learn from the bigger businesses and the bigger businesses can look back at their achievements to say we come from here. And it sort of just resets and makes you realize where you started and

The only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, "behind bars." After the three-hour hearing ended, Senator Paul told reporters he plans to schedule a vote next week to hold Dr. Fauci in contempt of Congress. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson joins us now. She's also professor of at Loyola Law School in Los Angeles. So, Jessica, did Dr. Fauci have the right to invoke the Fifth Amendment? Can he get punished or held in contempt for doing so? So, yes and yes. He absolutely has the right, like the rest of us, to invoke his right against self-incrimination. Uh, the question is whether or not, as you said, he could be held in contempt for exercising that right. And I think the answer is likely not, but only because President Biden issued a broad pardon for Dr. Fauci. And so, the idea is that if you are pardoned, if you can't face any criminal liability, at least with respect to federal crimes, then you should potentially be forced to answer, that you shouldn't be able to invoke your Fifth Amendment right without repercussions. title: Heather Cox Richardson: Feb 23, 2026 Video Summary - Trump Defies Court, Tariffs & SOTU Boycott
transcription: All right, let's dive in. Today we're going to unpack a really chaotic weekend that, honestly, pushed American democracy right to its limits. We're going to look at how a direct, pretty unprecedented showdown between the president and the Supreme court unfolded, and in doing so, tested the very foundations of the rule of law. So where did this all kick off? Well, it started right here with this absolutely explosive social media post. I mean, in a single message, the president didn't just defy the nation's highest court, he actually claimed their ruling against him somehow made him even more powerful. This post right here set the stage for a major constitutional confrontation. So, how did a constitutional conflict like this ignite so quickly? The thing is, this whole confrontation just escalated over the course of one single chaotic weekend. Let's walk through the timeline. Okay, just look at how this played out. On Friday, the Supreme Court comes out and rules the president's tariffs are unconstitutional. Now, these were tariffs he levied under a specific law for national emergencies. But then, just hours later, he openly defies them, announcing a new 10% tariff anyway. By Saturday, he's on social media, hiking it up to 15%. And then, by Monday morning, we get that post where he claims the court's decision actually expanded his authority. We're talking 72 hours where a Supreme Court ruling was not just ignored, but completely flipped on its head. And this, right here, really gets to the core of the whole thing. On one side, you have the court's official judgment, a clear check on executive power. And on the other, the president's direct rebuttal, basically saying he doesn't need Congress. It's that classic constitutional friction point, right? The judiciary's check on power being met with a declaration of unchecked authority. And look, this whole showdown wasn't just some abstract debate about the constitution. It had immediate, very real world consequences for the economy and for America's standing on the world stage. The international reaction was swift and, frankly, pretty bewildered. The head of the European Parliament's Trade Committee, Bernd Lange, he just called it pure tariff chaos. And his statement really captures that global feeling of instability, which led the EU Parliament to immediately propose pausing a major trade deal with the US. And the fallout wasn't just limited to Europe. Officials from India, who were literally about to finalize their own trade agreement, they postponed their trip to the US. And at the same time, back home, all this uncertainty sent shudders through the financial system, with the stock market falling pretty sharply. Now, what's really fascinating here is how the American public already felt about all this. Even before this constitutional crisis blew up, a poll from ABC News and the Washington Post showed that nearly two-thirds of Americans already disapproved of the president's handling of tariffs in the first place.

title: Heather Cox Richardson Video Summary: Supreme Court Expands Presidential Power (June 29, 2026)
transcription: For over a century, unassuming buildings like this have served as the quiet engine rooms of the American government. Inside, thousands of civil servants do the unglamorous work of regulating markets and keeping the country running. Starting in the late 19th century, Congress began building a specific feature into these independent agencies. They were intentionally designed as bipartisan bodies, deliberately insulated from the direct control of the President. The logic was simple. Keeping the air clean, ensuring consumer products are safe, and stopping monopolies requires technical expertise that doesn't change with every election. By keeping the executive branch at arm's length, Congress created a buffer. It guaranteed that decisions affecting public safety and financial security were driven by scientists and economists rather than political favors. In a single morning, with a landmark 6-to-3 decision, the Supreme Court erased over 90 years of established legal doctrine. President Trump immediately hailed the decision as a monumental victory, calling it the largest expansion of presidential power in over a century. He is correct about the scale of the change. The ruling legally grants the President the power to fire the head of any independent agency at any time for any reason. To understand how a foundational power of the United States government was dismantled overnight, we have to look at the legal theory that made it possible. The test case began in March 2025. The President abruptly fired Rebecca Slaughter, the last remaining Democratic member of the Federal Trade Commission. Since 1935, the standard for removing someone from these commissions was strict. You had to prove neglect of duty or malfeasance. But Trump argued he could fire her because her presence was inconsistent with his administration's priorities. This defense relies on the unitary executive theory, a framework conservative strategists have built since the 1980s. The core argument: as head of the executive branch, the President holds absolute authority over everything within it. No other branch can limit his control. By neutralizing Congress's ability to shield these agencies, this theory bypasses the legislative process. It takes national regulatory power and concentrates it into the hands of one person.

title: FP1 Highlights | 2026 Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix
transcription: A brand new race at a very familiar circuit. First practice ahead of the inaugural Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix. George Russell has been disappointed by recent results. A combination of bad luck, poor planning, and a teammate in white-hot form have left him 68 points back in the driver standings, now in third place behind Lewis Hamilton. But he found something in FP1 in Barcelona, topping the tables with a lap time of 1 minute 16.363. Ferrari have brought a slew of upgrades to Spain, including a new front wing and endplate, a redesigned floor, reshaped sidepods, and amendments to the diffuser. Added to the changes already brought in Miami, the Scuderia will be hoping these new bits will bring them much closer to Mercedes. title: Day 1 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 1
transcription: F1 is back for the first official test session of the season. All 11 teams and 22 drivers are present for 6 days of running across 2 weeks at the Bahrain International Circuit. McLaren entered the 2026 season as reigning back-to-back Constructors' Champions, and it was Oscar Piastri in the car for the morning of Day 1. The Aussie, who had battled for last season's Drivers' Championship until the very final round, was on the pace from the off in Bahrain. Despite McLaren running just over half the number of laps of Mercedes in Barcelona, the Woking-based outfit were raring to go in Bahrain. Piastri, second fastest in the morning session, just 2/10 of a second behind Max Verstappen. The Australian gave Turn 10 a wide berth following Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, but completed 54 laps before the lunch break. 2025 World Champion Lando Norris took over for the afternoon session, topping the Day 1 times with a 1:34.669. The Brit added a further 58 laps to McLaren's total, ensuring they ended the day with well over 100 tours of the circuit. George Russell was the only driver other than the title protagonists to win a Grand Prix in 2025, the Brit victorious on two occasions at Canada and Singapore. And the Silver Arrows were in fine form throughout shakedown, logging 500 laps in Barcelona, more than any other team. On to Bahrain, and Mercedes were again getting the laps in. Russell ran the morning session, completing 56 laps, before teammate Kimi Antonelli took over for the afternoon. The Brit did have a little trouble at the off-camber Turn 10, running wide on three separate occasions. Antonelli's running was delayed after Mercedes found an issue while changing setups, but the Italian was able to hit the track, completing 30 laps despite a wild snap at Turn 4. Team Principal Toto Wolff, offering his thoughts on Mercedes' progress so far: "I think everything goes according to the plan we have. You know, it isn't smooth sailing. We have complication on car balance, which are a little bit more articulated here than they were in Barcelona, obviously due to the hot conditions. And we've seen a very, very strong Verstappen this morning. So, you know, we have to get our act together, all of us, and then maybe by the end of the test we will understand more whether what we've done is good, and good enough." Max Verstappen described 2025 as his greatest-ever season, just 2 points away from a fifth world title, despite driving a car which, quote, "he hated at times". title: FP2 Highlights | 2026 Monaco Grand Prix
transcription: Second practice in Monte Carlo. F1's finest with another hour of track time ahead to really get to grips with the Circuit de Monaco. Many have touted Ferrari as the team to beat on this narrow, twisty course, where downforce rather than extreme speed rules. And so it proved in FP1 when Charles Leclerc had been fastest from teammate Lewis Hamilton. The seven-time world champion, playing catch up in this session, he flirted with disaster on an early quick lap. Oh, you just feel it's a place that you can split a Formula One car in two if you get it wrong. It's that difficult and that high speed with no barrier margin. Three times a winner on these streets, he continued to push throughout the session, locking up approaching the Nouvelle Chicane, and then taking a whole bunch of curb at the same spot the next time around. My word, that's more curb than I've seen so far down at that chicane, I think. Hamilton on the, on the edge of rear grip, pings it over the curb, bounces through. And it was the Briton with the bragging rights in this session. His lap of 1 minute 13.026, more than a tenth quicker than Leclerc's best effort for P2. The teammates even had a little race after the flag. Great foretaste perhaps for Sunday's main event. Max Verstappen had not been entirely happy with his ride in FP1, despite a decent P3 performance. This time out, he seemed much more hooked up, especially on the soft tires, and managed the same placing again. Only this time, he was a bit closer to the Scuderia drivers. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar, who crashed out of FP1, was P6 this time around, his mechanics working wonders in the interim. There was a hairy moment for George Russell early doors. Oh my word, the car getting loose through the first part of the swimming pool. He will need an underwear change. He was later blocked on a fast lap by a slow-moving Gabriel Bortoleto. The Briton believes he's had more than his fair share of bad luck so far this season, but was upbeat coming into the weekend, feeling the odds would even out across the year. He's currently P2 in the drivers' championship, some 43 points behind Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, but he was one place ahead of the Italian in second practice, P4 after the hour. It was a short session for reigning world champion and defending Monaco master, Lando Norris, who encountered a technical problem...

title: FP2 Highlights | 2026 Austrian Grand Prix

By contrast, teammate George Russell's best time was more than half a second back, and only good enough for P6. Much of Western Europe is currently engulfed in a heatwave, and consequently, this weekend's Grand Prix in Spielberg has been designated as a heat hazard race. Drivers will have a body cooling system available to them, which delivers chilled liquid through a series of pipes into a jacket worn beneath their overalls. It's optional, and those choosing not to use the apparatus will have to carry 5 kg of ballast to even out the weight between the cars. Lando Norris went for a spin at turn three. Strapping on the softs a bit later, the Briton took a wide line out of turn seven and touched the gravel on the approach to eight. He managed to stay out of trouble. He was clearly pushing hard as this post-session radio exchange makes clear. And can we cool the brakes from the... help us cool the brakes? Yeah, I think some brakes have been on fire for like five laps. Yeah, they are hot. McLaren have planned to test an experimental rear wing this weekend. It was due to debut on Norris's car in FP1, but the defending champ missed most of the session. When he did appear, he had the standard fin on the back. Both Mercedes and Red Bull suggested the other were the team to beat after one week of running in Bahrain. Mercedes were top of the pile on week one, setting the fastest lap, more than half a second quicker than anyone else. But Red Bull logged over 60 more laps than the German outfit across the week, albeit neither team were in the top five of laps completed. Ferrari sporting director Laurent Mekies played down their chances ahead of the season. We very well know the size of the mountain that is still in front of us, we just had a, a very good start at it. title: Day 2 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 1
transcription: Day two of testing in Bahrain. Eight further hours of running for teams and drivers to better understand their 2026 machines. Turn 10 was once again a talking point on the second day of running. The tricky off-camber corner caught out the majority of the runners on day one. And it was Sergio Pérez first to head off-piste after a big lockup in his Red Bull. The Mexican also brought out the day's first red flag, his team quickly fixing the issue, allowing him to return to the action soon after. But it was Alex Albon who locked up, not once, not twice, not thrice, but four times into the troublesome turn 10. The Thai driver also had a mishap at turn one on two occasions before setting the fifth fastest time of the morning. Two of the most experienced drivers weren't immune to a mishap either, both Fernando Alonso and Nico Hülkenberg locking up and running off at the 10th turn. Despite this, the German was optimistic with the progress made in Bahrain so far. I think good step forward in terms of performance, in terms of reliability and just, you know, being able to get laps in, to get kilometers on the car. We've made some some big steps forward there, you know, between Barcelona and here. Then, you know, Bahrain is a very, very different circuit to Barcelona, you know, much more stop-and-go, low-speed dominated. It's a very hard, you know, and unforgiving track that really exposes a lot of weaknesses usually, you know, and historically from from any car because the rough tarmac, kind of low grip, very windy, hot track temp, so, you know, it's a there isn't many other, you know, tracks that or where you find the harder conditions. So it's a it's a true good test. Teammate Gabriel Bortoleto would take over for the afternoon, the Brazilian struggling for purchase as he tested the limits of his 2026 challenger. It's uh it's like teaching a baby how to walk and and talk, and um yeah, we need to do this uh as quick as possible and uh in a good way as well. Charles Leclerc started the day for Ferrari, having set over 130 laps alongside Lewis Hamilton on Wednesday. The Monégasque driver claimed seven podiums last season but was unable to add to his eight Formula One race victories. A positive week in Spain...

transcription: The paddock had eyes for just one team on Thursday morning. Now, watch it go back into corner mode. There you go, the wing has fully rotated around. Ferrari has discovered something quite clever in the regulations, I feel. It doesn't specify that the wing has to be mounted the right way up when the active aero is deployed. An upside-down wing, aircraft wing configuration, should reduce aerodynamic drag because it's even generating a bit of lift, and then they've come up with a mechanism to allow it to rotate all the way around. title: Sneak peek at 'Piper Rockelle: Barely Legal'
transcription: Now with the story of scandal and survival involving one of YouTube's biggest child stars, Juju Chang is here with more on this. Hey Juju. Hey guys, good morning. You know, Piper Rockelle was absolutely a YouTube darling making jaw-dropping amounts of money as a tween, but she says scandal cost her everything. Now her pivot to more risque content has also been jaw-dropping. She sat down with us for her first extensive TV interview addressing all the controversy to make it clear she's in charge. Hey, it is Piper Rockelle and welcome to my vlog. One of the biggest former kid influencers on YouTube with millions of subscribers when she was just 12, now 18 and taking on her detractors. Some of your critics say, well, you know, Piper never got to be a kid, that your childhood was all work or maybe even worse, a facade. I had one of the best childhoods. Like, I wouldn't change it. I had to become the person that I am today. I'm the luckiest person alive, honest. Raised by a single mom in Georgia, Piper went from pageants to social media and hit it big on YouTube with her squad, a group of kids that made viral content from challenges to pranks. I'm not doing this alone. I'm inviting my whole entire squad over today. Come on, girls. Her mom, Tiffany Smith, in the director's chair for it all. Tiffany has the creative mind and Piper has the she just wants to do it. Today we're going to be playing headbands. We are going to be filling this huge bathtub... Piper reportedly making $400,000 to $500,000 a month. How old were you when you realized you were the breadwinner in the family? I don't know, I never really thought of it that way, kind of. I just felt like it was a team effort. I didn't just think that this was my thing and all this money is mine. But in 2022, it all came crashing down. In 2022, 11 former members of the squad filed a lawsuit, and they alleged emotional, verbal, physical, and at times, sexual abuse. They sought $22 million in damages, and the claims in the lawsuit are incredibly harrowing. The suit was filed against Piper's mom, Tiffany Smith, her company, Piper Rockelle, Inc., and the squad's videographer, Hunter Hill. Now, Piper and her family addressing the aftermath of the lawsuit and the Netflix doc, "Bad Influence," for the first time on network TV. All of these allegations that were lodged mostly against your mom, are you saying they're untrue?

title: Outdoor Boys Told Law Grads What No Professor Would
transcription: Some, some people call me a survival expert. Well, as a survival expert, I want to clear up a common misconception. Survival is not something we just do in the woods. It's something each and every one of us has to do every single day. And whether you're building a fire, gutting a moose, or drafting a motion, we're just trying to survive as best we can with the resources we have. So, I would like to help give you some advice to survive whatever is coming next. And while I do not know what your future holds, I can tell you that the world is changing at a terrifying and fascinating pace. You know, so, here I am, I'm 47 years old, I'm not properly old yet, and, I've seen some crazy stuff. I remember watching the Berlin Wall come down live on television as a child. I remember hearing about the internet for the first time, and I thought it was a fake. I thought, I didn't understand that. I was an adult the first time I ever saw an email. I was married when 9/11 happened. And the year before I went to law school, this thing called YouTube was invented. I was practicing for 3 years before I ever got my first social media account. I've seen 7 US wars, 6 recessions, and I've survived one global pandemic so far. I'm only 47. I don't know what the next 40 years holds for you. But, I doubt any of us are going to get through it without seeing terrible and amazing things. We don't know what these changes are going to be, but we do know they're coming. You need to be ready to grab the opportunities that are going to come in this changing world. And, you need to be ready to survive the storms. And, the best survival advice I can give you is very pragmatic. I would say, save some money. It's pretty simple, but it's not. The best, the most important things are often simple, but hard to do.

title: Hannah Harper Auditions With Original Song About Her Postpartum Depression - American Idol
transcription: I'm going to sing an original that I wrote called String Cheese. You're like my favorite person, you're wearing homemade clothes, you're singing songs called String Cheese. What's the song about? My youngest is one, and shortly after he was born I had postpartum depression, and so I was sitting on my couch, I said I wasn't going to cry. I was sitting on my couch wallowing. And you have boys, you know, everybody wants to touch you, and I didn't want to be touched. And my youngest son, like I was just having a pity party and praying that the Lord would calm my, calm my spirit. And my son kept coming up to me, he was like, "Mom, open this. Mom, open this, open my cheese." I'm like, "Dude, leave me alone with the doggone cheese." And I finally opened his cheese, and when I did, I realized that God had put me in that place, and that where I was in my house was the biggest ministry that I could ever have. And being a mom, so I gathered myself and I got up off the couch, and I quit throwing a pity party, and I realized that that was exactly what I wanted. And I kind of kicked the postpartum depression in the butt, and I said, "I ain't doing it." There you go. So I wrote this song called String Cheese. Do you need a second? I want to give you like Probably just give me one second. Yeah, yeah. It, I can't, I can't cry and sing, so. I don't, I don't want to put you in that position. Here. Thank you so much. Love it. Ready? I think so. I warm my morning coffee up for the third time. Miss Rachel on the TV with their favorite nursery rhyme. Hot Wheels and little people under my feet. Baby's crying, it's pure chaos, but I don't miss a beat. Always knew that a nine-to-five wouldn't suit me very good. But my hours are extended, that's just motherhood. I never knew this is what my 20s would look like, but they saved me before I had the chance to waste my life. One day I'll be alone with a hot, fresh cup of Joe, wishing that someone would just drop by. And I'll sit and reminisce on times that I sure miss.

title: YouTuber ‘Reckless Ben’ BREAKS SILENCE amid legal battle over missing Legos | Jesse Weber Live
transcription: Tonight, Reckless Ben is here. Yeah, in just a minute, the YouTube star is going to talk with us exclusively about his big legal win in the mystery of the missing LEGO. Yep, a judge just granted him the right to talk again. This is a big development. I got to give you a background though, a quick look at how this whole LEGO legal drama unfolded, okay? It all started when an Oregon family entrusted a franchise of a chain called Bricks & Minifigs to sell their reportedly $200,000 Star Wars LEGO set on consignment. But, the franchise was apparently sold, and the LEGO owners say they never got their LEGO, they never got paid. Now, the family sued the franchise claiming their agreement was breached, that Bricks & Minifigs stole the LEGO collection, and that is when Reckless Ben got on the case. He allegedly traveled to Utah where the franchise executive lives, reportedly started documenting attempts to make contact at his property, posted videos, all going viral. The executive apparently called police, led to Ben getting arrested twice, and as we reported, Bricks & Minifigs also filed a lawsuit against Ben. And, that brings us to this week. Ben is facing a total of four criminal charges. They're all misdemeanors. Provo, Utah, he's charged with disorderly conduct, also reportedly commercial obstruction for allegedly going to the Bricks & Minifigs corporate headquarters. Ben tells us he was there to ask for the LEGOs back. Over in American Fork, Utah, he's charged with stalking and residential picketing for allegedly going to the franchise owner, Josh Johnson's house. Now, Reckless Ben just scored a big legal win. This is when a Utah federal court, this judge lifted the ban that had been on him, posting videos related to Bricks & Minifigs. This was a TRO. However, the revised order still prohibits Ben from coming within 100 meters of any Bricks & Minifigs stores or offices, prevents him from making any threats. Now, we've reached out to Bricks & Minifigs for a statement today, but we haven't heard back. The company has maintained it does not have the LEGO, and in a statement to local media, they said that this issue in its civil case against Ben, real name, Ben Schneider, is going to be addressed through private mediation. It hopes to resolve everything in the coming weeks. But for now, Ben says he got his freedom back, his freedom of speech back. He's already made a new, a new YouTube video. Here's an exclusive sneak peek.

transcription: ഹായ് ഫ്രണ്ട്സ്, എല്ലാവർക്കും നമ്മുടെ പുതിയൊരു വീഡിയോയിലേക്ക് സ്വാഗതം. നമ്മളിന്ന് നോക്കാൻ പോകുന്നത് ജെ.ആർ.സി.-യുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട ചോദ്യങ്ങളാണ്. അപ്പോ ജെ.ആർ.സി. എക്സാമിന് ചോദിക്കാൻ സാധ്യതയുള്ള കുറച്ചു പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട അടിസ്ഥാന വിവരങ്ങളാണ് ഈ ഒരു വീഡിയോയിലൂടെ നമ്മൾ നോക്കുന്നത്. അപ്പൊ എല്ലാവരും വീഡിയോ മുഴുവനായിട്ടും കാണുക. നിങ്ങൾക്കായി ഒരു സ്പെഷ്യൽ ക്വസ്റ്റ്യൻ അവസാനം കാത്തിരിപ്പുണ്ട്. ആ ക്വസ്റ്റ്യന്റെ ഉത്തരം അറ്റൻഡ് ചെയ്യുകയും ചെയ്യുക. അപ്പോ ആദ്യമായിട്ടാണ് ഈയൊരു ചാനൽ നിങ്ങൾ കാണുന്നതെങ്കിൽ പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ ഒന്ന് സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്തു വെച്ചോളൂ. നിങ്ങൾക്ക് യൂസ്ഫുൾ ആയിട്ടുള്ള ഒരുപാട് വീഡിയോസ് ലഭിക്കുന്നതായിരിക്കും. അപ്പോ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് ഇനി ഏത് വീഡിയോയാണ് വേണ്ടത് എന്നുള്ളത് കമൻറ് ചെയ്യാൻ മറക്കരുത് കേട്ടോ. അപ്പോ നമുക്ക് പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ ഓരോ ചോദ്യങ്ങളായിട്ട് നോക്കാം. ആദ്യത്തെ ചോദ്യം ഇതാണ്. ജെ.ആർ.സി.-യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ജെ.ആർ.സി.-യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം, ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്. ജെ.ആർ.സി. എന്നാൽ എന്താണ്? ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് എന്നാണ് ജെ.ആർ.സി.-യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം, റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സംഘടനയുടെ സ്ഥാപകൻ ആര്? റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സംഘടനയുടെ സ്ഥാപകൻ ആരാണ്? ഉത്തരം വരുന്നത്, ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ്. ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് എന്നാണ് ജെ.ആർ.സി. സംഘടനയുടെ സ്ഥാപകന്റെ പേര്. മറന്നുപോകരുത്, പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ടതാണ്. ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് ആണ് ജെ.ആർ.സി. സംഘടന സ്ഥാപിച്ചത്. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം, ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് ജനിച്ചത് എപ്പോഴാണ്? ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് ജനിച്ചത് എപ്പോഴാണ്? അപ്പോ, 1828 മെയ് 8-നാണ് ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് ജനിച്ചത്. ജനീവയിലാണ് അദ്ദേഹം ജനിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത്. ഏതാണ് വർഷം? 1828 മെയ് 8-ന് ജനീവയിൽ ജനിച്ചു. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യത്തിലേക്ക് കടക്കാം. ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ് ദിനം എന്നാണ് ആചരിക്കുന്നത്? ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ് ദിനം എന്നാണ് ആചരിക്കുന്നത്? ഉത്തരം, മെയ് 8. അപ്പോ നമ്മൾ പറഞ്ഞു ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് ജനിച്ചത് 1828 മെയ് 8-നാണ്. അപ്പൊ അദ്ദേഹത്തിൻറെ ജന്മദിനമാണ് ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ് ദിനമായി ആചരിക്കുന്നത്. ഏതാണ് ദിവസം? മെയ് 8. മെയ് 8-നാണ് ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ് ദിനം. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യത്തിലേക്ക് കടക്കുന്നു.

title: Haley Stevens vs Abdul El-Sayed: How Dems can regain trust from Jewish, Arab-American voters
transcription: And we'll dive right into that right now. You've heard many people ask the question about AIPAC, and it seems as though on many instances, you haven't directly answered the question. Do you see why some people are bothered by the fact that so much money, $40+ million, has come from AIPAC, uh, for these PACs to talk about you and to promote you and to put them, put you up as their candidate? Yeah, and I, I appreciate the question, Roop, because this moment in this country and here in Michigan, people have every right to be frustrated about our campaign finance system. My opponent here on the stage, Abdul, he's got a super PAC that his father-in-law funds that has millions of dollars going into it. And look, in terms of foreign policy, you know, Abdul and I do differ. I believe in a two-state solution. He has attacked me by name for purporting that the people of Palestine and the people of Israel deserve to live side by side, peacefully. The goal is always long-term peace. And also, the Prime Minister of Israel has attacked me by name. They both represent the extremes. Look, Michiganders want peace, they deserve to see peace, and that is where I have always cast my vote, and the, that is the work that I want to do for Michigan and the US. But Congresswoman, specifically about AIPAC money, more than $46 million has been spent on AIPAC spending to back your campaign. A lot of people wonder if that is something where there, you know, you're going to do their bidding when you, should you win this seat. Is that something should, people should be concerned about, and if not, why not? Absolutely not, Roop. Look, I have been very clear, consistent, and transparent. And I have continued to be. I want to see long-term peace. I want to see a two-state solution. I am deeply proud to represent one of the largest Jewish populations in, uh, a congressional district in the country. This is a community that I have grieved alongside, that I've mourned alongside, and have fought to bring the hostages home. And I'm still working to get us to long-term peace. But no concern about the $46 million plus spent on the behalf of AIPAC that should worry people about perhaps you doing their bidding, should you win the seat? transcription: क्या बुलाऊँ आपको, खान सर या बाहुबली फैजल खान? फैजल खान फैजल खान... फैजल खान और... फैजल खान का हाथ... फैजल खान चर्चा में आए... जिन बच्चों को हमने पढ़ाया है, हम आज भी उनके लिए खान सर हैं और कल भी खान सर रहेंगे। हमारे ससुराल वाले हमको फैजल खान कहते हैं। जो हमें ससुराल पक्ष का समझता है, जो जीजा मानता है, वो फैजल खान कहते हैं। आपको हमारा रोशन सर का इंटरव्यू कैसा लगा? title: Ransom Note Clues Revealed | Jesse Weber Live
transcription:
6 months ago tonight. This is after 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Tucson-area home. The Pima, the Pima County Sheriff's Office has finally released the alleged ransom notes that were supposedly sent by these alleged kidnappers. Now, as you may know, these notes have been the source of more than a little controversy in the months since Today Show host Savannah Guthrie's mother vanished, mostly because we still don't know if they're real. And though the cops still won't verify their authenticity, because of something that I'm going to get into in just a little bit, it is important to read them in full. So here we go. The first alleged note that was apparently sent on February 2nd says this, "Hello, Savannah. We have your mother, Nancy. She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom and once payment is received, she will be released unharmed. We will be holding her for a maximum of 7 days. You will need to send Bitcoin in the amount of $4 million USD, United States Dollars, before 5:00 p.m. on Thursday the 5th. If payment is not received, the ransom will be increased to $6 million USD, which will need to be paid by 5:00 p.m. on Monday the 9th. Once payment is received to the Bitcoin address below, she will be released within 12 hours of deposit to a safe drop-off location back in Tucson. If payment is not received by the last deadline on Monday the 9th at 5:00 p.m., she will be killed. Your mother is aware of this, and her life is in your hands. It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible. You will not be able to contact me from here on out. There will be no negotiation. Do not play games. Law enforcement will not be able to help you. She had a white smartwatch on the floor of the foot of her bed, and the white floodlight in back yard was destroyed."

Then you have the second alleged note. Very different, very different tone. This was apparently sent on February 6th, so 3 days before the deadline from that first note. It says, "Guthrie family, we did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart-related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this, and hope you can find peace. We are truly sorry."

Now, despite the fact that the Sheriff's Office couldn't authenticate the notes, they are now asking for the public's help in finding whoever wrote them. Said in a press release, quote, "These communications reveal distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax, and phraseology that reflect the writer's unique linguistic style. We believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the note's writer."
