title: God sees the heart
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Yeah. They say the quiet ones scream the loudest. Guess we didn't hear it in time. This is for Nick. Yeah. You walked in smiling, jokes ready on your lips, light in the room, yeah, everybody felt it. But behind closed doors, you were fighting your head, carrying wars that you never once said. You were strong for the world, weak when alone, learned early on how to suffer in silence. Bullied as a kid taught you how to put armor on, smile like you're fine when you're dying inside it. Divorce on your shoulders, books on your back, trying to build a future while your past kept attacking. People saw progress, grades, and ambition, never saw depression rewriting the mission. Funny how pain can hide in plain sight. Funny how "I'm good" can really mean "I'm done tonight." If love could have saved you, you'd still be here, so I won't blame myself, but damn, it's hard to accept it. You didn't show it, you didn't say it, you carried it alone, yeah. You tried to brave it, but God sees hearts, not the masks we wear. He knew you were sick, he knew you were scared. He judged the ending, ignore the fight, ignore the nights you survived somehow. God sees hearts, yeah, deeper than scars. He knows who you were, not just how you're gone. Left behind a little girl with your eyes, two years old, too young to ask why. That's the part that breaks me, tears me apart. How does a loving dad end up here in the dark? But pain lies, it twists what's true, tells you the world's better off without you. That's illness talking, not your love, not the man we knew, not the father you were. You weren't weak.

title: Sustainability Strategy Masterclass: Engagement
transcription:
So now we've
now we know why we want a sustainability strategy. I'm going to move on to engagement, which is the process of collating views from your stakeholders to understand which themes are most important to them, because typically a sustainability strategy is led by an individual or one or two individuals within an organisation. And it's really important to make sure that the ideas that they come up with are able to contribute towards the wider goals of the business and are themes that everybody will be comfortable working towards, and that's where this engagement process comes in. Before you begin engaging your stakeholders, though, I always recommend taking a bit of time to prepare. So, that's understanding the organisational priorities, whether that's reading strategy documents, whether it's your own experience from having worked in the organisation, whether your parent company... so, a lot of the organisations that we work with, um, will be coming up with a sustainability strategy for their business, but they'll have a parent organisation, maybe it's a private equity fund, maybe it's, um, an overarching corporate parent that will have already set out, um, their organisational priorities, and it's important to understand what those are so you can ensure alignment with them. Similarly, looking at regulation, looking at what your business actually needs to do, whether that's reporting on carbon, whether that's reporting on, um, whether the the materials you're buying, if they've been involved in deforestation, which is what you need to do for EUDR. And then similarly to what we said about looking at what your competitors are doing, looking at what those industry best practices are, are there voluntary standards that your industry is signing up to? And the reason that I think it's always worth taking a bit of time to research these topics and to prepare is that you want to go into your conversations with your stakeholders able to really paint a picture of where your organisation is and what commitments it's already made so that you can be respectful of their time and have a really valuable discussion. On the same vein of making the most of your stakeholder's time, I always recommend spending just 15, 20 minutes writing down the names and the job titles of all the people within your organisation and around your organisation that will be pivotal to making change. So, is your organisation's culture quite top-down? Is it that you need a senior leader to be, um, speaking in a... in a town hall about sustainability to really put it on everybody's radar? But the the real challenge is finding original pieces that give a space identity, carry a genuine history, and create a connection people want to live with. I create one-of-a-kind mixed media artworks using found objects and my original photography. These materials already carry traces of real lives, and I transform them into pieces that give collectors and interior designers something increasingly valuable: artwork with identity, a story, and lasting emotional presence. title: Micheaux Media - U.S. Bank Pitch Competition Video
transcription: Hi, I'm Chris Avery, I'm the founder of Michaux Media. And this journey for me started back in 2010 while I was deployed to Afghanistan. My mom at the time had sent me a care package, and tucked inside that care package were these stamps featuring this man named Oscar Michaux. Now my mom knew that I had a passion for TV and film, but what she didn't know was that this subtle introduction would drastically change my life. Oscar Michaux lived as a black man during the Great Depression and the segregation of the Jim Crow South. During that time, and despite all of that, he somehow managed to produce, finance, and self-distribute over 40 of his own films entirely independently. He was a maverick who didn't ask for permission. His legacy of self-determination and independence is the absolute inspiration for Michaux Media. Right now, the modern film industry is facing its own unique challenges. Currently, over 85% of the media produced doesn't return its investment, and less than 10% even manages to break even. Hollywood is losing millions because they are bound by outdated production models that fail to engage modern audiences. They are trying to solve a 21st-century problem by gatekeeping 20th-century methods, and it's costing them everything. Michaux Media exists to capture a shift. We want to bet on modern mavericks just like Oscar Michaux. We are building an accelerator platform to de-risk, scale, and monetize creative media before committing massive investment, and shift the power dynamics back to the independent creator. Our platform operates on a four-phase model. First, we host a development sprint designed to test the validity of a project. Second, based on the results of the validation process, we use an internal VC-style model to invest in those ideas that are great and excellent and will go above the mark. And third, we use the most advanced yet financially accessible tools to create proof of concepts. And fourth, we distribute our final result to our pre-vetted and highly curated direct audience. And now is the time for this shift. We are witnessing massive disruption in the entertainment industry. Independent creators are breaking box office records, and we've already seen this in artists like Markiplier and his Iron Lung movie.

He concludes with a strong call to action, referencing current industry disruptions and the success of independent creators.

title: VCs See 100s of Decks a Week — Here's How to Not Get Rejected in 5 Seconds
transcription: The greatest lie ever told in Silicon Valley is build it and they will come. We love to imagine if you code a brilliant product, users will magically appear, and venture capitalists will throw term sheets at your feet. Investors see countless high-performance products fail because no one ever finds out they exist. Without a distribution plan, a startup is effectively an expensive hobby. Most founders assume investors reject them because their idea is bad. In reality, investors reject them because their pitch deck is completely confusing. Industry veteran Guy Kawasaki points out a classic mistake: cramming slides with 10-point font. If you are reading tiny text aloud to an investor, they read ahead, tune out, and the pitch is dead on arrival. You have to understand the psychology of the person across the table. Venture capitalists see hundreds of pitches a week. They are actively looking for a reason to say no so they can move on to the next one and save time. A pitch deck's utility is limited to surviving that initial wave of skepticism and securing a 30-minute meeting. To survive, you have to clear two psychological hurdles. Hurdle 1: Do I care? To get a yes, your problem statement has to be stupidly simple. If you use MBA jargon to describe a synergistic paradigm, you lose. You need to state exactly how many hours or dollars your user is currently wasting because your product doesn't exist yet. The solution slide should offer immediate relief to that exact pain point. Investors don't want a complex technical schematic of your software architecture here. They want to see the pain disappear. This diagram shows three concentric circles of market size: total addressable market, serviceable available, and serviceable obtainable. This clears Hurdle 2: Is this a real business? Calculate market size here without sounding delusional about capturing all of it day one. That requires detailing your go-to-market strategy. Founders often spend weeks polishing product screenshots and maybe 10 minutes thinking about customer acquisition. A brilliant business model is entirely uninvestable if you can't articulate exactly how your first 100 or 1,000 customers are going to find you. Next is Hurdle 3: Is there proof?

Instead, she highlights that many high-performing products fail due to a lack of distribution plans, and pitch decks are often too confusing, leading to investor rejection. 

Referring to industry veteran Guy Kawasaki, she warns against using tiny fonts that cause investors to disengage. She explains the psychology of VCs, who look for quick reasons to say 'no,' and defines the pitch deck's ultimate goal as securing a 30-minute meeting. 

To achieve this, she breaks down three critical hurdles. First, 'Do I care?' requires a simple, pain-point-driven problem and an immediate, clear solution. Second, 'Is this a real business?' involves demonstrating market size (using TAM, SAM, and SOM) and a robust customer acquisition strategy. She ends by introducing the third hurdle, 'Is there proof?' title: GEW and The Experience Gap
transcription: The traditional model of higher education is a passive one. You spend years in wood-paneled rooms like this, absorbing information and waiting to be evaluated by a single focal point of authority. But the moment you graduate, that model breaks. You enter a job market that demands prior experience, yet you can't get that experience because no one will hire you without it. It's the universal paradox of the modern graduate. Most students respond by polishing a resume and submitting it to an online portal, hoping to be chosen from a stack of thousands. This path relies entirely on relinquishing control and waiting for someone else to grant you permission to start your career. In an economy that moves as fast as ours, relying on that passive strategy of waiting to be chosen is a losing bet. The traditional line is simply moving too slowly. If you look at how the most significant career opportunities are actually created, they are rarely assigned by a teacher or a hiring manager. They are discovered by people who notice a problem and step in to fix it before they are asked. This suggests a different logical step after graduation. Instead of spending months finding a job, what if you spent a week building a solution to a problem that already exists? There is a sharp contrast in mindset here. A traditional applicant is looking for an empty slot to fill. A creator is looking for a functional gap in the market, and designing a way to close it. Our current economy is full of powerful tools, but short on people who know how to apply them to specific, messy problems. That gap in the market is exactly where students can transition from being consumers of a curriculum to creators of real-world value. Historically, launching a new venture was a high-stakes game. It required massive capital, a team of specialized engineers, and the backing of a large institution. But as this chart shows, the cost of developing a new product has exponentially collapsed, dropping towards zero. Modern artificial intelligence, cloud services, and no-code tools erased those old gates, making infrastructure accessible to anyone with an internet connection. This toolkit has expanded the definition of an entrepreneur. It is no longer a label reserved for business school students. It is now a functional set of skills. For tradespeople scaling a service, artists automating their sales, or educators reaching new students. For example, a student might notice that a local nonprofit struggles with a repetitive administrative bottleneck. Using AI tools, that student can now build a lightweight, functional prototype to solve that specific problem in a single afternoon. Technology has democratized the power to build. This means the primary barrier to entry is no longer capital or a degree. It is the individual decision to hit start. Even with the tools available, most students stay on the sidelines because they feel they lack professional experience. They are waiting for a level of authority that no textbook can give them.

She contrasts this with a proactive approach: identifying existing gaps or problems in the market and using modern tools like artificial intelligence, cloud services, and no-code platforms to quickly build functional solutions. transcription: कहना है की आवाज हो। देखिए, मैं थोड़ी सी एक मिनट की मेरी स्टोरी है। ये तब से मैंने 11th क्लास में जब जर्नी स्टार्ट की 10th क्लास के बाद तो क्या हुआ कि मैं मिडिल क्लास फॅमिली का अक्सर यही होता है कि अब मैं क्योंकि जब हम बड़े होते हैं ना, तो हमें लगता है की अब हमारी फॅमिली हमारे ऊपर डिपेंड करेगी लेकिन होता अक्सर यही है की जो हमारे पेरेंट्स होते हैं जो हमे पढ़ाना चाहते हैं, वो अपने बच्चों के ऊपर डिपेंड हो जाते हैं। ऐसा ही हुआ कुछ मेरे साथ कि हमारे जो पेरेंट्स थे पिताजी, हमारी माताजी, दादाजी, वो हमारे ऊपर ही डिपेंड हो गए की भाई अब बच्चे को हमने 10th क्लास करा दी है, पढ़ा दिया है 10th क्लास तक, 11th क्लास में पढ़ रहा है। इस बीच स्कूल में था बच्चा तो अब ये जो करेगा, जो ये कहेगा वो सब सही होगा। इसी तरह से क्या हुआ की अब "तुम्ही जाओ और तुम ही जॉब करो।" ठीक है जी। कोई बात नहीं, हम जॉब कर लेंगे। लेकिन हुआ ये वहां था कि ₹10,000 सैलरी थी, ₹5,000 देकर निकाल दिया। अब ₹8,000 की ये जॉब मिली। ये चलता रहा 11th क्लास में। तो हुआ ये हमने, मैंने खुद से जाकर ताकि एक कोचिंग सेंटर बनाया, कंप्यूटर कोचिंग सेंटर, ग्रेटर नोएडा में। और ये बनाया एक साल के बाद। एक साल से पहले कम से कम 200 से 250 कंपनियों में, डिपार्टमेंट में गया जहां पर इंटरव्यू दिए। जॉब कैसे मिलती है? हम धक्के खाए। एक दिन जॉब मिली। कहीं तो ऐसा लगता था की हमें वो काम पसंद नहीं आ रहा, कभी ऐसा लगता था की डिपार्टमेंट को हम पसंद नहीं आ रहे। तो एक दिन जॉब करी, दो दिन करी, तीन दिन में करके छोड़ दिया। अब घर वालों के साथ गए। और घर वालों का यही होता है हमेशा। भाई, एक तो ये हो गया कि तुमको कोई जॉब नहीं मिल रही है। खाली तुम ही पूरे काम कर रहे हो। तो यही हुआ हमारे साथ बहुत ज्यादा। जब एक साल ये सब कुछ झेलने के बाद, इतना सब होने के बाद ये था की जो कुछ करना होगा सब वो खुद ही करना होगा। मेरी उम्र उस वक्त 17 इयर्स की थी, 17 साल का था मैं और जब एक साल मेहनत किया। तब दिमाग में आया की सुसाइड अटेम्प्ट कर लेते हैं। नहीं हो रहा कुछ भी जीवन में। तो एक अचानक कोई मुझे याद आया की मैंने क्या हुआ जैसे मैं सिक्स्थ, सेवंथ, सेकंड स्टैंडर्ड में था, थर्ड स्टैंडर्ड में था, तब से मैं राधा राधा नाम से बहुत ज्यादा प्यार करता था। तो मैंने अपनी नोटबुक में, किताबों में राधा राधा लिखना स्टार्ट किया। उससे इतना मोटीवेट हुआ और एक साल धक्के खाने के बाद एक कंप्यूटर कोचिंग सेंटर बनाया जहां पर बच्चों को बहुत ही कम फीस में मैंने एडमिशन देना स्टार्ट किया और उन एक साल के भीतर भीतर मैंने खुद कोचिंग दी, यूट्यूब से पढ़ा, बहुत सारे बच्चे सीखें। ये सब सीखने के बाद जब मैं कोचिंग चलाता हूँ तो वही सब रखता हूँ बच्चों के सामने जो एक्चुअल में नहीं है। आज के दिन में गवर्नमेंट का बहुत ज्यादा चलता है। गवर्नमेंट का लोगो बहुत ज्यादा चलता है गवर्नमेंट का। बच्चे चार-चार साल मेहनत करते हैं, कुछ नहीं होता है और फिर घर बैठ जाते हैं। फिर पेरेंट्स कहते हैं

title: Why Shark Tank Rejections Often Create Billion-Dollar Businesses
transcription: Television framing suggests that a golden key, and investor's approval, is the only way a startup can scale. Yet a growing list of multi-million dollar companies share a counterintuitive origin story. Their trajectory only accelerated after their golden opportunity publicly shattered. Over the last decade, business reality television has engineered a very specific cultural myth: the idea that a panel of billionaires possesses a flawless intuition for predicting market winners. The audience is sold a clean, dramatic narrative. A broadcasted handshake equates to instant wealth and market dominance, while a harsh rejection signifies the immediate death of a company. Behind the cameras, the reality of these negotiations is heavily obscured. Real pitches often last anywhere from 45 minutes to two and a half hours, but editors aggressively splice these marathons down into 8-minute segments designed purely for pacing and conflict. The resulting broadcast is a highly engineered media product. It is optimized for entertainment, capturing dramatic confrontations rather than providing a definitive verdict on a company's fundamental market value. The manipulation of the narrative extends beyond the editing bay. A significant percentage of filmed pitches are completely scrapped by producers, meaning many founders endure the entire gauntlet only to never make it to the airwaves. The psychological toll of the process is severe enough that immediately following a rejection, founders are ushered into a room with a show-appointed psychiatrist to evaluate their mental state before they leave the studio. Even for those who survive the pitch and secure a deal, the instantaneous on-screen handshake is largely theatrical. It is immediately followed by months of grueling off-camera due diligence. During that period of intense scrutiny, the most heavily guarded secret of the production comes to light. Roughly two-thirds of the agreements made on television completely collapse in the real world. Consider the case of HyConn. The founder secured a massive 1.25 million dollar agreement on-air, only to see the entire deal evaporate once the camera stopped rolling and the investor decided to aggressively alter the terms of the agreement. Founders are legally prevented from discussing these collapsed deals or leveraging their television appearance to attract other backers because they are bound by strict non-disclosure agreements enforced by the production company. A televised handshake is a flimsy illusion of success. A startup's true test does not happen in the studio. It begins the exact moment the production crew leaves the room. title: Uber's Original Pitch Deck: The Slides That Raised Millions
transcription: When you walk into a venture capital pitch, you are stepping into a room defined by heavy skepticism. Every word you say and every slide you show is either building a bridge of trust with the people across the table, or giving them another excuse to say no. The reality of fundraising is that you don't actually win these meetings, you survive them. You keep the conversation alive just long enough to earn a second meeting, by systematically identifying and removing every single reason an investor might hesitate. In 2008, Garrett Camp and Travis Kalanick raised a $200,000 seed round using this presentation. That check grew into an operation valued at $140 billion, even though the deck looks like a rough draft. It runs 25 slides long, ignoring modern advice on brevity. It lacks complex financial models, and barely mentions a business plan. On paper, it should have been discarded during the brutal 3-minute skim test that most VCs use to filter their deal flow. The UberCab deck suggests that at the seed stage, the specific sequencing of trust and psychology can be more influential than the quality of the graphic design. Most founders fall into the trap of the McKinsey-style presentation. They lead with dry market sizing, abstract industry jargon, and theoretical frameworks. It is a logical approach that often feels disconnected from the actual problem being solved. Uber used a structure we call the flipped pyramid. Instead of starting with the math, they hooked the audience with raw, relatable frustration first, saving the spreadsheets for later. They avoided transit industry jargon entirely. Instead, they forced investors to recall the shared misery of trying to hail a cab in a major city. They evoked specific visceral pain points: the 45-minute wait times with zero status updates, and that helpless feeling of standing on a street corner in a downpour hoping an empty car might eventually pass by. Only after they established that emotional wound did they introduce the solution. This direct mapping, linking a technological feature like automated dispatch to a specific human frustration, makes the product feel inevitable. Notice the lack of dense text on these slides. By using simple icons as visual anchors, the deck prevents the investor from reading ahead. It forces the founder to remain the primary storyteller in the room.

Her delivery is professional, informative, and engaging, with clear articulation and a measured pace. The analysis highlights how Uber's pitch deck used a "flipped pyramid" structure to connect with investors through relatable frustrations before introducing their solution, emphasizing simplicity and emotional engagement over complex financial models.

title: 🔥 Smart Hostel Maintenance System | Startup Pitch | BMC Presentation | 5-Minute Team Video
transcription: Good morning, everyone. Before we begin, I want to ask you one simple question. How many of you have stayed in a hostel or PG? And how many times you have faced problems like a fused bulb, broken fans, water leakage, or bathroom issue? Now think about what happened next to inform to the warden or the watchman, or maybe a senior. But most of the time, nothing happens immediately. There is no system, there is no tracking, there is no responsibility. What looks like a small issue is actually a daily frustration for millions of students. And this is exactly where startups are born. According to Y Combinator, the best startups don't start with big technology, they start with real problems focused by real people. So, today we are not here to present just an idea, we are here to present a solution to a problem that students face every single day. Our idea is called Smart Hostel Maintenance System. Let me now explain how this simple idea can create a big impact. Our solution is called Smart Hostel Maintenance System. It is simple and helpful. Every room or floor in the hostel has a QR code. When the when a student scans the QR code, they choose the problems and upload the photos. The room's room's number comes automatically, comes. Then the complaint is sent instantly. After that, the system sends the problems to technician. Students can scan the status any anytime. When the work is finished, students give the feedback. No calls, no no confusions, no waitings. This system makes the hostel maintenance fast and easy and clean. Now I will explain our startup again with the Business Model Canvas. Hostel, hostel, PG owners and college management is key. These management handles of students and daily daily maintenance complaints and canteen, and infrastructure issues. Managing all this manually is time-consuming and inefficient. So, they are our main target. Next is our value propositions. We offer a centralized digital complaint system that helps hostel association faster tracking and complaint resolution. This reduces the workload of wardens and management, and improves the student satisfaction. In simple, it converts this slow manual process into a smart automated system. Now coming to key resources. We uses student mobile app, web dashboard, QR code for rooms, and a database.

transcription: Raise your hand if you've ever skipped buying a textbook because it was too expensive. Well, I have. So, you guys just proved our pitch for us. So, we're just four students, and like every student in this room, we felt the weight of a textbook cost on a budget that was already stretched thin. And we're team IDE $1 Extra, and we have Fakaio, my name is Precious, Cleopatra, and Tolu. And we're not researchers, we're just students who live this problem every single semester, and that is exactly why we're the right people to solve it. Did you know that 65% of students have skipped buying the required textbook because they simply could not afford it? And they knowingly accepted the risk of a lower grade to avoid paying. Also, 33% of students have earned a poor grade because they couldn't afford their course material, materials. And 17% have dropped a course entirely because of textbook costs. At University of Alberta alone, $17 million is spent over textbooks every single semester, and $10 million is just left on the table, not being used, just being wasted as textbooks on their shelves that they're never going to use again. With seeing this, we realized the market is fragmented, and the experience is broken, and the students are paying the price academically and financially. And we're here to fix that. So, let's imagine a student, Betty, and another student, Tolu. So Betty, she is a student in, at the U of A in Edmonton, but she lives in, but she, her family is from Regina. And she would love to go visit her grandma over in Regina for her birthday, who she's missed a lot, or she even wanted to get more groceries because her allowance right now in the middle of the month, and she needs more money to get those groceries. And how do we fix this problem? Over to you, Cleo.

title: Forget Startups — These 6 Boring Businesses Have a 90% Success Rate and Create Millionaires
transcription: What if I told you that the path to your first million has nothing to do with a brilliant idea, a viral moment, or a tech startup burning through investor cash? What if the real road to financial freedom is so unglamorous that most people drive right past it without ever noticing? Today, we are talking about six businesses, so boring, so ordinary, so completely unsexy, that the average person would never consider building one. Stay until the end, because the last piece of this video is the one that actually changes what you do tomorrow morning. Here is the stat that should shake you awake: nearly half of all millionaires built their wealth through business ownership. But here is what nobody tells you: the vast majority of those businesses are not disruptive platforms or bold consumer brands. They are boring, repeatable, local service businesses that generate predictable cash flow month after month, while their owners live quiet, comfortable lives. Meanwhile, most flashy startups are gone within five years. Laundromats, self-storage facilities, and vending routes have historically sat in the 90% success range. That number alone should flip everything you thought you knew about entrepreneurship. Business number one: laundromats. I know what you're thinking. Laundromats? Seriously? But think about what a laundromat actually is. It is a machine that collects money around the clock from people who have no other option. Renters in dense urban areas, families washing oversized bedding, people whose home machines break down. Every single week, people need clean clothes. They show up without being reminded. They pay without negotiating. Dirty clothes are not a trend. They are a permanent condition of being alive. Business number two: vending routes. title: 🏆 WINNER: Best Video Pitch & 4th Runner-Up Overall | PSC X Bicol Region
transcription: The heart of the Philippines, a broken system is hurting everyone. Farmers harvest with sweat and sacrifice, yet sell at prices too low to survive. Ang hirap po kasi kahit malakas ang ani ay mababa pa rin ang presyo na naibibigay sa amin. Yung ni-harvest ko ngayon may presyo pero hindi naman alam kung magkano ang pagbili niya. Presyo ng gulay is uh parang ang may gain doon is yung middleman. Mababa ang bili ng disposer sa farmer. Kasi mababa ang presyo pag hinarvest wala na, pupunta sa ano sa pamasahe wala nang matitira para sa amin. Buyers want local produce but face high cost and unreliable supply, and customers they pay more for less. This isn't just a gap, it's a broken chain that fails us all. Lalong lumalalim pa ang ugat ng problemang kinakaharap ng mga kababayan nating magsasaka lalo na nitong nakaraang buwan. Farmers face unfair pricing, limited market access and constant uncertainty. Buyers pay inflated cost and face inconsistent supply. Consumers struggle with affordability and freshness. This inefficiency hurts our economy, our health and our communities. But what if we could bridge this gap fairly, transparently and sustainably? Agrikita is a digital marketplace connecting farmers, buyers, consumers and organizations. We're not just an app, we're a movement to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals and transform Philippine agriculture. Agrikita empowers four key segments: smallholder farmers, local businesses, consumers, and support organizations. Farmers are verified through secure digital profiles, ensuring trust and authenticity. They can also create product listings with just a few taps, giving them direct access to reliable buyers.

First up, those key figures. Okay, let's get right into it with the headline results for the first quarter. Disney kicked off the year with total revenues of a nice, round $26 billion. Now, when we look at profitability, the adjusted earnings per share, and remember that's the number that kind of strips out the one-off items to give us a clean view, that came in at $1.63. So, the question is, why? But on the other hand, both the entertainment and sports segments got hit with some pretty significant pressure on their operating income. After that, we'll look ahead to their future guidance and finish up with their key strategic moves. Pretty straightforward. Okay, let's get right to it. The executive summary, what are the headline numbers telling us? Okay, first up, the number that really jumps out at you, sales growth of just 6.4%. Now, to put that in perspective, this is a massive, massive slowdown from the blistering 25% growth they posted just last year. And you know that slowdown in sales, it hit the bottom line and it hit it hard. Operating profit growth was basically flat. Actually, it dipped just a tiny bit, down half a percent. Again, when you compare that to the huge 25% growth they saw in 2024- Wow, what a difference a year makes. -but, here's where it gets interesting. Despite all that pressure on the top line and on operating profit, their diluted earnings per share actually went up a little bit by 2%. So, what does that tell us? Well, it suggests they were really pulling some levers behind the scenes, maybe some sharp cost controls or share buybacks, to prop up those per-share earnings even while growth was stalling out. Okay, this five-year view really tells the whole story, doesn't it? Just look at that sales growth line. You see it just falling off a cliff from 25% in 2024 all the way down to 6.4% in 2025. And, it's the exact same story for operating profit, from over 25% growth to a slight dip. I mean, this chart is basically the picture of an extraordinary growth cycle coming to a very abrupt end.

title: How to Read an Earnings Call Transcript With AI — 3 Prompts to Find What Management Avoided
transcription: The stock dropped 6% after earnings. The revenue number actually beat, the EPS beat, and yet, 6% down. If you only read the headline numbers, you missed what the market actually reacted to. The real signal was buried inside the earnings call transcript, in the language management used, the questions they avoided, and the tone that shifted quarter over quarter. Today, I'm going to show you how to use AI to read an earnings call transcript the way a professional analyst does: three prompts, 30 minutes, a level of insight that used to take a whole research team. Every public company holds an earnings call after it reports results. Management presents the numbers, but more importantly, they explain what's driving them. Then, analysts from investment banks ask questions. The transcript captures all of it, word for word. And here's what most retail investors don't realize: the transcript almost always contains more useful information than the press release. Executives choose their words carefully. When growth is slowing, they don't say "growth is slowing." They say things like, "We're prioritizing quality over volume," or "The macro environment remains dynamic." AI is exceptionally good at detecting this kind of language. Before we get to the prompts, you need the transcript. Here's how to get one for free. First option: the company's own investor relations page. Go to the company website, find investor relations, and look for earnings or events. Most companies post transcripts within 24 to 48 hours. Second option: The Motley Fool publishes free transcripts at fool.com/earnings-call-transcripts. Search the company name and the quarter. Third option: Seeking Alpha has a free transcript section under the earnings tab on any stock page.

title: PAYPAL ( $PYPL ) Q4 2025 Earnings Breakdown | Financial Analysis
transcription: All right, let's jump right in and break down PayPal's latest earnings report. We're going to look at the fourth quarter and the full year numbers for 2025. So, here's how we're going to tackle this. First, a quick snapshot of the results. Then, we'll dive into how each part of the business is doing, check out their profitability, see what management is forecasting, and finally look at where they're planning to put their money. Okay, first things first. Let's get that high-level view of the results for the quarter and the entire year. So, looking at the top line, PayPal brought in about $8.7 billion in Q4. And, for the full year, we're talking over $33 billion. In both cases, that's a 4% bump from the year before. Steady, but not exactly explosive growth, you know? But here is where it gets really interesting. Look at that earnings per share number for the full year, it jumped 14%. That is way faster than the revenue growth. So, what does that tell us? It means they're getting much, much better at managing their costs and squeezing more profit out of every dollar that comes in. That's a huge signal of efficiency. Okay, so we've seen the big picture. Now let's peel back the layers a bit and see what's really going on under the hood with their different business segments. Real quick before we dive in, let's define a key term you're going to hear a lot: TPV, or total payment volume. It's pretty simple. It's just the total dollar value of all the payments they process. This chart is pretty revealing, right? It shows exactly where all that payment volume is coming from. And check it out. The PSP business, that's their unbranded, back-end processing for merchants, is now the biggest piece of the pie. This isn't just your classic PayPal button anymore. They've really diversified their business. And this is really the core of the story right here. You've got two very different tales playing out. The PSP business is growing at a solid 8%, and Venmo is just on an absolute tear, up 13%. But, then you look at their classic branded experiences, that blue PayPal button we all know, it's only up 4%. That's a definite slowdown and it's for sure something to watch closely. Yeah, speaking of Venmo, it's really turning into a powerhouse for the company. It pulled in $1.7 billion in revenue all by itself for the year, which is a 20% jump. It's crystal clear that Venmo is a huge part of their growth story right now. Okay, so we know where the growth is coming from and, well, where it's slowing down. But the big question is, how does all of this actually translate to the bottom line? Let's dig into profitability.

title: The Moment Her Ex Knew Something Was Very Wrong (Lindsay Clancy Trial)
transcription: Lindsay Clancy's husband Patrick took the stand at her murder trial and told a story so heartbreaking, so gut-wrenching, that it's almost past understanding. He is the ex of Lindsay Clancy, who is on trial right now in a Massachusetts courtroom accused of murdering their three children, ages 5, 3, and 8 months. Now, Lindsay says she should be found not guilty by reason of her mental illness, she says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Patrick is the most important witness by far for both sides, unless maybe Lindsay testifies. But after the murders, Patrick and Lindsay divorced. He's remarried. But he has continued to support Lindsay, saying she wasn't evil, she was sick. He has sued the numerous mental health providers she contacted trying to get help before everything went to hell in a handbasket. The prosecution put him on the stand as their very first witness, and he went through the very ordinary, very mundane day that they were having until this happened. He was working from home, and then Lindsay asked him to go to the drugstore and to pick up dinner. 55 minutes, that's it, that's how long he was gone from home. He returned home to discover that this was actually the worst day of his entire life. In fact, it was one of the most horrible days imaginable. When you came into the house and you were taking off your boots and putting things down, um, was there anything you noticed? Yeah, the house was really quiet. Is that unusual? Yeah. And when you, you realized it was really quiet, what did you do? Um, I called out. And who did you call out to? Everyone. Did anyone answer? No. After you called out and no one answered, what did you do next? Uh, I think I, I don't know the order, but I called down in the basement and no one answered. And then, um, I called Lindsay to see if she was home, because I looked out and I, I couldn't see her car, but it's because it was dark and her car's black. title: Tate brothers arrested: Attorney claims Tristian, Andrew Tate 'innocent', 'never done nothing wrong'
transcription: Good afternoon, everyone. So, today went as expected. There was never going to be any fireworks today. Today wasn't about controversy. Today was about just enforcing Mr. Tate's, Andrew and Tristan Tate's, rights and objecting to the extradition process. We are, of course, objecting to extradition because Andrew and Tristan are innocent. They've never done nothing wrong. They shouldn't be extradited for crimes they did not commit. They're entitled to have their day of court. We've been litigating the case for three years in Palm Beach County in Florida. So, we're fighting extradition. We've assembled a team here. These are from the Roy Black's prestigious firm. The honorable, and since passed on, Roy Black, he is a legend, and they're here. They have joined our team. We have a competent team. The allegations, their first reaction to the allegations is the first reaction that any innocent man or woman would have. It's, uh, it's garbage. It's a stitch-up job. They're after us to punish us with the process. The process is the punishment. When you drag somebody's name through the media, when you slander them, when you defame them, when you accuse them of heinous and terrible allegations, the process becomes the punishment until you can clear your name. title: Why the Iran War May Hurt Trump
transcription: When we look back at this war, people will see it as a game-changing event for the region. There hasn't really been a precedent ever in history where the response out of Iran has involved as many countries as we're seeing today. We'll never be threatened by a nuclear-armed Iran. There are multiple political risks for Trump. It's arguably the most definitive decision and move that he has made since coming into office for the second time. With the big US military buildup that had occurred, there was an assumption that there would be some form of military action. One of the tenets of that America First policy was no new wars, and now he started a war. Everyone in this region, including the Gulf states, had underestimated the scale and the breadth of the Iranian response. The President campaigned as a candidate in 2024 as someone who upheld the America First policy, and it's important to note that he started this war in the middle of what is an election year. I think one of the biggest fears is the unintended consequences of pursuing a war without a clear objective. The biggest political thorn in his side, at least as far as his base has been concerned, is the Jeffrey Epstein files. But Iran has the potential to be high up on that list, potentially equal with that. The President was supposed to be, according to his advisors, spending the next several months doing a multi-state domestic tour talking about his economic record. The opportunity, I think, presented itself. This was our last best chance to strike. The President decided that this was the window to do it, and made very clear that he wanted to see what he called regime change. We're finding ourselves in, if not the worst case, very close to one of the worst-case scenarios that these Gulf states had been actively trying to avoid. It came at a time when the economy in Iran was weak

title: How Argentina Became The Most Hated World Cup Team
transcription: Argentina's World Cup, let's get into it. Argentina entered the 2026 World Cup as the defending World Cup champions, the reigning Copa América champions, and the number-one ranked team in the world. On paper, they looked unstoppable, and with this expected to be Messi's last World Cup run, millions of football fans from around the world were hoping for one last magical run. But as the tournament went on and Argentina kept winning, the controversy only continued to grow. The first major controversy of Argentina's tournament involved their supporters after their match in the round of 32. Cabo Verde was by far the surprise story of the tournament. They shocked the football world by holding Spain to a scoreless draw and earning their very first World Cup point. Their 40-year-old goalkeeper had about 50,000 Instagram followers before the Spain match, and after his incredible performance, he gained millions of followers overnight, currently sitting at nearly 30 million. So on July 3rd, when it came time for them to play Argentina in the round of 32, IShowSpeed, who is a Ronaldo fan, naturally was cheering for Cabo Verde and made that pretty clear. "Let's go! Cabo!" During the match, Speed was streaming from the stands, and all was fine until one Argentina supporter appeared to shout a racist slur and repeatedly told him to go home. Then during Argentina's next match against Egypt, one Argentina supporter could be seen attempting to mock IShowSpeed by doing this. The supporter later defended himself, insisting he wasn't being racist and he was simply imitating Speed. But to many people, including myself, it looked like he was mocking a chimpanzee. He even added that if it was racist, then tough luck, because Speed has spent the tournament busting balls against Argentina. The fan then went on to say Egypt's only culture is building pyramids and suppressing women, which truly just dug his grave even deeper. I made a TikTok about this topic, and just like this fan, many people in the comment section were trying to justify this racist behavior, claiming that IShowSpeed started it by insulting Messi and the rest of the Argentina team. I grew up playing sports. Hockey and football, or soccer as we call it in Canada, were my main two. Banter is simply part of sports. Making fun of someone's performance on the ice or on the pitch is just a part of the game. But once you cross into attacking someone's race, appearance, or family, that's where a line is drawn, and the World Cup has no room for this behavior. Don't get me wrong, Argentina supporters are not the only ones who are at fault for this. There's a senator from Paraguay who went viral for her disgusting and flat-out racist comments towards Mbappé. But because Argentina are the defending champions, and the team that everyone is watching, the reality is that everything, every controversy, even involving their supporters, is amplified. And this was only the first of several incidents that completely changed how football fans viewed Argentina throughout the World Cup. The controversy didn't stay in the stands for long. As Argentina kept advancing through the tournament, a completely different narrative started circulating on social media. Fans began asking one question: was FIFA trying to give Messi a happy ending? "Happy ending."

title: UEFA Finally Issues BOYCOTT Threat to FIFA!
transcription: Football could be on the brink of its biggest civil war in decades. UEFA has just issued one of the strongest statements we've ever seen against FIFA. And it's not just criticism, it's a warning. A warning that Europe's 55 Football Associations are prepared to boycott FIFA competitions if FIFA pushes ahead with its controversial new plan. If that sounds unbelievable, that's because it is. For years, FIFA and UEFA have disagreed over football calendars, tournament expansion and governance. But this time, the stakes are much higher. So what exactly has happened? It all started when FIFA unveiled a proposal to create a new commercial company called FIFA Forward Enterprise. The idea is for this company to manage the commercial side of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. FIFA would still remain the majority owner, but it also wants to sell a minority stake to private investors. The goal? Raise billions of dollars to invest in football development around the world. On paper, FIFA says it's simply creating a smarter financial model, one that can generate more money for member associations and help grow the game globally. But UEFA sees it very differently. In an extraordinary statement released on behalf of all, all 55 European football associations, UEFA unanimously rejected the proposal. Its message couldn't have been clearer. The World Cup is not for sale. According to UEFA, football's greatest competition should never become an investment product for private shareholders. The organization says the World Cup belongs to players, national teams and supporters across generations, not investors looking for financial returns. And UEFA wasn't just angry about the proposal itself. It also criticized the way FIFA handled the entire process. According to the statement, such an important decision was developed behind closed doors and brought close to approval without meaningful consultation with the people responsible for governing the sport. That criticism goes beyond business. It's about trust. UEFA believes decisions that shape football's future should involve open discussions with confederations, leagues, clubs and national associations. Instead, it believes FIFA acted alone.

title: Despite losses, Supreme Court grants Trump significant power today
transcription: A crushing blow for Trump at the Supreme Court. In a major loss for the president, the Supreme Court today shutting down his efforts to meddle in the upcoming election. Two of the conservative justices joining the liberal justices to allow states to continue counting mail-in ballots that are postmarked by election day. Trump did not take it well. The mail-in ballot ruling, which was a little bit surprising, gives people more time to vote illegally, let's say. I think it was very detrimental to honest elections. Now, of course, there's no evidence of widespread fraud when it comes to mail-in ballots, and frankly, sometimes it's frustrating even have to say it that way. They've looked and looked and looked. title: Supreme Court weakens Voting Rights Act by voiding Louisiana's congressional map
transcription: Hello, everyone. I'm Major Garrett in New York. Welcome to The Takeout. When it comes to voting representation in modern post-Jim Crow America, there are many ways to measure. Access at the voting booth is one. Numerical representation in Congress is another. The landmark 1965 Voting Rights Act addressed both head-on. Section 2 of that Act, which the Supreme Court eroded today, intentionally attempted to increase minority representation nationwide in Congress by allowing for the drawing of so-called majority-minority districts, even if the drawing of those district lines were unusual in geographic ways so as to knit together minority voting blocks. Now, in 1980, the Supreme Court restrained the interpretation of that Act by saying Section 2 only prohibited district lines that prevented minority representation on purpose. Congress stepped in in 1982 to say no, no, Section 2 barred district lines that had discriminatory effect. It didn't need to be on purpose. If the effect was discriminatory, it could be challenged in court. And that interpretation held for decades. Until today, when a 6-3 majority on the High Court ruled that the benefit of drawing district lines with the intent of increasing minority representation had to be weighed against other considerations, specifically Equal Protection Clause protections in the Constitution against discrimination suffered, in this particular litigation, by white voters, who sued to block creation of a second congressional district in Louisiana, which, as you can see here, stretches from Shreveport in the northwestern part of the state to Baton Rouge in the southeastern part of the state. With more on this decision, the dissent to it, and the possible political implications, we turn to our Chief Legal Correspondent, Jan Crawford. Jan, walk us through what happened. Well, I mean, Major, I think you've really kind of nailed all of it. I mean, it's going to make it much harder for people to justify these so-called majority-minority districts that, as you said, were designed to increase representation in Congress. The way people had done it was they would argue that we needed this district, you know, under Section 2, that key provision, the crown jewel of the Voting Rights Act. And so, therefore, you could consider race when you were drawing it, and do those kind of long lines like you just showed.

title: Supreme Court rules 2024 Louisiana redistricting map is unconstitutional
transcription: In a 6-3 decision along ideological lines, the High Court has just ruled that Louisiana's 2024 map, which created the state's second majority-black congressional district, is unconstitutional. The court writing that, quote, "the Constitution almost never permits a state to discriminate on the basis of race," with Justice Alito delivering the opinion for the court. The decision marks a major win for Republicans, as Louisiana will now have to redraw its districting map and could have major implications for upcoming elections. For that, I want to bring in senior Justice reporter Ryan Reilly, who has been following this for us. Um, Ryan, talk about those implications, right, of this decision out of Louisiana. We have a huge election now, just what, seven months away come November. Yeah, it's going to be a real scramble. And remember, Yasmine, before all of this, you know, they originally drew this map that despite Louisiana's population being a third, uh, black, that only one of the six districts that they drew originally, uh, was majority black. And so when they came, when they came back in order to sort of comply with the Voting Rights Act, uh, they had drawn maps that created two majority-black districts. But overall, if you look at the course of, uh, the Supreme Court's, uh, jurisprudence on the, uh, Voting Rights Act over the course of the last decade plus, I mean, they've been chipping away at the Voting Rights Act ever so slowly. And I think this is another big chunk, uh, that essentially they're taking out, uh, of the Voting Rights Act, which was sort of meant to originally, you know, make voting more equal, give, uh, individuals who had been suppressed for generations, uh, and for, for years, uh, more power in their own government. And so, uh, this is, you know, from a, purely political standpoint, should benefit, uh, Republicans, as you sort of mentioned, um, and I think that, you know, voting rights advocates see this as another, uh, another sort of, uh, clip out of, uh, taking, uh, being taken out of the Voting Rights Act, which has already been, you know, severely weakened by the Supreme Court, uh, over, uh, since, you know, 2013, really. We're hearing from the Attorney General, too, Louisiana, Ryan, in which the, the Attorney General says, um, "the Supreme Court has ended Louisiana's long-running nightmare of federal courts coercing the state to draw a racially discriminatory map that was always unconstitutional." title: "No Country Matches India's Energy": Sam Altman's Viral Speech at AI Summit 2026 | News18
transcription:
**Shereen Bhan**: I'm Shereen Bhan and we've got probably one of the biggest headliners here at the India AI Impact Summit, OpenAI's Sam Altman. Sam, great to have you join us on CNBC-TV18. It's wonderful to see you here back in India. You were sharing the stage with the Prime Minister just a few moments ago talking about how important India is, but how significant is India for OpenAI specifically? It is your second-largest market today.

**Sam Altman**: It is our second-largest market and the energy here, that people are, what people are building with the technology is just amazing to watch. We have more than 100 million weekly active users of ChatGPT. This is the fastest-growing market for Codex. And it's, it's amazing to see the energy here. Every time I come, it feels like it's gone up another level.

**Shereen Bhan**: You know, Sam, you've also shared the stage with Pratyush Kumar of Sarvam. The last time you were here, there were questions being asked on whether India can do an LLM. Have you had a look at what Sarvam has been able to put out?

**Sam Altman**: India's, yes, but more generally, India is just building incredible AI, the entire AI stack, from, you know, like data centers to models to applications, and I think there's no country in the world quite matches India for total AI energy.

**Shereen Bhan**: Sam, can you give me a sense of what we can expect now from OpenAI for India? How much can you customize OpenAI and ChatGPT for India? What should we expect?

**Sam Altman**: The number one request we get is better support of local languages and dialects, which is something we are hard at work on, and we're open to taking any other requests if you have some.

**Shereen Bhan**: Is that something you are going to double down on?

**Sam Altman**: Yeah, we're hard at work on that already now.

**Shereen Bhan**: Okay. You've just announced a partnership with TCS, and of course, you're going to be one of the first clients as far as TCS's data center is concerned. What do you envisage as far as that relationship and that partnership is concerned, and do you believe you're likely to ink more partnerships here in India, especially on the enterprise side?

**Sam Altman**: Totally. Hard to overstate, as I mentioned earlier, how much energy there is for building AI and building with AI in India, and I think you should expect to see more partnerships and much more activity here as we try to work with the Indian people to bring AI to the rest of the world in all of these amazing ways.

title: Report: Trump orders new strikes on Iran, aimed at getting Tehran to surrender
transcription: But first, breaking tonight, President Trump reportedly has ordered a fresh attack on Iran, aimed at getting Tehran to surrender. Wall Street Journal reporting tonight that attack could begin as soon as this weekend and would last a few days. The White House press secretary not denying that report. It comes following a televised cabinet meeting from Camp David today, where the president talked about the Iran conflict and touted his administration's openness. Senior Foreign Policy Correspondent Jillian Turner starts us off live tonight from the North Lawn of the White House. Good evening, Jillian. Good evening to you, Brett. This just into the newsroom now, Karoline Leavitt responding to a Fox News question about whether the president does plan to renew strikes targeting Iran. She says, quote, in part, "Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table in what President Trump deems a meaningful way." Now, this morning, the president convened the first-ever televised cabinet meeting from Camp David. The entire cabinet was there minus Howard Lutnick. The president is now at Bedminster for the weekend. Brett, we are the party of transparency, and we believe in transparency. Foreign policy topped the agenda, the first line item being the war in Iran. So we're in there for five months, and if you look at Vietnam, they were in there for 20 years. The president today went on defense against criticism that the conflict has no end in sight. Backing his boss, the War Secretary says launching operations at the Khuri back in February, quote, "took guts." The world saw what the American military was capable to do, but that doesn't happen unless the commander-in-chief says, "You're authorized to do it." Despite repeated claims that Iran's military arsenal has been decimated, the commander-in-chief acknowledged today that the regime does have some capability left. Their missiles have been largely, they have some left, they have some, but they have far fewer than they had four or five months ago. Uh, they, the manufacturing capacity is almost gone, the drone capacity is almost gone, they have very few, but they have some. They have, if they have one, that's too many as far as I'm concerned. But missiles aren't the only threat the US is worried about. Last night, the State Department Rewards for Justice program posted a new offer, $15 million for information about Iran's military drone program. The Treasury Secretary says the US is having plenty of non-military successes in Iran, too. The largest bank in Iran collapsed. The Central Bank had to print money, that caused inflation, now they got 180% inflation. They aren't able to pay their troops, and on your orders, we are searching for their assets all around the world, and that money will go to the Iranian people. So, in neighboring Iraq, new reporting tonight is that the US withdrawal is nearing completion, this as the autonomous Kurdistan region faces increased military attacks by Iran and its proxy groups there in the region. All US troops must be completely withdrawn from Iraq by the end of September, this per an agreement between President Trump and Iraq's Prime Minister. Brett. A lot happening in the Middle East, Jillian Turner live on the North Lawn. Jillian, thanks. Be sure to like and subscribe for all the Fox News latest on YouTube, and catch full shows streaming now on Fox Nation.

title: Spoken-Word Quiet Kind Of Heavy
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Lingering memories follow him
like shadows along the wall
The echoes of a screaming past
refusing to fall
Chaos
crashing through his chest
lightning strikes in his lungs, thunder roars in his thoughts and
grey skies left standing there alone and
torn
untamed storm
His mind on endless repeat
every ache silent, looping, every wound carved deeper
heavier
every piece of his soul it chose to take
moment by moment, it consumes a little more
torment after torment
and in the quiet
he whispers
am I something I can't restore?
He begins to feel unfamiliar
a stranger in his own skin
where safety is a memory and fear is moving near
filling every corner of his own mind, every breath, every thought, every space
until even peace feels like
a forgotten place
And still, he searches for calm in the night
finding refuge in fractured light
from the demons that dance
just beyond his sight
His healing moves slow
but it moves
through roads that twist
through paths that bruise
a journey that tests the strength of his soul
yet step by step
he regains control
head held high, eyes sharp awake
though exhaustion whispers
he's still there
because something inside him refuses to break
refuses to bend, refuses to fade
He won't
he can't
a silent vow
through the dark he'll devour
to reclaim his light
from his own shadowed hour

As the narrative progresses, the music subtly builds, and her voice gains strength and urgency. Around the midway mark, the spoken-word transitions into a passionate, soulful singing performance. Her vocals become powerful and resonant, effortlessly hitting high notes filled with determination and hope. The instrumentation swells with layered synthesizers and a driving beat, mirroring her emotional ascent. The performance ends with a mix of powerful vocals and a resolute spoken-word declaration about healing and reclaiming one's life, leaving a lasting, inspiring impression.

title: SF Game Developers Conference welcomes attendees from 100+ countries | KTVU
transcription:
Daniel, Game Developers Conference started today in San Francisco. Tens of thousands of attendees from big game companies to small independent developers are gathering this week for workshops, game demos, panel discussions on the future of gaming platforms, AI, and other big issues. KTVU's Jana Katsuyama gives us a look at the buzz inside this year's GDC.

The 2024 GDC, Game Developers Conference, kicked off Monday, bringing participants from more than 100 countries to San Francisco's Moscone Center. This year, organizers say they've expanded the scope.

It's not just game developers you'll see this year, as you've seen in the past, but it's everything that goes into making a game and publishing the game and marketing the game. So, you'll see the entire ecosystem of games, including investors, publishers, developers, audio...

Also new this year, a Luminary series for executives to network with industry leaders, and a new Game Commons area with podcasting and a Game Jam where attendees make brand-new games right at the conference. The last GDC drew more than 30,000 people. This year, there are some 1,100 speakers and companies from Xbox and Meta to Roblox, Discord, and smaller independent developers.

Now when I come here, I can connect with all my West Coast friends, friends at studios, and talk about how the industry has changed and connecting with different players. Things that worked, things that haven't. So, it's really great.

See a lot of our users out here. So, every year we can get a lot of really great feedback about what, where are the tooling in the ecosystem lacking.

My biggest thing that I want to get, more people that I network with, more people in the same industry.

AI, of course, is one big factor in many sessions.

There's a lot of discussion around both generative AI as well as agentic AI, working with agents as part of game development pipeline.

Some say they're glad to see more women in the industry and hope that will grow.

The ratio is about 1:25 or 30 maybe, so, so, I think there is, we need to be doing more.

And many people say it's important this year to be face-to-face and network with others at this very critical time for the gaming industry.

Different funding organizations have started to pull their funding from really big, key studios. And what ends up happening is is those studios have to make really hard cuts. And it kind of runs the gamut. It's everything from small studios to even really large, existing studios.

The conference is giving San Francisco's economy a welcome boost. Again, this conference goes all the way to Friday when the last sessions wrap up. Reporting from the Moscone Center in San Francisco, Jana Katsuyama, KTVU, Fox 2 News.

title: HIGHLIGHTS: Qualifying 1 | 2026 Isle of Man TT Races
transcription: Conditions were once more perfect for the first qualifying of TT 2023, with record temperatures and clear skies across the island. It would be Superbike and Superstock machines that would open the evening, with Dean Harrison leading the field onto Glencrutchery Road. The Honda Racing UK rider would complete two laps on his Fireblade Superbike with the best lap of 133.514 mph, the fastest lap ever seen on an opening day of qualifying. The adopted Manxman looking for his first Superbike win since 2018. Second fastest on the Superbike, a similar Fireblade of Michael Dunlop. The 21-time TT winner returning to Honda machinery on the big bike with a fastest time of 130.398 mph. Also in the 130 club on Tuesday evening, and sporting a similar Honda, John McGuinness. Just two seconds adrift of Dunlop, the Morecambe Missile finished with an average speed of 130.088 mph. While the returning Peter Hickman was seventh fastest, his best lap at 125.592 mph. Hickman fared much better in the Superstocks, finishing second fastest on the day, just six seconds adrift of the fastest time. With the nine-time TT winner crashing in both the previous two events, he will surely be aiming for a clean 2023 Tourist Trophy. Australia's Josh Brookes was the only other rider to break the 130 mph barrier on the Superstock, piloting his FHO Racing BMW to a 130.197 mph time. With Davey Todd fifth, Brookes could be a dark horse for podiums or more. And in third place, Jamie Coward. The Yorkshireman missed the 2022 event with injury, but it's clear he's quickly jelling with the KTS team, a best time of 128.788 mph. What's next? Following the Superbike and Superstock session, the next outing was for the Supersport and Supertwin machines. And in the Supersport class, it was all the familiar faces at the front, bar Dean Harrison. The pit limiter on his Honda got stuck on, so he had to return to the assembly area while the mechanics got to work, missing out on important track time. Of those who completed laps, it was no surprise to see Michael Dunlop at the top of the timesheets. Aiming to continue his Yamaha dominance in class, an average lap speed of 126.917 mph would be good enough for the top spot. Next best was the BPE by Russell Racing Yamaha of James Hillier, the Hampshire...

transcription: Yeah. Look. You ever feel the storm coming before the first drop of rain even hits? It's a specific kind of terror. When you look around your room and you realize it's happening again. You're watching your own mind slide into the dark, and you can't find the brakes. I can feel it in my chest. Listen. I can feel the exact moment the chemistry starts to shift. The heavy gravity pulling me down, beginning to drift away from the people I love, away from the things that I enjoy. My phone rings and the sound of a simple notification just starts to annoy me. I haven't left my bed in two days, the sheets feel like a prison cell. I'm looking at the clutter in my room, it's just a physical reflection of my mind. Motivation is dead, the creative spark is a ghost. The things that used to bring me joy are the exact things I'm avoiding the most. It starts with a heavy sigh, then it moves to a blank stare, then suddenly you're sitting at the edge of the bed, completely unaware of the time passing by. An hour feels like a second or two. And you're desperately trying to remember the last time you felt like yourself. I'm pulling away from my friends, I'm making up excuses to hide. I'm just tired, I'm busy, I'm good. But the truth is, I am lying. I see the shadows stretching out, and I can hear the train coming down the track. Oh, I can feel it in my bones. I'm headed for the dark again. I'm losing all my focus, I don't know where the light has been. I see the walls closing in, I feel the weight on my chest. I'm trying to fight the shadow, but my spirit can't arrest. Is anybody out there watching themselves start to slip? Losing your footing, losing your mind, losing your grip. I'm screaming at the mirror, trying to make the monster stop. title: Does Civic AI Mean? | Ron Ivey (Noēsis Collaborative) | Civic AI Conference 2026
transcription: With the question that we've been wrestling with today about how should AI care for communities and who gets to decide, I think one of the challenges I have is the it's kind of very fundamental uh kind of premise of that question, whether AI can care. From what I understand and from, you know, talking to and working with uh the developers of these systems, there's there's a real debate whether AI actually cares, where whether it actually has the capacity for empathy, uh whether it has the capacity for moral consideration of others, attentiveness to others, and and really understanding others' uh feelings and perceptions. We already heard this morning about how, you know, the systems themselves cannot distinguish between these issues of of parental sacrifice, which I'm a parent, I'm having to sacrifice every day in terms of my relationships, and child sacrifice. So, just that fundamental understanding of relationship of relational language uh these systems don't understand. So, can an AI care? I don't think so, but could an AI system be designed to support care, to support human relationships? Well, we had already have some great examples from today's conference uh of both in the context of democracy, the use of of AI as a tool to support uh participation uh and engagement and real understanding and legitimacy of bills that are being passed related to synthetic media. That's exciting. Uh we have the application of AI to support uh care and relationship in the healthcare context, in terms of what's happening related to to some of the patients and and getting data that their caregivers can can improve the care. That's exciting as well. And then, in terms of who gets to decide, I think it goes back to this fundamental question of how these systems are built and the power that's that's driving them. Do we have the right kind of cultural framework, uh ethical framework, and the right kind of policy framework to decentralize uh power and decentralize the way these markets are concentrated right now? Until we do that, until we fundamentally deal with the market concentration, the wealth concentration, the power concentration, we'll have challenges on a broader scale in terms of really implementing AI systems that support both those intimate, close relationships and then as the relationships expand into these larger uh contexts of solidarity and trust. Now, that being said, we do have an opportunity, even in the midst of the dominant systems, to to create an alternative ecosystem. To think about funders and investors and inventors and and researchers and policy uh uh experts and local activists and community uh groups. I, you know, seeing inspiring things at the local level where communities are taking control and building their own models, and that's exciting. So, even if we have a dominant system that's can continue to move forward in one direction, there might be a pathway, and I'm hopeful there is a pathway, for alternative systems. It's just about encouraging those and and supporting them and and finding the right kind of resources and uh connecting the dots between those that are doing incredible things in different communities around the world.

Not just a random thought, I mean a real idea, something you couldn't stop thinking about, a product you wished existed, a problem you knew how to solve, a brand name you already imagined in your head. And for a moment, it feels real. You can already picture the first customer, the first sale, maybe even quitting your job one day. But then reality kicks in. Everything here is designed to simplify tasks that normally feel complicated. I don't know manufacturing. I don't have money. What if it fails? What if I'm not ready yet?" So the idea stays in your notes app forever. title: Exercise Burnout & Anxiety: My Recovery Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What if your healthy exercise routine is secretly fueling burnout? Mine did, wrecking my nervous system, spiking anxiety, and turning sleep into a nightmare. I literally ran into my doom. A few tweaks to my routine, however, kept my cardio fitness soaring while calming my nervous system and restoring sleep. The changes I will share are backed by 40 years of scientific research proven to help runners and cyclists of all ages, and they're easy. Stick around, I'll reveal the symptoms I ignored and how I fixed them to reclaim my energy using the CAT, hockey stick, ego approach. Hello, all. I am Daniel, father of two, corporate and weekend warrior, and had a severe burnout last year. First, let's talk about the sneaky symptoms, all equally important, which indicated that I was on the verge of nervous system collapse, and I completely ignored because I thought I was invincible. Number one, changes in level of tiredness. Legs like lead, stiff even after rest. You start to also have post-run highs, crashing in the afternoons with headaches, or even directly after the run, not experiencing the euphoria you normally feel. This is hard to identify because you think, "This is just normal tiredness." Be alert of increases in duration and frequency. Any increase is a red flag. Number two, skyrocketing heart rate. My runs pushed me to max zones way too often. What was moderate became intense. Your body is basically screaming, "Slow down." Number three, sleep quality goes down. Exercise should help sleep, right? Nope, mine tanked. And this is essentially because too much exercise stimulates hormones to be elevated at the wrong times, leading to anxiety and body still on edge at night. For example, cortisol levels are elevated throughout the day and night. Number four, moody without workouts. Skip a run, felt off, guilty, irritable. Turns out it's hormone havoc from overdoing it, not just missing the endorphins.

title: I Spent 5 Days at Techstars Startup Week Abuja. Here's What Happened
transcription: My team won the pitch competition at Techstars Startup Week Abuja. 5 days, 1 idea, 1 MVP built from scratch. And this video is the full story. Every day, every lesson, every moment. Let's go! Techstars Startup Week is a 5-day entrepreneur-led event that brings founders, developers, investors, and creators together to learn, connect, and build their ideas. This year, it took place in Abuja, and I attended every day from start to finish, participating in sessions, workshops, panels, and networking events, while actively building with my team. Day 1 was all about ideas and community. Walking in, I immediately felt at home among like-minded innovators. We had meaningful conversations about the Nigerian startup ecosystem and the importance of building products that truly matter. By the end of the day, our group was formed, and we agreed on an idea that we would work on collectively. Day 2 was focused on knowledge. We attended sessions on AI ethics, cloud infrastructure with AWS, and a deep dive into MedGemma, Google's open-source AI model. We were also assigned a hands-on project to work on. Day 3 was all about execution. We remained fully focused on building our MVP. I completed the landing page for our product and worked closely with a senior engineer on my team to review it. That experience taught me a great deal. Day 4 was focused on depth. We explored startup leadership, financial discipline, and we had a panel with four senior tech experts who discussed AI, the Nigerian market, the japa syndrome, and the importance of giving back to community. Meanwhile, our MVP was nearly complete. Day 5 was pitch day. Before the pitch began, we had sessions on startup funding, storytelling, and robotics. After the sessions, the room went quiet, and it was time for each team to pitch their ideas. I didn't want to be the only one to describe what this week felt like. I wanted you to hear from someone who experienced it first-hand. So, at the end of the event, I interviewed Victoria to capture her perspective. Here is what she shared. Okay, I'm Victoria Ofuasia. I am a researcher, I'm a reinforcement learning researcher, also a backend developer, and I build communities.

title: FP3 Highlights | 2026 Australian Grand Prix
transcription: There was big drama for one of the pre-season favorites in FP3, Kimi Antonelli losing control of his Mercedes at Turn 2. The Italian, a passenger as his car thudded into the protective barriers, causing huge damage to the new W15. Oh, it's a big smash. It's a big smash. The barrier greets you so quickly there on the exit, and he doesn't have the perfect grip. It's not rubbered in, it's slippery off that Astro. And when you've got the power, the acceleration these cars have got, for some of their limitations, the the exit of the corners are quicker than they've ever handled, and that is why Antonelli then has just smashed his Mercedes into many, many pieces. And that could come back to bite him in a big way for the team that we think has a march on everyone. Antonelli is looking to become the first Italian to win a Grand Prix since Giancarlo Fisichella in 2006. And should he claim a victory this season, he'll enter the record books as the second-youngest driver to do so, behind only Max Verstappen. Fernando Alonso was one of the first to hit the track in FP3. The Spaniard missed the weekend's first session but was able to secure some mileage in FP2. The 44-year-old suffered a big front-right lockup as he pushed the car's limits early on, eventually ending the session in P18. Alonso's fellow countryman Carlos Sainz brought out an early yellow flag, his Williams grounding to a halt in the pit lane entry. He's lost power and then the car switched off. Now, there are a couple of ECU issues that arose yesterday, and I wonder if that's a similar thing there that Sainz has just had, or it's a Mercedes power unit issue. Yeah, copy, but everything is turned off still. Just sit tight unless someone come look at you on track. Yeah, it does look like a game over, but I'll let you know. So a game over would suggest it's a power unit. The red flag flew shortly after, allowing the marshals to retrieve his stricken Williams. And once the session was underway once more, teammate Alex Albon was forced to stop on track. The Thai driver performing a control-alt-delete before restarting moments later. Four teams look to be in the mix at the front. Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull, and McLaren all seem to have an edge over the rest.
